inspiration: A high-value defector is moved under a ceremonial escort that cannot be openly attacked; the snatch must happen inside the procession's own rules, taking the asset out before the ritual ends and the safe-conduct everyone is hiding behind evaporates.
skeleton: an extraction element must take a willing high-value asset out from inside a moving honor-procession whose ritual safe-conduct is the only thing keeping the asset alive and reachable, so any shot fired voids the very protection the snatch depends on and the window closes the instant the ceremony ends
title: OPERATION COLD COURTESY
situation: A scientist working for {TARGET_FACTION} on {WORLD} wants to defect, and {EMPLOYER} wants what is in that scientist's head before a rival gets it. Talking them over is done — the scientist has already agreed to come. The hard part is how the Clans are moving them. The scientist is being marched across {DISTRICT} in a caste-honor procession: a formal hand-over from the occupying garrison to the touman's refit command, on foot, at parade pace, down the old ceremonial avenue. The escort is one OmniMech honor-guard and a star of Elementals — five powered-armor infantry. A ritual rule protects the whole procession. While the ceremony is underway, no warrior in the escort may fire first, and no rival Clan may interfere. Breaking that rule brings a formal censure the warriors fear more than death. That rule is the only reason your team can get within a kilometer of the scientist. It is also the trap. The instant any weapon fires, the rule is void: the escort is freed, and every Elemental and the OmniMech turn on the one unarmed civilian in the middle of them. {NPC:intel-source} got the route and timing from a watch-caste contact. The march runs from the lower avenue gate to the refit command's door — about ninety minutes of slow walking through six blocks of old stone buildings, on a street 11 to 16 meters wide. The scientist walks in the center in a plain robe, with the data already memorized. The route is {INTEL_AGE_DAYS} days old, and if the garrison smells a threat it may shift one block to either side. The avenue is the problem. It runs dead straight, walled on both sides by solid building faces, watched from upper-floor windows the whole way. Exactly one side street lets a 'Mech reach the column, and exactly one covered exit lets you take the scientist out before the march ends. Recommended force: {FORCE_SIZE}, light and fast, no heavy machines. You are not here to fight a star of Elementals. You are here to pull one walking person out of the middle of them in the seconds before they may react, then vanish down the covered street — before the ritual that shielded you becomes a censure hunting whoever broke it.

objectives.primary: Get the scientist out of the center of the procession alive and unharmed. Then clear the avenue and reach the covered exit before the march ends at the refit command's door.
objectives.secondary: Take the scientist without firing a single shot inside the procession. A bloodless lift leaves {TARGET_FACTION} no way to prove a raid even happened — they must instead admit they lost a defector. That spares {EMPLOYER} the reprisal that breaking the ritual would bring.
objectives.bonus: Recover the scientist's sealed research case, carried in a cradle on the OmniMech honor-guard. It holds the physical proofs that turn memorized knowledge into hard evidence a buyer will pay full price for.

complications.name: The Safe-Conduct
complications.text: While the ritual is in force, no warrior in the escort may attack first. Your element can move in close under that same protection. But the instant any weapon fires, the rule flips: the escort is freed, and the Elementals and the OmniMech turn on the scientist and on you. The same rule that shields you becomes the trap. One shot decides which.
complications.mechanicalEffect: Until someone fires the first shot, the escort star and the OmniMech cannot start an attack, and your element may close to contact untouched. The first shot from anyone releases the full escort onto your element and the scientist. If your element grabs the scientist by hand without firing, this protection holds all the way to the exit.

complications.name: The Walled Avenue
complications.text: The avenue is a straight stone corridor. Solid building faces wall it on both sides, and windows overlook it the whole way. A 'Mech can enter the column from exactly one side street and carry the scientist out through exactly one covered exit. Everywhere else, the walls box in the escort and your element together, with no room to break away.
complications.mechanicalEffect: Your element can only leave the avenue at the marked side-street entry and the marked covered exit. If it fires and then fails to reach the exit hex with the scientist, it is trapped in the corridor against the freed escort, with infantry in the windows spotting its every move.

complications.name: The Route May Shift
complications.text: The garrison knows its own streets. If it spots a threat set up on the planned avenue, it moves the procession one block over, onto a parallel street you did not prepare. The route is days old, and these warriors are experienced. They will react to anything that looks staged.
complications.mechanicalEffect: On a die roll at step-off, the procession takes the parallel avenue one block over. An element set up on the planned route must then cross a block under observation to reach the column. It loses the early minutes of the ninety-minute window, and cannot make that time back.

complications.name: The Censure Hunts Both Ways
complications.text: If a shot is fired and the ritual breaks, the formal censure falls on whoever broke it — and {TARGET_FACTION} will tell the story so the blame lands on you. A bloodless lift forces the garrison to explain how it lost a scientist it was parading. A firefight lets them brand {EMPLOYER} as the side that violated the safe-conduct.
complications.mechanicalEffect: If the asset is taken without a shot fired, the enemy's response after a failure is softened: {TARGET_FACTION} cannot openly mobilize against {EMPLOYER} without admitting the defection happened. If a shot is fired, follow-on hostility against {EMPLOYER} in the area rises by one level regardless of the outcome.

decisionPoints.name: Taking the Asset
decisionPoints.context: You have one walking civilian, a star of Elementals around them, and a safe-conduct that lasts only until someone fires. You have three ways to take the scientist. Grab them by hand and trust the safe-conduct to hold to the exit. Drop a smoke screen and fight them out. Or split the formation with a feint and lift them through the gap. The cleaner the lift, the less of the freed escort you face — but each option risks that trade differently.

options.title: The Bloodless Hand
advantages: Move in under the safe-conduct, take the scientist by hand, and walk out before the escort may react. No shot fired, no censure, no proof a raid even happened
If no weapon fires, the safe-conduct holds all the way to the covered exit, leaving the escort stuck in a ritual it is forbidden to break
disadvantages: One nervous trigger pull — yours, theirs, or a spotter's — voids the safe-conduct and drops a star of Elementals on the scientist at arm's length
Your element must close to physical contact inside a hostile formation with no room for error, betting everything on perfect discipline while the enemy watches
options.consequence: If discipline holds, you take the scientist cleanly and {TARGET_FACTION} cannot prove anything happened. If even one shot fires, your element is in the worst spot possible: hand on the scientist, surrounded, safe-conduct gone.

costs.resource: the whole lift depends on zero shots fired inside the procession
costs.risk: Any weapon fired at contact range releases the escort star and the OmniMech onto your element, with the scientist in the middle

options.title: Cover and Fight Out
advantages: Drop smoke and put a 'Mech between the scientist and the escort, then fight them across to the exit on your timing, not the enemy's
You start the firefight on terms you choose, instead of waiting for a trigger pull you do not control
disadvantages: Firing first on purpose voids the safe-conduct. The full escort is freed, and {EMPLOYER} takes the censure for breaking the ritual
A running fight down a walled avenue against Elementals and an OmniMech is not a fight a light element can win
options.consequence: You get the scientist moving on your own schedule, but you spend the safe-conduct and all deniability to do it. The lift becomes a fighting retreat down a stone corridor with the whole escort freed to attack.

costs.resource: the safe-conduct, spent on purpose to control the timing
costs.risk: A fight in the walled avenue against a star of Elementals and an OmniMech, while protecting the scientist

options.title: Feint and Lift From the Gap
advantages: A staged disturbance a block ahead pulls the OmniMech and part of the escort away to check it, opening a gap to lift the scientist through
Splits the escort, so your element faces only part of it at the moment of the snatch, even if the safe-conduct breaks
disadvantages: The feint itself may read as the threat that triggers a route change, moving the whole procession off the planned avenue
The gap has to be timed to a slow walking pace. Sprung too early or too late, the scientist is still surrounded when your element commits
options.consequence: Timed right, you pull the scientist through a thinned escort and face only part of the star. Mistimed, the feint either shifts the route or springs while the formation is still closed — and your element commits into the full ring anyway.

costs.resource: a staged disturbance that may trigger the very route-shift it was meant to use
costs.risk: A mistimed feint leaves the scientist surrounded by a whole escort when your element commits

entries.event: The procession steps off at the lower avenue gate. The safe-conduct is now in force, and the ninety-minute walk to the refit command begins.
The formation reaches the middle blocks. It passes the one side street a 'Mech can enter and the one covered exit it can leave through.
If no lift has happened yet, the procession enters the final blocks, where the buildings crowd closest together and the scientist is hardest to reach.
The formation comes in sight of the refit command's door. The escort closes up tight and your escape routes narrow.
The scientist crosses the threshold and the hand-over is done. The ritual ends, the scientist is inside the refit command, and your chance to act is gone.

reactionTimeline.hardDeadline: Lift the scientist and clear the avenue before the procession reaches the refit command's door at T+90:00. Once the hand-over is done, the scientist is behind the touman's perimeter and the safe-conduct no longer applies. Arrive even a minute late and you find the door shut — and the escort no longer required to hold still.

opforSketch.composition: A Clan honor-escort, MECH_ONLY on the board: one OmniMech honor-guard (medium, 50-60 tons, Veteran) walking with the procession, supported by a star of Elementals (powered infantry, represented in the narrative — they fill out the formation and the threat but are not placed as playable units). Until the ritual breaks, none of them may attack first. Once it breaks, the OmniMech engages aggressively and the Elementals swarm the asset and the element. A garrison quick-reaction force — one light-to-medium star, Regular — waits off the avenue and moves in only after weapons fire is reported, then withdraws if reduced below roughly a third strength.
opforSketch.behavior: Ceremonial restraint until provoked, then sudden ferocity. The escort will not fire first and will hold formation under provocation, but it knows its own streets and will divert the route if it senses a staged threat. Once the safe-conduct is void, it converges on the asset above all else and will let the element flee if it recovers the asset.

forks.name: OPERATION QUIET LEDGER
forks.trigger: The asset and its research case are extracted, ideally without a shot fired inside the procession.
forks.consequence: {EMPLOYER} now has the defector and the physical proofs, and {TARGET_FACTION} cannot openly retaliate without admitting it lost an asset it was parading. The next operation uses the asset's intelligence for a precision strike against a refit site the asset identified, while the garrison is still pretending nothing happened.

forks.name: OPERATION BROKEN COURTESY
forks.trigger: The lift failed — shots were fired and the asset was killed, recaptured by the escort, or stranded while the element is pinned in the avenue.
forks.consequence: The ritual is void and the censure falls where {TARGET_FACTION} says it does: on {EMPLOYER}. The next operation is a hurried extraction of the surviving element off {WORLD}, ahead of a garrison now freed to hunt it and a rival faction that has been told {EMPLOYER} violated the safe-conduct.

storyElementSeed: A scout walks a light 'Mech at parade pace, one street over from the procession. Its steps match the slow drumbeat of boots on stone. Through a gap in the buildings, the pilot watches for one plain robe in the middle of the armored escort, counting down the blocks to the only doorway wide enough to vanish through.

is-davion.objectives.primary: Get the scientist out of the middle of that parade alive, then clear the avenue to the covered exit before the procession reaches the refit command. Do it without firing a shot if you can. The quiet way is the way everyone goes home.

is-steiner.objectives.primary: Pull the scientist out of the procession intact and reach the covered exit before the hand-over is done. A bloodless lift is worth paying for. It denies {TARGET_FACTION} any proof, and without proof they cannot turn a lost defector into a war.

PROCESSION_BLOCKS.unit: city blocks of the ceremonial avenue

inspiration: Raiders hit an enemy supply artery to strangle a forward garrison, but the same span that carries the supplies also carries the prize they were sent to seize intact — so cutting the line and capturing the cargo become the same overloaded problem on one piece of ground.
skeleton: an interdiction element must stop a recovered-tech resupply column on a single elevated transit span and capture its cargo intact, where dropping the span strands the garrison but destroys the very salvage the raid exists to take, so the crux is halting the column without wrecking the span or the prize it carries
title: OPERATION SEVERED ARTERY
situation: {TARGET_FACTION}'s forward garrison in the {DISTRICT} highlands of {WORLD} depends on one supply line, and {EMPLOYER} wants both the line cut and the cargo on it. The garrison sits at the head of a valley with no real road in. Everything it eats, and every ton of HarJel and ferro-fibrous armor it needs to keep its recovered-tech machines running, comes up one maglev viaduct. That viaduct is a single elevated span, eleven kilometers of piers and deck running along the valley wall. It is the only bulk route from the lowland depot to the highland railhead. Cut it, and the garrison runs out of supply in about two weeks. {NPC:intel-source} has obtained the manifest for the next supply run, and that manifest turns this into a raid, not just a demolition job. The same run carries a flatcar of recovered drive components. This is salvaged lostech the garrison is sending back to its refit command, and it can pay for a whole campaign if it comes off the bridge undamaged. The intelligence is {INTEL_AGE_DAYS} days old, and the schedule can slip a few hours either way. Here is the problem: you cannot both cut the line and take the cargo on the same run. Dropping a span strands the garrison, but it also drops the flatcar a hundred meters into the gorge, and salvage at the bottom of that fall is scrap. Stopping the train and lifting the flatcar off keeps the cargo whole, but then you have to fight for it on the deck. The deck is the hard part. It is one elevated roadway with sheer drops on both sides and no room to flank. A 'Mech can reach it only at the two end ramps and one maintenance gantry at mid-span. While you fight there, the garrison's reaction force comes down from the railhead and the depot's security comes up from the lowland end, and you are caught between them. Recommended force: {FORCE_SIZE}, with a recovery section and a vehicle element for speed on the ramps. Stop the train, get the drive components off before either reaction force reaches the span, and decide whether the supply line is worth more cut or the cargo is worth more carried. You can only have one.

objectives.primary: Halt the supply consignment on the viaduct, then do one of two things: capture the flatcar of recovered drive components intact, or destroy the span to cut off the garrison's supply. The operation cannot do both, so the commander must choose.
objectives.secondary: Destroy the consignment's HarJel and ferro-fibrous armor stores no matter what else happens. A garrison that loses its repair stocks loses readiness, even if its supply line is later restored.
objectives.bonus: Recover the consignment's forwarding manifest. This document maps {TARGET_FACTION}'s recovered-tech salvage flow across the whole highland front, naming what is being moved, where, and when.

complications.name: The Span or the Prize
complications.text: Dropping the viaduct strands the garrison, but it also sends the drive components into the gorge with the span. Stopping the column to lift the cargo instead leaves you fighting for a flatcar on an elevated deck with no room to maneuver and a reaction force closing from each end. Cutting the line destroys the salvage. Capturing the salvage forces the fight.
complications.mechanicalEffect: Severing the span and capturing the flatcar cannot both be done on the same run. Demolition charges set to drop a span cannot be moved to take the cargo once the column is on it, and an element that commits to the lift cannot also rig the span before the reaction forces arrive.

complications.name: The Narrow Deck
complications.text: The viaduct is a single elevated roadway with drops on both sides and no width to flank on. 'Mechs can reach the deck only at the two end ramps and the mid-span maintenance gantry. Once on it, there is nowhere to go but forward or back, and a wreck lying across the deck blocks everything behind it.
complications.mechanicalEffect: On the deck, units can only move forward or back along the span. There are no flanking hexes. A destroyed unit or a dropped load left across the deck becomes a hard obstacle. Following units must clear it or detour all the way around by an end ramp.

complications.name: Both Ends Answer
complications.text: The garrison's reaction force comes down from the highland railhead. The depot's security comes up from the lowland end. An element on the span is caught between these two forces with the gorge on either side. They do not arrive at the same time. One reaches the span before the other, and which end opens first changes the whole shape of the fight.
complications.mechanicalEffect: Two reaction forces enter from opposite end ramps on the reaction timeline, the highland force arriving first. An element still on the deck when the second arrives is engaged from both ends at once, with no flank to use and the gorge blocking any other exit.

complications.name: The Escort Knows
complications.text: The consignment escort is heavier than a routine supply run would normally get, because the escort knows what is on the flatcar. It will fight for the drive components longer than a normal supply detail would, and it will try to drive the consignment off the far end rather than let it be captured.
complications.mechanicalEffect: The escort fights past the break point its weight would suggest, and on its turn it will try to move the flatcar toward the nearest end ramp and off the span. An element that does not pin the flatcar early may find the cargo driven off the deck before it can be lifted.

decisionPoints.name: The Bridge Bargain
decisionPoints.context: The consignment is stopped on the deck, the cargo is on the flatcar, and two reaction forces are coming. You can drop the span and cut off the garrison, pin the column and lift the components off intact, or grab the stores and the manifest and leave the rest. Each choice trades the supply line against the salvage against how long you can hold the bridge.

options.title: Drop the Span
advantages: Sever the viaduct and the highland garrison runs out of supply in about two weeks, with no quick way to repair the span — a clean, certain strategic cut
Placing charges on a pier does not require winning the fight for the flatcar. You rig, detonate, and withdraw before either end's reaction force fully commits
disadvantages: The flatcar and its recovered drive components go into the gorge with the span — the prize is destroyed
Dropping the span is a loud, unmistakable act that brings the full weight of both reaction forces down on your withdrawal
options.consequence: You cut off the garrison but give up the salvage. {EMPLOYER} gets a supply cut it could also have gotten from an orbital strike. Meanwhile the drive components that would have paid for the campaign lie broken at the bottom of the gorge.

costs.resource: the recovered drive components, destroyed in the gorge along with the span
costs.risk: Dropping the span draws both reaction forces onto your withdrawal at full strength

options.title: Fix and Lift
advantages: Stop the column dead on the deck, take the drive components off the flatcar intact, and carry off the prize that can pay for the campaign
The viaduct stays standing and the manifest tells you when the next consignment runs — so the cut can be made another day, on your terms
disadvantages: Lifting a flatcar on a narrow elevated deck is slow, and the recovery section is exposed the whole time with no flank to cover it
The garrison's supply line survives this run, so the strategic cut {EMPLOYER} also wanted does not happen
options.consequence: You win the prize at the cost of the supply cut and a hard fight on the deck. The recovery section must hold the flatcar against the escort and beat the second reaction force to the ramp, or the lift fails with the element strung out on the span.

costs.resource: the strategic cut given up, the garrison's supply line left intact this run
costs.risk: A slow lift on a deck where you can only move forward or back, while caught between two converging reaction forces

options.title: Stores and Manifest, Then Out
advantages: Destroy the HarJel and ferro-fibrous stores, take the manifest, and withdraw fast without committing to the slow flatcar lift or the loud span demolition
Reduces the garrison's readiness and hands {EMPLOYER} the salvage-flow map while keeping the element light and quick on the ramps
disadvantages: You achieve neither the strategic cut nor the campaign-paying prize — a middle path that wins less of each
The garrison replaces the lost stores within weeks and the drive components reach the refit command untouched
options.consequence: You take the cheap, fast wins — repair stocks denied and the salvage map in hand — and leave both big prizes behind. The garrison is hurt but not cut off, and the lostech gets through.

costs.resource: both the span-cut and the drive components left untaken
costs.risk: A fast raid that wins the small objectives but gives up the war-level ones

entries.event: The consignment is halted on the viaduct deck. The escort engages, and the highland railhead reports the line under attack.
The garrison's reaction force leaves the highland railhead and starts down toward the upper end ramp.
The depot's security element starts moving up from the lowland end toward the lower ramp.
The highland reaction force reaches the upper ramp and moves onto the deck. An element on the span is now engaged from the railhead end.
The depot security reaches the lower ramp. Both reaction forces are now committed and the span is closed at both ends.

reactionTimeline.hardDeadline: The element must be off the viaduct — with the prize lifted, the span dropped, or the stores destroyed — before both reaction forces close the deck at T+28:00. After that, an element on the span is pinned between two converging forces on a roadway with no flank and a gorge on each side, and a recovery section caught mid-lift loses both the prize and the section.

opforSketch.composition: A combined-arms supply escort plus two converging reaction forces. The consignment escort is heavier than a routine run would get: two to three medium 'Mechs (45-65 tons, Regular to Veteran) plus tracked escort vehicles (the vehicle element of the combined-arms board), guarding the flatcar and fighting past a normal supply detail's break point. The highland reaction force is a light-to-medium 'Mech star (Regular) built for speed down from the railhead; the depot security is a mixed 'Mech-and-vehicle element (Regular) coming up from the lowland end. Each withdraws if reduced below roughly a third strength.
opforSketch.behavior: The escort focuses on protecting the flatcar and, if pressed, driving it off the span, fighting hard to keep the prize. The two reaction forces race for the end ramps to trap an element on the deck and engage it from both ends. They will not blindly charge a held ramp, but they will pressure relentlessly to block the withdrawal, and they are content to recover the salvage if the raiders are driven off.

forks.name: OPERATION DRY VALLEY
forks.trigger: The span was dropped or the prize was lifted, and the element withdrew with its objective achieved.
forks.consequence: Whichever {EMPLOYER} chose — a cut-off garrison or a campaign-paying haul of recovered drive components — the highland front shifts in its favor. The next operation presses the advantage against the now-weakened garrison while {TARGET_FACTION} scrambles to restore the supply line or replace the loss.

forks.name: OPERATION STRUNG OUT
forks.trigger: The element was caught on the deck between the two reaction forces, the lift failed or the charges did not detonate, and the raid is being cut apart on the span.
forks.consequence: The raid is pinned on the viaduct with the gorge on both sides and a force at each end. The next operation is a fighting withdrawal off the highland front — get the surviving element clear of the valley before {TARGET_FACTION} seals the lowland routes and turns a failed raid into a destroyed company.

storyElementSeed: A recovery crew works fast at a flatcar's tie-downs on an elevated deck barely wider than the load. The valley drops away into mist on both sides. On the ramp, a lance commander counts the seconds until the first reaction force comes around the railhead bend.

is-steiner.objectives.primary: Stop the consignment on the viaduct and make the call: drop the span and cut off the garrison's supply, or take the recovered drive components off the flatcar intact. You cannot do both — a cut supply line costs them a front, a captured cargo pays for ours.

merc.objectives.primary: Halt the column on the deck and decide what the contract is really buying — cutting the supply line or taking the salvage. Drop the span and the garrison runs dry, but the prize goes into the gorge. Lift the flatcar and we get paid, but the supply line survives. Pick one. The bridge will not give us both.

GORGE_DROP_M.unit: meters of drop on each side

inspiration: A single dominating enemy asset, too valuable to simply blow up, must be put out of action by a precise strike at its one delicate working part — disabled long enough to matter but left whole enough to be reclaimed, so the raid is a surgical denial rather than a demolition.
skeleton: a strike element must reversibly disable a fixed recovered-tech super-asset by ruining its one irreplaceable working component rather than cratering it, where total destruction is forbidden because a friendly party means to reclaim the asset later, so the crux is the surgical denial under guard rather than the easy demolition
title: OPERATION GLASS THROAT
situation: {TARGET_FACTION} has restored a piece of lostech that changes the strategic picture, and {EMPLOYER} needs it silenced but not destroyed. On the high plateau above {DISTRICT} on {WORLD} stands a recovered Star League hyperpulse booster array. It is an interstellar relay the occupiers brought back to life, and it lets the touman talk across the front faster and more securely than any force it faces. {EMPLOYER} wants it off the air, but wants it left whole. The array is irreplaceable lostech, and a friendly remnant means to retake this plateau within the year and inherit it working. So the order is exact and hard: kill what the array does, without wrecking the array. The array's greatest strength is also its one weak point. {NPC:intel-source}, a defected technician who helped restore it, reports that the whole relay hangs on a single part. It is a recovered phase-conjugation core, about the size of a coffin, mounted in the array's signal vault. The Star League hand-built it, and no one can build another today. Destroy that core and the array goes dark for years, but the structure survives for the remnant to repair. Blow up the whole array and you destroy the core with it, leaving the remnant only rubble. The route is {INTEL_AGE_DAYS} days old, and the technician's map of the vault may be out of date. The approach is the problem. The array sits on a bare, wind-scoured shelf. One switchback service track climbs to it, and open rock runs a kilometer on every other side. A guard post on the rim watches it, and a fixed defensive emplacement covers it — built to stop exactly this kind of raid. You cannot cross that bare shelf unseen. The track is the fast way in, and the careful work is in the vault, and you do not have time to do both slowly. Recommended force: {FORCE_SIZE}, with a demolition specialist who can wreck a machine without leveling the building around it, plus a vehicle element to cross the open shelf at speed. Reach the signal vault, destroy the core with precise charges that leave the structure standing, and get off the plateau before the guard reaction and the fixed defense pin you on bare rock. The easy answer is a satchel charge against the wall. That is the one answer the contract forbids.

objectives.primary: Reach the array's signal vault and disable the relay by destroying the recovered phase-conjugation core. Destroy the core itself while leaving the array structure and its other recovered components intact, so the asset can be reclaimed later.
objectives.secondary: Recover or copy the array's restoration logs from the vault. These documents tell {EMPLOYER}'s friendly remnant how the Star League core was brought back online, so they can repeat the work when they inherit the asset.
objectives.bonus: Plant a hidden intercept tap on the array's feed before disabling it. While the relay is still running, the tap gives {EMPLOYER} a window into {TARGET_FACTION}'s communications traffic in the time before the relay is shut down.

complications.name: Ruin It, Do Not Crater It
complications.text: The simplest way to silence the array is a demolition charge against the vault wall. The contract forbids it: blowing up the array destroys the irreplaceable core along with it and leaves the remnant rubble instead of a working relay. The job is precise — destroy the one component, spare the building around it — and that takes longer than a satchel charge and a fuse.
complications.mechanicalEffect: Generic demolition that would destroy the vault fails the primary objective, because the asset must survive for reclamation. Disabling the core instead requires the demolition specialist to work in the vault for a set period with precision charges. That time in the vault is exposure the easy method would not cost.

complications.name: The Bare Shelf
complications.text: The array sits on a wind-scoured plateau with one switchback service track up to it and open rock for a kilometer on every other side. There is no concealed approach. The element either crosses the shelf in the open, in full view of the guard post and within range of the fixed defense, or it does not cross at all.
complications.mechanicalEffect: All approach hexes outside the service track are open rock with no concealment. Units crossing them take fixed-defense fire and are freely spotted from the guard post. The track is faster, but it funnels the approach into one predictable lane the defense is already laid against.

complications.name: The Fixed Defense
complications.text: The occupiers built a fixed defense to keep raids off the plateau: emplaced weapons positioned to cover the open shelf and the track, crewed and active. It cannot pursue, but it does not need to — it covers the ground the element must cross to reach the vault and cross again to leave.
complications.mechanicalEffect: Emplaced defensive positions cover both the approach and the withdrawal with ranged fire. They are immobile and can be suppressed or destroyed, but doing so costs time and alerts the enemy to the raid. Bypassing them means crossing their fields of fire both going in and coming out.

complications.name: The Access Map May Lie
complications.text: The defected technician's map of the signal vault is days old, and a working relay is a maintained machine that changes. A panel that was open may now be sealed. A route into the vault may have been re-keyed since the technician left. The specialist may reach the core only to find the last few meters harder than expected.
complications.mechanicalEffect: On a die roll at the vault, the technician's access route is partly out of date: the specialist needs extra time to reach the core through a re-secured panel. This lengthens the exposed work time inside the vault while the guard reaction builds up outside.

decisionPoints.name: The Surgeon's Choice
decisionPoints.context: The core is in the vault, the shelf is bare, and the guard is starting to react. You have three ways to do this. Run the track fast and rely on speed. Suppress the fixed defense first, then work in the quiet that buys you. Or split the job, disabling the core while a fire element holds the shelf. The less exposed your specialist is, the louder and slower the raid tends to get.

options.title: Up the Track Fast
advantages: Run the service track at speed with the vehicle element leading, reach the vault before the guard can fully crew the fixed defense, and bet the whole raid on speed
Spends the least time on the open shelf — by never slowing, you minimize how long you are under the emplaced weapons
disadvantages: The track is the one lane the fixed defense is laid against, so a fast run up it is a fast run into pre-aimed fire
Arriving in a hurry leaves the specialist working the vault while the guard reacts and the defense behind you is still active
options.consequence: If your speed beats the guard, you are in the vault before the defense is fully crewed. If it does not, the element is on the pre-aimed track taking emplaced fire with the precise vault work still ahead of it.

costs.resource: the approach committed to the one lane the defense expects
costs.risk: A fast run up the track into pre-aimed emplaced fire, with the vault job not yet started

options.title: Suppress, Then Work
advantages: Destroy the fixed defense and the guard post first, then cross the shelf and work the vault in the quiet the suppression buys you
The specialist gets the time the precise work needs, without emplaced fire raking the vault approach
disadvantages: Suppressing the defense is loud and slow. It announces the raid and starts the wider reaction clock early
Time spent destroying emplacements is time the garrison's off-plateau reaction force uses to start its climb
options.consequence: You buy the specialist his quiet at the price of raising the alarm. The vault job goes cleanly, but the broader reaction is already moving by the time the core is reached, leaving you a tighter withdrawal.

costs.resource: the time and noise of destroying the fixed defense before the real job
costs.risk: An early, loud alarm puts the off-plateau reaction force on the climb before the core is even reached

options.title: Split the Job
advantages: A fire element holds the shelf and ties up the guard while the specialist and a small escort slip into the vault to disable the core — working two problems at once
The core can be destroyed while the defense is occupied, saving time on the precise-work phase
disadvantages: A divided element is weaker everywhere. The fire element may not hold the shelf, and the vault party has little to fall back on if discovered
Coordinating across the open shelf under fire is fragile — if the fire element breaks, the specialist is cut off at the core
options.consequence: Done well, the core is destroyed while the guard is occupied and the element reunites for the withdrawal. Done poorly, the fire element is overrun and the specialist is stranded in the vault with the shelf no longer held.

costs.resource: the element split between holding the shelf and working the vault
costs.risk: A broken fire element strands the specialist at the core with the shelf lost behind them

entries.event: The element commits to the plateau. The guard post on the rim raises the alarm and the fixed defense begins ranging the shelf.
The guard fully crews the fixed defense, and the off-plateau garrison is alerted that the array is under attack.
The garrison's reaction force begins its climb toward the plateau by the only vehicle route up.
The reaction force is partway up the climb. An element still working the vault is racing it to get a clean withdrawal.
The reaction force reaches the top of the plateau approach. An element not off the shelf by now must fight for the track against fresh 'Mechs.

reactionTimeline.hardDeadline: The core must be disabled and the element off the plateau before the garrison's reaction force reaches the top of the approach at T+50:00. After that, the only way down is blocked by 'Mechs holding the track, with the fixed defense still ranging the shelf behind you. An element caught on the bare rock with the reaction force above it has nowhere to go.

opforSketch.composition: A plateau garrison detachment, combined arms. The fixed defense is emplaced weapons (represented in the narrative and by vehicles: turreted positions and a dug-in support vehicle or two, the vehicle element of the board) positioned to cover the open shelf and the track, crewed at Regular quality. A guard star of light-to-medium 'Mechs (Regular) holds the array and crews the defense. The off-plateau reaction force is a medium 'Mech star (Regular to Veteran) that climbs the vehicle route to relieve the plateau. The array and its core are inert objectives, not combatants.
opforSketch.behavior: The fixed defense covers the approach and does not pursue. The guard star defends the array and the vault entrance, falling back into the structure rather than giving it up. The reaction force climbs hard to trap the raiders on the plateau and will press the track aggressively. The garrison fights to keep the array intact — it does not want it destroyed any more than {EMPLOYER} does — and withdraws if reduced below roughly a third strength.

forks.name: OPERATION LONG SILENCE
forks.trigger: The phase-conjugation core was destroyed, the array was left structurally intact, and the element withdrew.
forks.consequence: The relay goes dark for years and {TARGET_FACTION} loses its fast, secure communications across the front, while the array stands waiting for the remnant to reclaim it. The next operation exploits the garrison's slowed coordination with a strike timed to the communications gap the raid just opened.

forks.name: OPERATION SCORCHED RELAY
forks.trigger: The raid was pinned on the plateau — the core was not reached, the array had to be blown up to silence it at all, or the element was trapped on the shelf.
forks.consequence: Either the array still works or it lies in rubble the remnant cannot inherit, and the element is pinned on bare rock. The next operation is a fighting extraction off the plateau front, getting the survivors clear before the reaction force and the fixed defense finish what the raid started.

storyElementSeed: A demolition specialist kneels in a signal vault with a coffin-sized recovered core open in front of them, laying small charges by hand against the one part that matters, while overhead the array hums with traffic it does not yet know it is about to lose.

merc.objectives.primary: Get into the vault and shut down the relay by destroying the one recovered core that runs it. Leave the rest standing. The contract pays for a silence the client's friends can reverse later, not a hole in the ground. Destroy the component, not the building.

comstar.objectives.primary: Reach the signal vault and silence the array by destroying its phase-conjugation core, while sparing the structure and its other recovered parts. The asset itself is sacred. Only the use the enemy makes of it is the target. Silence it, but leave it whole for the rightful inheritors.

SHELF_OPEN_KM.unit: km of open rock around the array

VAULT_WORK_MIN.unit: minutes of surgical work on the core

inspiration: A force feigns weakness — a wounded, retreating quarry — to draw a confident enemy past the point of caution into ground already prepared for his destruction, where the whole art is making the bait convincing without letting the trap spring an hour too soon.
skeleton: a star must sell a staged crippled-machine retreat convincingly enough to lure a confident enemy recon force over a ridge into a prepared reverse-slope kill sack, where overselling the bait springs the trap early and underselling it lets the quarry break off, so the crux is the disciplined feigned weakness on a tightening leash
title: OPERATION LAME WOLF
situation: The Inner Sphere remnant probing {DISTRICT} on {WORLD} is growing bolder, and {EMPLOYER} means to teach its scouts a lesson. The remnant's recon company has pushed deeper each day, trading caution for ground. {NPC:intel-source}, a Watch observer shadowing the advance, reports it now moves like a force that thinks it has the measure of this front. That overconfidence is the weapon. A confident scout will chase a wounded enemy, and a convincing wounded enemy can lead that scout onto ground the hunter chose. The plan is old and exact. A single OmniMech, dressed up to look badly hurt with a dragging leg and scorched armor, plays a straggler cut off from its star. It withdraws across the open saddle the enemy recon will reach by midday, then lets itself be seen limping over the ridge beyond. Past that ridge, the ground drops into a bowl the enemy cannot see until he crests the rim. In that bowl waits the rest of your star, hull-down, powered down cold, weapons aimed at the reverse slope. If the remnant takes the bait, it pours over the ridge chasing a cripple and runs into a full Clan star firing point-blank from prepared positions, with the saddle sealed behind it. If it does not, the trap is wasted and your star has shown itself for nothing. The intel on the enemy's pace is {INTEL_AGE_DAYS} hours old, and a recon company can change its mind within an hour. The ground sets the problem. The saddle is open and watched. The ridge crest is the one line the enemy must cross to take the bait. The bowl is a kill zone only while the enemy does not know it is there. Timing is everything, and there are three ways to get it wrong. Spring the trap before the enemy has come over the crest, and he simply backs off the open saddle and escapes. Let the bait fight back too hard, and it gets killed and the lure dies with it. Let the bait run too easily and look too healthy, and the scout smells the trap and breaks off. Recommended force: {FORCE_SIZE}, MECH_ONLY. You need one warrior with the nerve to be the lame wolf, and a star with the discipline to hold fire until the enemy is past the point of escape. Sell the wound, draw the bold scout over the ridge, and seal the saddle behind him — or waste your position and your surprise on a quarry too careful to bite.

objectives.primary: Lure the remnant recon company over the ridge crest into the reverse-slope kill zone and destroy or break it there. Spring the ambush only once the enemy is committed past the point where he could withdraw cleanly.
objectives.secondary: Keep the bait OmniMech alive through the lure. A cripple that survives to be repaired keeps both a warrior and a machine. A bait sacrificed to make the trap work is a loss the codex will record.
objectives.bonus: Take a functional enemy 'Mech as isorla from the kill zone rather than destroying all of them. A captured machine from a broken recon company is both honor and materiel.

complications.name: The Disciplined Leash
complications.text: The bait must look wounded enough to be worth chasing but move freely enough to run, and the star must stay cold until the enemy is past the crest. Spring early and the quarry escapes off the open saddle. Spring late and the cripple is dead before the trap closes. The whole engagement comes down to one right moment to open fire.
complications.mechanicalEffect: The ambush star may not fire until the enemy commits over the ridge crest into the bowl. Firing before that commitment threshold lets the remnant reverse off the saddle (the mission then succeeds only at its lower diversion value). Firing after the threshold catches the enemy in the kill zone, with the saddle able to be sealed behind him.

complications.name: The Bait Can Die
complications.text: The lame wolf is a real warrior in a genuinely damaged machine, drawing fire to sell the wound. The remnant will shoot at a straggler it thinks it can finish, and a cripple that fights back too effectively stops looking like a cripple. The bait must stay convincing without getting itself killed.
complications.mechanicalEffect: The bait OmniMech takes incoming fire while selling the lure and cannot return fire effectively without breaking the illusion. If the bait is destroyed before the enemy crests the ridge, the lure collapses, and the remnant — having already killed its quarry — may withdraw rather than push into the bowl.

complications.name: The Scout May Smell It
complications.text: A recon company is trained to be suspicious. If the bait runs too cleanly, the saddle looks too obviously open, or the ridge seems too perfectly inviting, the enemy commander hesitates at the crest and probes instead of charging. A trap that looks too convenient gets refused.
complications.mechanicalEffect: On a die roll at the crest, the remnant sends a small probe element over the ridge instead of committing the whole company. The probe may discover the hull-down star and report it, forcing the ambush to spring against only a fraction of the enemy while the main body is still on the safe side of the saddle.

complications.name: The Enemy's Pace Is Its Own
complications.text: The lure is timed to the remnant's advance, but the enemy controls the pace of that advance. A recon company that halts to consolidate, swings wide, or pushes faster than expected reaches the saddle off the bait's schedule — and a bait limping across an empty saddle convinces no one.
complications.mechanicalEffect: On a die roll at mission start, the remnant arrives at the saddle earlier or later than the staged retreat planned for. The bait must then adjust its withdrawal on the move to meet the enemy at the crest, risking either a too-hasty run that looks staged or a delay that lets the enemy settle and grow cautious.

decisionPoints.name: The Lame Wolf's Run
decisionPoints.context: The enemy is coming, and the bait must decide how to play the wound. The lame wolf has three ways to run. A hard, hurt sprint that looks like an easy kill. A slow staggering crawl that begs to be chased. Or a fighting limp that trades a little return fire for believability. The more convincing the wound looks, the less likely the bait is to survive selling it.

options.title: The Hard Sprint
advantages: A wounded machine running flat-out for the ridge looks like a straggler desperate to rejoin its star — the most tempting possible quarry
Speed gets the bait over the crest quickly, closing the window in which the enemy might pause to think
disadvantages: A sprint may outrun the remnant's commitment, cresting the ridge before the company has chased far enough to be trapped
Running hard reveals the staged limp if the machine moves better than its supposed wound should allow
options.consequence: If the enemy takes the bait and chases at speed, he pours over the crest fast and fully committed. If the bait outpaces the pursuit, the company is still short of the saddle when the bait is already gone, and the trap has nothing to close on.

costs.resource: the illusion of the wound, risked by moving faster than a cripple should
costs.risk: The bait outruns the enemy's commitment and crests the ridge before the company is trapped

options.title: The Staggering Crawl
advantages: A barely-moving cripple is almost irresistible to a confident scout — the surest lure to draw the whole company over the ridge
A slow bait keeps the enemy closing steadily, giving the ambush star time to confirm the commitment and the saddle time to be sealed
disadvantages: A crawling machine is an easy target. The bait takes sustained fire and may be destroyed before the trap can spring
If the enemy is cautious, a too-slow cripple invites him to shoot from a distance rather than charge
options.consequence: The crawl draws the boldest pursuit but gives the bait the worst odds. The enemy commits deep, but the lame wolf may not live to see the trap close behind him.

costs.resource: the bait's survival, staked on a slow crawl under sustained fire
costs.risk: The cripple is killed before the enemy crests the ridge, collapsing the lure

options.title: The Fighting Limp
advantages: A cripple that fires the occasional shot as it withdraws looks like a wounded warrior still dangerous — believable, and harder to dismiss as a trap
Returning measured fire lets the bait shape the enemy's approach, drawing him onto the line the ambush wants
disadvantages: Every shot the bait fires risks revealing that the machine is less hurt than it looks, spoiling the lure
A fighting withdrawal is slower to manage and may let a cautious enemy settle into a deliberate advance instead of a chase
options.consequence: The middle path buys believability at the risk of overdoing it. A disciplined limp draws a deliberate, committed pursuit, but one shot too confident and the scout reads the wound as fake and breaks off.

costs.resource: believability traded against the risk of revealing the wound is staged
costs.risk: An overconfident shot from the bait tips the scout off to the trap and he breaks off

entries.event: The remnant recon company enters the open saddle. The bait OmniMech begins its staged withdrawal toward the ridge.
The enemy commits to pursuing the cripple, advancing across the saddle toward the ridge crest.
The bait crests the ridge. The enemy reaches the base of the crest, and the moment of commitment is close.
If the enemy comes over the crest into the bowl, the ambush springs. If he hesitates instead, the window to close the saddle starts to run out.
Either the kill zone is sprung and the saddle sealed, or the remnant has recognized the trap and is withdrawing off the saddle out of reach.

reactionTimeline.hardDeadline: The ambush must be sprung with the enemy committed in the bowl before the commitment window closes at T+55:00. After that, the remnant has either been destroyed in the kill zone or recognized the lure and pulled back across the saddle. A star that has revealed itself to a quarry now withdrawing has spent its position and its surprise for nothing, and will face a forewarned enemy at its next meeting.

opforSketch.composition: An Inner Sphere remnant recon company, MECH_ONLY: light and medium 'Mechs (20-55 tons) at Regular to Veteran quality, mobile and aggressive, built for scouting rather than a stand-up fight but dangerous in numbers if it catches the ambush half-formed. It fields no vehicles in this action — a pure 'Mech recon push. The bait it chases is one of {EMPLOYER}'s own; the kill zone is manned by the rest of the star.
opforSketch.behavior: Confident and advancing, inclined to chase a wounded straggler — but professional enough to probe an opening that looks too good. The company commits hard when it believes it has an easy kill and reverses fast off open ground when it senses a trap. Once caught in the bowl at close range by prepared fire, it fights to break out toward the saddle rather than trade blows, and a company that loses cohesion in the kill zone scatters back the way it came.

forks.name: OPERATION CLOSED SADDLE
forks.trigger: The remnant committed over the ridge and was destroyed or broken in the reverse-slope kill zone.
forks.consequence: The bold recon company is gone, and the remnant's whole advance on the front loses its eyes. {EMPLOYER} pushes into the now-blind sector, exploiting the gap the ambush tore in the enemy's reconnaissance before a replacement screen can be moved up.

forks.name: OPERATION SHOWN HAND
forks.trigger: The trap sprang early, or the scout recognized the lure and withdrew, and the star's position and intent are now known to a forewarned enemy.
forks.consequence: The ambush is wasted and the remnant knows both the ground and the trick. The next engagement is a stand-up fight on a front where the enemy now advances cautiously and the star has lost the advantage of surprise — a harder battle the failed lure made necessary.

storyElementSeed: A warrior holds a hull-down machine dead cold on a reverse slope, sensors dark. They watch the ridgeline above for the first enemy shape to break it. One hand rests off the trigger by an act of will. Over the crest, a wounded packmate's dragging stride comes closer.

clan-wolf.objectives.primary: Draw the bold scout over the ridge with the lame wolf and break him in the bowl beyond. Spring the trap only once he is past the point of escape. A Wolf does not waste the kill by closing the jaws on empty air.

SADDLE_WIDTH_M.unit: meters of open saddle to cross

BOWL_DEPTH_M.unit: meters from crest to the kill sack floor

inspiration: Before a main body commits, a reconnaissance-in-force probes a prepared defensive belt to find the one weak seam — but the belt only reveals itself by firing, so every meter of intelligence is bought by drawing the very fire that finds the gap.
skeleton: a recon-in-force element must map a prepared defensive belt of hidden mines and emplaced fire to locate the one usable seam before the main body commits, where the belt is invisible until it shoots and every probe that finds a position pays for the knowledge in the fire it draws, so the crux is reading the gap from the pattern of what kills you
title: OPERATION READING THE WALL
situation: The Republic remnant holding {DISTRICT} on {WORLD} has built a defensive belt, and {EMPLOYER} must learn where it is weak before sending in the main body. The remnant cannot match the touman in the open, so it did what a weaker but smarter enemy does. It dug a prepared belt across the only practical approach to the district seat. The belt is a band of buried mines, emplaced weapons, and pre-ranged kill zones, laid across kilometers of hardpan and dune to break an assault before it can close. The main body is coming. But a Galaxy commander who charges a prepared belt blind pays for the ground in casualties the bidding never planned for. So your element goes in first. Not to break the belt, but to map it. Somewhere in it is a seam. Every prepared line has one: a stretch the defenders could not mine, could not cover, or could not man. Find the seam and the assault walks through. Miss it and the assault is cut to pieces. {NPC:intel-source}, a Watch element that has watched the remnant dig for weeks, has a partial picture: emplacements suspected along the high dune line, mines thickest where the hardpan funnels movement. But the belt is invisible until it fires, and that picture is {INTEL_AGE_DAYS} days old. Here is the hard part. The belt only shows itself by shooting. You find each position by drawing its fire, and you map each mined stretch by the vehicle that hits the first charge. Every piece of the map costs you the unit that exposed itself to find it. The terrain is part of the trap. The hardpan corridors that let a force move fast are exactly where the mines are thickest. The dune lines that give cover are exactly where the guns are aimed. Fast ground is mined, and cover hides the guns. Recommended force: {FORCE_SIZE} combined arms, with expendable vehicle scouts to set off the mines and 'Mechs to survive the fire that follows. Push into the belt far enough to find the seam, read the gap from the pattern of what shoots at you, and pull back with a map the main body can assault through — without spending so much of the element that nothing is left to carry it home.

objectives.primary: Locate the usable seam in the prepared defensive belt — the stretch the main body can assault through — and withdraw with the belt's layout mapped before the element is used up finding it.
objectives.secondary: Pin down the locations and types of the heaviest emplacements along the dune line, so the main body's assault can suppress them one after another instead of meeting them blind.
objectives.bonus: Provoke the belt into revealing the mobile reserve behind it. If the probe draws out the remnant's counter-move, the main body learns not just where the wall is thin but what waits behind the gap.

complications.name: The Wall Shows Itself by Firing
complications.text: The belt is invisible until it shoots. An emplacement looks like an ordinary patch of dune until it opens fire on you. A mined corridor looks like clear ground until a vehicle hits the first charge. You map each position only by drawing its fire, and each piece of the map costs you the unit that drew it.
complications.mechanicalEffect: Hidden emplacements and minefields are revealed only when they fire or are triggered. Each piece of the belt you add to the map costs the element exposure — drawn fire, a tripped mine, or a committed scout. There is no way to read the belt without provoking it.

complications.name: Good Going Is the Trap
complications.text: The hardpan corridors that let a force move fast are exactly where the mining is densest. The dune lines that offer cover are exactly where the emplacements are aimed. The belt is built so the natural moves — speed across the open, cover behind the dunes — both lead onto prepared killing ground.
complications.mechanicalEffect: Fast open-corridor hexes carry the highest mine density. Covered dune-line hexes fall under the heaviest emplaced fire. An element that moves by instinct, fast through the open and cautious into cover, walks into the densest parts of the belt. Finding the seam means moving against what the terrain seems to invite.

complications.name: The Picture Is Partial and Stale
complications.text: The Watch has observed for weeks, but the belt is an actively worked line and the picture is days old. Emplacements may have shifted, fresh mines may have been laid, and a seam that was open when the report was written may have been closed since. The element cannot fully trust a map this far past its date.
complications.mechanicalEffect: On a die roll at contact, part of the intel picture is out of date: a suspected emplacement is gone or has moved, or a stretch reported clear is freshly mined. The element must verify the seam by probing rather than trusting the briefed gap, spending additional exposure to confirm the way through.

complications.name: The Spending Trap
complications.text: The whole value of the operation is the map delivered, not the belt defeated. An element that pushes too hard, drawn deeper by each new position it finds, can use itself up gathering a picture it then has nothing left to carry home. The probe must know when it has enough.
complications.mechanicalEffect: If the element is reduced below a set threshold while still mapping, the intelligence gathered cannot be reliably extracted (the primary objective slides toward FAILURE even if the seam was found). Breaking off with a usable-but-incomplete map beats pushing for a perfect one and losing it.

decisionPoints.name: How to Read the Wall
decisionPoints.context: The belt is out there, and the only way to see it is to make it shoot. You have three ways to read it. Drive the corridors with expendable scouts to set off the mines. Press the dune lines to draw the emplacements. Or commit the whole element to a broad probe that reads the belt fast but takes losses doing it. The more of the belt you map, the more of the element you spend mapping it.

options.title: Trip the Corridors
advantages: Push expendable vehicle scouts down the hardpan corridors to find the mines cheaply, using machines that are meant to be expended
Maps the densest mined stretches — the parts of the belt most likely to wreck the main body's assault — without risking the 'Mechs
disadvantages: Reveals the mines but leaves the dune-line emplacements unmapped, so the main body learns the ground but not the guns
Uses up the scout vehicles quickly, and a probe with no scouts left cannot read the rest of the belt
options.consequence: You map the mines at the cost of the scouts but learn little about the emplacements. The main body knows where the ground will kill it but not where the fire will — a half-map that opens only half the wall.

costs.resource: the expendable scout vehicles, spent setting off the mined corridors
costs.risk: The emplacements stay unmapped, so the main body assaults knowing the mines but not the guns

options.title: Draw the Emplacements
advantages: Press the dune lines with 'Mechs that can survive the first volleys, mapping the emplaced fire that does the real killing
Locates and identifies the heaviest guns so the main body can suppress them one after another — the highest-value part of the picture
disadvantages: Deliberately drawing emplaced fire exposes the 'Mechs to the belt's hardest-hitting positions, costing armor and risk
Maps the guns but not the mines, so the assault may suppress the emplacements and still bog down in an unmapped minefield
options.consequence: You read the guns at the cost of armor but learn little about the mines. The main body can suppress the fire but may still drive into charges — a half-map that silences the wall but not the ground.

costs.resource: the 'Mechs' armor, spent drawing the heaviest emplaced fire
costs.risk: The mines stay unmapped, so the assault suppresses the guns and then bogs down on the charges

options.title: Broad Probe, Fast Read
advantages: Commit the whole element across a wide front to make the belt fire everywhere at once, and read the seam from the overall pattern quickly
The most complete picture in the least time — mines, guns, and the gap between them all mapped together
disadvantages: A broad probe is exposed everywhere and takes losses across the whole front, risking the over-spending that loses the map
Provoking the entire belt at once may draw out the mobile reserve before the element is ready to break contact
options.consequence: You get the fullest, fastest map at the highest cost. If the element breaks off in time, it delivers the whole wall. If it does not, it uses itself up gathering a complete picture it cannot carry home.

costs.resource: the whole element, exposed across the front to read the belt at speed
costs.risk: A broad probe takes losses past the point it can extract the map, losing the picture it paid for

entries.event: The element enters the belt's outer edge. The first emplacement opens fire or the first mine is tripped, and the wall begins to reveal itself.
The remnant realizes this is a reconnaissance-in-force, not the main assault, and begins firing its belt carefully to deny the map.
The mobile reserve behind the belt is alerted and moves toward the probed sector to seal any gap the element finds.
The reserve reaches the rear of the belt. An element still inside the wall now risks being trapped between the belt and the counter-move.
The remnant commits to driving the probe out. An element that has not broken contact is now fighting its way back through the belt it came to read.

reactionTimeline.hardDeadline: The element must break contact and withdraw with its map before the mobile reserve and the belt close on the probed sector at T+55:00. After that, the element is caught inside the prepared belt with a counter-move behind it. A probe destroyed in the wall delivers nothing. The main body then assaults blind, and the whole point of the operation is lost with the element that was gathering the map.

opforSketch.composition: A Republic remnant prepared defense, combined arms. The belt itself is emplaced weapons and minefields (represented in the narrative and by vehicles: dug-in support vehicles, turreted positions, and buried charges — the vehicle element of the board sits in the emplacements), laid across the approach at Regular quality. Behind it waits a mobile reserve — a medium 'Mech company (Regular to Veteran) with a few combat vehicles — held back to counter any breach. The belt does not maneuver; the reserve does.
opforSketch.behavior: Once it realizes this is a probe rather than an assault, the belt fires carefully to deny the map, revealing as little as it can while still stopping the element. The mobile reserve moves to seal any seam the probe finds and to trap the element inside the wall. The defense fights to protect the secret of where the belt is weak — it would rather drive off the probe with the seam unmapped than win a costly fight that gives away the gap — and the reserve withdraws if reduced below roughly a third strength.

forks.name: OPERATION OPEN SEAM
forks.trigger: The element located the usable seam and withdrew with a map the main body can assault through.
forks.consequence: The wall now has a known weak point, and the main body knows where to concentrate its weight. The next operation is the assault itself, driving the touman through the mapped seam before the remnant can close it — exploiting the breach the probe paid for.

forks.name: OPERATION SPENT PROBE
forks.trigger: The element was driven out or destroyed inside the belt without delivering a usable map.
forks.consequence: The wall keeps its secret, and the element is broken or has fled with nothing to show. The next operation is a costly deliberate assault on the unmapped belt, or a withdrawal of the survivors under pursuit — the main body now faces the prepared line blind, paying the price the failed probe could not.

storyElementSeed: A scout vehicle creeps a hardpan corridor at a crawl while a 'Mech commander watches from a dune shoulder, reading the belt by the bloom of each emplacement that opens up, marking guns on a map paid for one drawn volley at a time.

merc.objectives.primary: Find the weak spot in that wall — the stretch the main push can go through — and get back out with the map before the probe is all used up finding it. We are paid to read the belt, not to break it. Spend just enough of the element to see the seam, and not one machine more.

is-davion.objectives.primary: Locate the seam in the remnant's belt and bring the layout home before the element is used up finding it. The main body will assault whatever you map. A probe that finds the gap saves a battalion the wall would have chewed up, and a probe that dies in the wall sends that battalion in blind.

inspiration: A boarding party cuts a single prize out of a defended harbor — slipping in among the guard ships, taking the one vessel that matters, and getting it out before the harbor's defenders can organize a response, where the whole act turns on speed and audacity rather than a stand-up fight.
skeleton: an extraction element must cut a single irreplaceable working component out of a guarded industrial yard annex and haul it clear before the yard's defense star can form, where the prize is delicate and one-of-a-kind so it cannot be fought over or risked in a firefight, and the crux is getting it out intact ahead of the forming response rather than winning the yard
title: OPERATION CUTTING OUT
situation: {TARGET_FACTION} is rebuilding a WarShip on {WORLD}, and {EMPLOYER} means to steal the one part it cannot replace. The orbital-yard ground annex at {DISTRICT} is the planetside works where heavy components are prepared before they are lifted up to the orbital slip. In it sits a recovered capital-grade drive subassembly. It is lostech the occupiers have spent two years restoring, the single irreplaceable piece of the hull they mean to put back in space. {EMPLOYER} does not want it destroyed. {EMPLOYER} wants to take it. A WarShip drive in friendly hands is worth more than this raid and more than the whole campaign. It is the kind of prize that changes what a faction can do. {NPC:intel-source}, a yard technician on {EMPLOYER}'s payroll, has the annex layout and the lift schedule. The subassembly sits in a conditioning cradle in the annex's main hall, already loaded on a heavy transporter for the move to the slip. A yard-security detail guards it, and a defense star waits at the works perimeter. The intel is {INTEL_AGE_DAYS} days old, and the lift schedule is your deadline. Once the drive is lifted up to the orbital slip, no ground force can reach it. The prize itself is the problem. It is delicate, one-of-a-kind, and loaded on a transporter that moves at a crawl. It cannot be fought over. It cannot take a stray round. It cannot survive the kind of firefight a raid on a guarded yard usually causes. So the whole job is a cutting-out. Slip into the annex among the yard's own traffic, take the transporter and its load, and drive it out through the works gate before the defense star forms up at the perimeter. You are not trying to win the yard. You are lifting one fragile thing out of the middle of it, faster than the guard can close in. The terrain is part of the problem. It is a dense industrial complex of gantries, hardstand, and rail. The main hall opens onto one heavy-vehicle gate, and the transporter is restricted to the few routes that can bear its weight — every one of them overlooked from the perimeter where the star waits. Recommended force: {FORCE_SIZE}, with a vehicle element to drive and screen the transporter and 'Mechs to hold the gate. Get into the annex, get the drive moving on its slow way out, and screen it through the gate intact before the star forms across the only routes that can carry it. The prize cannot survive being fought over. A raid that wins the yard but cracks the drive has still failed.

objectives.primary: Extract the recovered capital-grade drive subassembly from the annex intact — undamaged, on its transporter, and out through the works gate — before the yard's defense star forms across the heavy-vehicle routes.
objectives.secondary: Destroy the annex's conditioning hall and its remaining recovered components on the way out. Even without the drive itself, a destroyed conditioning works sets {TARGET_FACTION}'s WarShip program back years.
objectives.bonus: Recover the yard's restoration records for the drive. These documents let {EMPLOYER} understand and actually use the stolen subassembly, rather than just possess a component it cannot install.

complications.name: The Prize Cannot Be Fought Over
complications.text: The subassembly is delicate, irreplaceable, and mounted on a crawling transporter. A stray round, a near miss, or a hard knock against a gantry, and the prize is scrap and the raid is pointless. It cannot be risked in a firefight, which means the routes it travels cannot become a battlefield while it is on them.
complications.mechanicalEffect: The transporter and its load can be destroyed or crippled by combat in its hex or an adjacent one. The element must keep the fight away from the transporter's route: a firefight along the heavy-vehicle lanes endangers the prize directly, and a damaged subassembly fails the primary objective even if it clears the gate.

complications.name: The Slow Transporter
complications.text: The drive moves at a crawl on a heavy transporter restricted to the few routes that can bear its weight. It cannot dash for the gate, take a shortcut, or outrun anything. The element can only move as fast as the transporter, and the transporter sets a slow, predictable pace the defense star can plan against.
complications.mechanicalEffect: The transporter moves at a fixed slow rate, and only along weight-bearing routes. The element's withdrawal is paced to it. Faster units must screen it rather than flee, and the predictable route lets the defense star set up to intercept it ahead rather than chase it from behind.

complications.name: The Defense Star Forms
complications.text: A defense star is held at the works perimeter, not in the annex. It is not in the fight at the start, but it forms up fast once the alarm goes — and it forms across the perimeter the transporter must cross. The race is between the slow prize reaching the gate and the star assembling across the routes that lead to it.
complications.mechanicalEffect: The defense star is off-board at mission start and enters at the perimeter on the reaction timeline, deploying to block the heavy-vehicle routes. An element that has not screened the transporter through the gate before the star fully forms must fight past an assembled star with the fragile prize in the middle of the lane.

complications.name: The Lift May Come Early
complications.text: The schedule says the subassembly lifts to the slip on a known day, but a yard sets its own priorities. If the occupiers move the lift up — a slip ready early, or a security scare — the component may already be rigged to go up, or already gone, when the element reaches the hall.
complications.mechanicalEffect: On a die roll at the annex, the lift is further along than the schedule promised. The subassembly is partly rigged for orbital transfer and needs extra time to free and re-mount on the ground transporter. That lengthens the element's exposure inside the works before the withdrawal can even begin.

decisionPoints.name: Cutting It Out
decisionPoints.context: The drive is in the hall, the transporter crawls, and the defense star will form at the perimeter. You can slip in quietly among the yard traffic and hope to be moving before the alarm, take the gate first and hold the route open for the slow haul, or go in loud and fast to seize the transporter before the guard reacts. Each choice trades how long the prize is exposed against how hard it will be to beat the star to the gate.

options.title: Slip In Quiet
advantages: Enter among the yard's own traffic, take the transporter before the alarm, and have the prize crawling for the gate before the defense star even forms
The quietest start buys the biggest head start against the slow transporter's clock — every minute before the alarm is a minute the star is not assembling
disadvantages: A quiet infiltration of a guarded works is fragile. One challenged credential and the alarm goes off with the prize barely moving
No gate is held in advance, so if the alarm comes early the transporter crawls toward a perimeter the star is already forming across
options.consequence: If the infiltration holds, you are moving the prize before anyone knows. If it fails, the slow transporter is caught in the works with the gate unheld and the star forming — the worst possible place for something that cannot be fought over.

costs.resource: the whole timing staked on staying quiet until the prize is moving
costs.risk: An early alarm leaves the slow transporter in the works with the gate unheld and the star forming

options.title: Take the Gate First
advantages: Seize and hold the heavy-vehicle gate before touching the prize, guaranteeing the slow transporter an open route out when it comes
The 'Mechs hold the one exit the transporter can use, keeping the fight at the gate and away from the fragile load on the lane
disadvantages: Taking the gate is loud and starts the defense star forming immediately, before the prize is even rigged to move
The element is committed to holding the gate for the whole slow crawl, pinned in place against the assembling star
options.consequence: You secure the route out at the cost of an early alarm. The transporter has somewhere to go, but must crawl the whole way to a gate the element is holding against a star that began forming the moment the gate fell.

costs.resource: the element pinned holding the gate through the entire slow withdrawal
costs.risk: An early alarm and a long hold at the gate against a fully forming defense star

options.title: Fast and Loud
advantages: Hit the annex hard and fast, seize the transporter before the yard guard can react, and start the crawl with the prize already in hand
Moving fast at the seizure minimizes the time the subassembly sits in a contested hall before it is under {EMPLOYER}'s control
disadvantages: A loud assault brings the defense star at once and fills the works with fire — exactly the firefight the fragile prize cannot survive
Fighting in the annex endangers the subassembly before it is even on its way, the one outcome that fails the whole raid
options.consequence: You take the prize fastest but put it in the most danger. The seizure is nearly certain, but the crawl out runs through a roused yard with the star forming early and fire near the lane the drive cannot afford.

costs.resource: the prize seized fast, at the cost of an immediate, loud, yard-wide reaction
costs.risk: Fire in the annex and along the lane endangers the irreplaceable subassembly before it is clear

entries.event: The element enters the annex. Depending on the approach, the yard guard either stays unaware or the works alarm sounds.
The subassembly is freed and the transporter begins its slow crawl toward the heavy-vehicle gate.
The defense star forms at the perimeter and begins deploying across the weight-bearing routes toward the works.
The defense star reaches the approaches to the heavy-vehicle gate. The slow transporter is still short of clear.
The star is fully assembled across the perimeter. A transporter not through the gate by now must be screened out past an organized defense.

reactionTimeline.hardDeadline: The transporter must clear the works gate before the defense star fully forms across the routes at T+32:00. After that, the fragile prize is crawling through an assembled star's killing ground, with fire it cannot survive on every side. A raid that loses the drive to a stray round, or is stopped at the gate with the prize still in the lane, has failed no matter how much of the yard it holds.

opforSketch.composition: An orbital-yard ground defense, combined arms. At the start, a yard-security detail (infantry represented in the narrative plus a light utility vehicle or two) patrols the annex. The main threat is a defense star held at the perimeter — a medium-to-heavy 'Mech star (Regular to Veteran) backed by a few combat vehicles (the vehicle element of the board) — that forms up and deploys across the heavy-vehicle routes once the alarm sounds. The subassembly and its transporter are the fragile prize, not combatants.
