opforSketch.behavior: The yard security delays the element and raises the alarm rather than fighting a stand-up action. The defense star forms fast and positions to intercept the slow transporter at the gate and along its predictable route, rather than chasing into the works. It fights to recover the drive intact — it will not destroy the prize it spent two years restoring — so it presses the screening force hard while trying to stop the transporter without wrecking it. The star withdraws if reduced below roughly a third strength.

forks.name: OPERATION DEEP WATER PRIZE
forks.trigger: The drive subassembly was extracted intact through the gate and hauled clear.
forks.consequence: {EMPLOYER} now holds a recovered capital-grade drive, and {TARGET_FACTION}'s WarShip program has lost its single irreplaceable part. The next operation covers the prize's lift off {WORLD} against a faction now desperate to recover or destroy what it lost — a hard extraction of something too valuable to abandon.

forks.name: OPERATION CRACKED HULL
forks.trigger: The prize was lost — cracked by fire on the lane, stopped at the gate by the formed star, or the element was pinned in the works.
forks.consequence: The drive is destroyed or back in {TARGET_FACTION}'s hands, and the element is pinned in a roused yard. The next operation is a fighting withdrawal out of the works district, getting the survivors clear before the defense star and the garrison seal the industrial zone around them.

storyElementSeed: A transporter crew coaxes a crawling heavy hauler around a gantry corner with centimeters to spare, a capital drive subassembly riding its cradle above them, while a 'Mech walks slow alongside between the load and the perimeter, putting its own body where a stray round might otherwise go.

is-davion.objectives.primary: Get the drive out of that annex in one piece — on its hauler, through the gate, not a scratch on it — before the defense star locks up the heavy routes. We are stealing something that cannot be shot at. The job is the careful crawl out, not the fight in the yard.

merc.objectives.primary: Cut the drive subassembly out of the works intact and through the gate before the star forms. The contract pays for a working capital-grade component, not a cracked one. Keep the shooting off the lane it crawls down, because a drive with a hole in it is a fee we never collect.

TRANSPORTER_ROUTE_M.unit: meters from the hall to the works gate

STAR_FORM_MIN.unit: minutes for the defense star to fully form

inspiration: A raiding party strikes deep to seize an enemy commander alive from his own headquarters during a brief, predictable lapse in his protection — where the value is entirely in taking him breathing, because killing him buys nothing and may cost everything, and the clock is the window his guard is light.
skeleton: a raid element must reach and capture an enemy field commander alive from his command post inside the brief window his protective detail is in handover, where killing him is forbidden because his death triggers a reprisal the employer cannot afford, so the crux is a bloodless snatch against the clock of his guard reforming rather than a strike to destroy
title: OPERATION HANDOVER HOUR
situation: {EMPLOYER} wants a {TARGET_FACTION} saKhan captured alive. Alive is the whole contract, because he is worthless dead. This saKhan runs the occupation's field forces in the {DISTRICT} uplands of {WORLD} from a forward command post. {EMPLOYER} has decided the fastest way to break the occupation is to take the commander running it. Killing him would make him a martyr and create a blood-debt the Clan must answer. {EMPLOYER} is not strong enough to survive that reprisal. Rival Clans would also treat the killing as a dishonor that ruins a mercenary command's name. Taken alive, the saKhan is a hostage, a humiliation for his Clan, and a lever to end the occupation. Killed, he is a disaster. {NPC:intel-source}, a defector from his own staff, has found the one opening. The saKhan is always guarded by his protective point, elite warriors who never leave his side. They change shift on a fixed schedule. During each shift change there is a short gap: the old guards have stood down and the new ones have not yet taken their posts. For those few minutes only a thin watch protects him. This intelligence is {INTEL_AGE_DAYS} hours old, and the schedule can change. The location is the hard part. The command post is a cluster of hardened bunkers on a high mountain shelf, reached by a single switchback road. A guard Star rings it, and an alarm covers it. The moment any threat is spotted, that alarm sends the guard Star and the re-forming protective point down on the post fast. So the raiders must reach the post, take the saKhan out alive, and get off the shelf before the shift change ends and his guard re-forms. They must do it without a firefight that could kill the man they came for. Recommended force: {FORCE_SIZE}, with a fast vehicle element for the approach and the snatch, and 'Mechs to hold the road against the reaction force. Get in during the shift change, capture him alive, and get him off the shelf before his guard re-forms. The one thing you cannot do is the easy thing: kill him.

objectives.primary: Capture the {TARGET_FACTION} saKhan alive during the shift change in his protective point. Get him off the mountain shelf before the shift change ends and the guard Star re-forms.
objectives.secondary: Take the command post's staff officers or its operational records along with the saKhan. These reveal the occupation's plans, so a captured commander also hands you the enemy's whole campaign.
objectives.bonus: Extract the saKhan without wounding him at all. An unharmed commander gives {TARGET_FACTION} no grievance over mistreatment, keeps the hostage useful, and denies the Clan any excuse for reprisal.

complications.name: Alive Is the Whole Contract
complications.text: A dead saKhan becomes a martyr and creates a blood-debt the Clan must answer. His death would also wreck {EMPLOYER}'s name with the Clans and its rivals. He is worth everything alive and worse than nothing dead. So the raiders must take him alive in a fight where it would be far simpler to just shoot him.
complications.mechanicalEffect: If the saKhan is killed at any point, the operation fails to its worst outcome no matter what else is achieved, and this triggers the reprisal fork. The force must subdue him and get him out alive. Heavy weapons fire near his position risks killing him. That forces the raiders to hold back at the moment they would normally use full force.

complications.name: The Handover Window
complications.text: The protective point is a solid wall of guards except during the shift change, when it thins to a light watch. That window lasts only a few minutes, while the old guards have stepped down and the new ones have not yet taken their posts. Arrive too early and the saKhan is behind his full guard. Arrive too late and the wall has re-formed. The capture has to happen inside those few minutes and no other time.
complications.mechanicalEffect: The capture is only possible during the shift-change window shown on the reaction timeline. Before and after it, the saKhan is behind his full protective point and capturing him is effectively impossible. The force must be in position to take him during the window. Waiting nearby too early risks being spotted. Arriving late finds the guard already back in place.

complications.name: The Schedule May Shift
complications.text: The shift change runs on a schedule, but the Clan can change that schedule at will. A security alert, the saKhan's own orders, or a cautious staff officer can move the shift change earlier, later, or to a different time of day. The defector's timing is already hours old, and a forward command post does not announce when it changes its routine.
complications.mechanicalEffect: If the dice call for it at the approach, the shift-change window has moved from the briefed time. The force must find the actual shift change by watching the command post and adjust its plan on the spot. This risks either striking too early, while the full guard is still in place, or too late, after the guard has begun re-forming.

complications.name: The Alert Brings the Star
complications.text: The command post is ringed by a guard Star and wired to an alarm. The moment any threat is spotted on the shelf, that alarm brings the guard Star and the re-forming guards down on the command post fast. The shift change that thins the saKhan's personal guard does nothing to slow the alarm. The instant the raiders are seen, the entire mountain defense converges on them.
complications.mechanicalEffect: Being detected on the shelf triggers the alarm. The guard Star and the protective point then converge on the command post on a faster timeline (see the reaction timeline). A force discovered before it has the saKhan must fight the whole mountain defense to reach him. Staying unseen until the capture is what keeps the odds survivable.

decisionPoints.name: Taking the Commander
decisionPoints.context: The saKhan is in his command post, the shift change thins his guard for a few minutes, and killing him is forbidden. You have three ways to take him. You can infiltrate the command post quietly and carry him out before the alarm sounds. You can storm the thin watch fast during the window. Or you can draw the guard Star away with a diversion and snatch him through the gap it opens. Each choice trades how likely the saKhan is to survive against how hard it will be to get off the shelf with him alive.

options.title: Infiltrate and Lift
advantages: Slip into the command post during the shift change, subdue the thin watch quietly, and carry the saKhan out before the alarm sounds. This is the surest way to take him unharmed.
A silent capture leaves the saKhan unmarked and gives {TARGET_FACTION} no grievance over mistreatment, making him the most useful possible hostage
disadvantages: A quiet entry into a hardened command post is fragile. One alert sentry and the saKhan is behind a guard that is waking up, with the raiders trapped inside the perimeter.
Infiltration is slow and does not handle a changed schedule well. If the shift change moves while the raiders are still creeping in, the window can close before they reach him.
options.consequence: If the infiltration goes undetected, you take the saKhan unharmed and quietly. If it is discovered, the raiders are inside the command post perimeter with the alarm sounding and the man they cannot kill in the middle of a firefight.

costs.resource: The whole capture is staked on entering silently through the thinned watch.
costs.risk: A sentry who spots the raiders traps them inside the command post perimeter with the guard waking and the saKhan unprotected.

options.title: Storm the Thin Watch
advantages: Hit the command post hard and fast during the shift-change window, overwhelm the thin watch before it can react, and seize the saKhan in the minutes his guard is down
Speed beats the re-forming guard. The saKhan is taken before the shift change finishes, even if the alarm goes off.
disadvantages: A fast, violent assault around the saKhan is exactly the kind of fire that risks killing the man you need alive
Storming the command post sets off the alarm immediately, bringing the guard Star down while the raiders are still securing the saKhan
options.consequence: You take him quickly during the window, but at the cost of heavy fire near him and an instant alarm. The capture is fast, but the saKhan is in the middle of a firefight he has to survive and the guard Star is already converging.

costs.resource: The saKhan's survival is risked in a fast, violent assault.
costs.risk: Fire near the saKhan during the assault endangers the one thing that cannot be lost, with the alarm already sounding.

options.title: Feint and Snatch
advantages: Draw the guard Star toward a staged threat on the road up to the shelf, then take the saKhan through the gap the diversion opens in the perimeter
Splits the mountain defense so the capture faces only part of it, giving the raiders room to take the saKhan unharmed
disadvantages: The diversion may set off the alarm that moves the shift change or closes the guard early, ruining the window the capture depends on
A divided force is weaker at the capture itself. If the diversion fails to pull the guard Star away, the raiders hit the command post with the full perimeter still intact.
options.consequence: Timed right, the diversion thins the perimeter and the saKhan comes out through the gap. Timed wrong, the diversion either sets off the alarm early or fails to draw the guard Star, and the capture goes in against a defense that is still whole.

costs.resource: A staged threat that may set off the very alarm it was meant to exploit.
costs.risk: A diversion that fails to draw the guard Star away leaves the capture facing the full command post perimeter.

entries.event: The shift change begins. The outgoing guards step down and the saKhan's protection thins to a light watch.
The shift-change window is at its widest. The saKhan is easiest to reach now and the incoming guards have not yet taken their posts.
The incoming guards begin taking their posts. The window to take the saKhan is closing.
If the alarm has sounded, the guard Star is converging on the command post and the protective point is re-forming around the saKhan's position.
The protective point is fully back in place and the guard Star is assembled. The saKhan is behind his full guard again and the shelf is sealed.

reactionTimeline.hardDeadline: Capture the saKhan and get the raiders off the shelf before the protective point re-forms and the guard Star assembles at T+30:00. After that the commander is behind his full guard on a sealed shelf. Any raiders still there are fighting the whole mountain defense for a man they are forbidden to kill. The capture has failed, and a saKhan killed in that fight is the exact catastrophe this contract was written to avoid.

opforSketch.composition: A Clan forward-command defense, combined arms. The saKhan's protective point is elite warriors (represented as powered infantry close around the commander). The command post is ringed by a guard Star of light-to-medium 'Mechs (Regular to Veteran) in prepared positions, backed by a few combat vehicles on the road up to the shelf (the vehicle element of the force). The reaction force is the re-forming protective point plus the guard Star, converging when the alarm sounds. The saKhan himself is the objective, to be taken alive, not a unit to be destroyed.
opforSketch.behavior: The guard Star holds the perimeter and does not pursue off the shelf until the alarm sounds. On alarm, it and the protective point converge hard on the commander's position to recover him. The defense fights to protect the saKhan above all else: it will close on his position rather than chase the raiders, and the moment he is in enemy hands it presses to retake him while he is still alive. It breaks off only if reduced to roughly a third of its strength and the saKhan is already lost.

forks.name: OPERATION HELD LEVER
forks.trigger: The saKhan was captured alive and taken off the shelf, ideally unharmed.
forks.consequence: {EMPLOYER} now holds the commander who ran the occupation. {TARGET_FACTION}'s field command is leaderless and forced to bargain. The next operation hits the now-disordered occupation forces, and the captured saKhan's records open up plans no raid could have reached.

forks.name: OPERATION BLOOD DEBT
forks.trigger: The saKhan was killed, recovered by his guard, or the raiders were pinned on the shelf without him.
forks.consequence: If the commander died, the reprisal {EMPLOYER} feared is now coming, and the rival Clans have the story they wanted. The next operation is a desperate escape of the surviving raiders off {WORLD}, ahead of a Clan answering the blood-debt, with the mercenary command's name in ruins. The catastrophe the capture was meant to prevent has happened, and now it has to be survived.

storyElementSeed: A raider crouches in the dark at the edge of the command post. The old guards file away and the new ones have not yet arrived. A tranquilizer charge and a set of restraints wait ready. The man inside is worth a fortune taken alive, and a whole war if he dies.

is-davion.objectives.primary: Take the saKhan alive out of his own command post during the guard change, and get him off that shelf before the guard re-forms. Alive is the order, and it matters twice over. A dead Clan commander means a war we cannot fight. A live one is the lever that ends this occupation.

is-steiner.objectives.primary: Capture the saKhan unharmed during the shift-change window and extract him before the guard Star forms up. The math is brutal and simple. Alive, he is the most valuable asset on this front. Dead, he is a debt that bankrupts the whole enterprise. Bring him back whole.

SHELF_APPROACH_KM.unit: km of switchback approach to the CP

inspiration: Lacking the explosives to destroy a hardened underground facility outright, a small team turns the installation's own safety system against it — triggering a flood or suppression mechanism built to protect the works so that it drowns or buries them instead, a denial achieved with the enemy's own infrastructure.
skeleton: an infiltration element must wreck a hardened subterranean refit depot by triggering the facility's own flood-and-suppression system to bury it rather than by explosives it does not have, where reaching and arming the control gallery is the whole problem and the trigger that destroys the works also seals the only way out, so the crux is the timed self-destruction from inside
title: OPERATION OWN WATERS
situation: {TARGET_FACTION} keeps its forward 'Mech-refit depot underground, and {EMPLOYER} means to destroy it by flooding it with the depot's own water. Beneath the ridge at {DISTRICT} on {WORLD}, the occupiers have dug a refit cavern into the rock. It is an underground workshop where the touman's machines are repaired and rearmed. It is hardened against both orbital fire and ground assault, and it is the one facility keeping the front's 'Mechs running. Air attack cannot reach it, and nothing {EMPLOYER} can field on the ground can break in. The rock is too deep and the few entrances are too well defended. But its builders left one weakness. The cavern has a flood-and-suppression system: large pumps and reservoirs meant to put out a fire or contain a breach and save the works. Turn that system on when there is no fire to fight, and it floods the very tunnels it was built to protect. The water drowns the repair bays and buries the depot. {NPC:intel-source}, an engineer who helped build the system, has the layout and the catch. The flood is armed from a control room deep inside the cavern, past the repair bays. The moment it triggers, the same system seals the entrances behind blast doors. This intelligence is {INTEL_AGE_DAYS} days old, and the engineer's access codes may have been changed since. The cavern is the hard part. A single hardened entrance opens into tunnels that descend into the rock, with the repair bays in the middle and the control room at the deep end. Every meter is underground, with no way around anything and no cover but the rock, and the guard force knows it is fighting in a sealed box. Here is the cruel part. The team has to reach the control room, arm the flood, then get back out past the repair bays before the blast doors close and the water rises. The trigger that destroys the depot is the same trigger that traps whoever throws it, so the whole mission is timing the flood against your own escape. Recommended force: {FORCE_SIZE}, light and fast, on foot and in light 'Mechs that can fit through the tunnels. Reach the control room, turn the depot's own flood against it, and get back through the entrance before the cavern seals and floods. There are no demolition charges for this job. The only weapon here is the cavern's own pumps.

objectives.primary: Reach the cavern's control room, arm the flood-and-suppression system to flood the refit depot, and get the team back out through the entrance before the blast doors seal and the water rises.
objectives.secondary: Wreck the repair bays' machine tools and ammunition stocks on the way in or out. Even if the flood is only partial, a depot stripped of its tools cannot repair whatever survives the water.
objectives.bonus: Recover the depot's repair records before triggering the flood. They show which of {TARGET_FACTION}'s machines are down here and for how long, telling {EMPLOYER} exactly what the flooding costs the enemy.

complications.name: The Cavern's Own Weapon
complications.text: There are no explosives for this job. The rock is too deep to crack, and any charges small enough to carry in would not matter. The only weapon is the facility's own flood system, built to save the works and now turned against them. The team cannot destroy the depot directly. They can only make the depot destroy itself, and that means reaching the one control room that triggers the flood.
complications.mechanicalEffect: The primary objective can only be achieved by reaching and arming the control room. There is no demolition alternative. The team must penetrate all the way to the deep end of the cavern past the repair bays. Destroying anything short of the control room does not trigger the flood and leaves the depot working.

complications.name: The Trigger Seals the Door
complications.text: When the flood system triggers, it closes the entrance blast doors. That is what it is designed to do: seal the works and contain the flood. So arming the flood starts a countdown both to the rising water and to those doors closing. Anyone on the wrong side of the doors when they shut is trapped in the flooding cavern.
complications.mechanicalEffect: Arming the flood starts a timer. When it runs out, the blast doors seal and the tunnels flood. The team must clear the entrance before the timer expires. The same trigger destroys the depot and closes the only way out, so the escape is a race against a countdown the team started.

complications.name: Fighting in a Sealed Box
complications.text: The cavern is underground with no way around anything and no cover but the rock, and the guard force knows it. A fight in the tunnels is a fight in a pipe. There is nowhere to maneuver and nowhere to break off. Numbers and position decide everything, and the only way past a defended junction is straight through it.
complications.mechanicalEffect: Movement through the tunnels is along a single path, junction to junction. There are no flanking routes and no cover except the rock. A defended junction has to be attacked head-on. A team bogged down in a tunnel fight burns the time it needs to reach the control room and get back out before the flood timer runs out.

complications.name: The Codes May Have Rotated
complications.text: The engineer's knowledge of the control room is days old, and a working system gets maintained. The codes that arm the flood may have been changed and the controls re-secured since the engineer left. The team may reach the deep control room only to find the trigger harder to throw than they were promised.
complications.mechanicalEffect: If the dice call for it at the control room, the flood-arming codes are partly out of date. The team needs extra time to work past the re-secured controls, which lengthens the time they are exposed at the deep end of the cavern and shortens their margin to escape before the doors seal.

decisionPoints.name: Into the Rock
decisionPoints.context: The control room is at the deep end past the repair bays, the guard holds the tunnels, and arming the flood seals the door behind you. You have three ways to do this. You can slip in quietly and reach the trigger before the guard knows you are there. You can fight straight through to the deep control room fast. Or you can split your force, leaving part of it to hold the entrance open while a small team arms the flood. Each choice trades how deep you can get without a fight against how sure you are of getting back out before the doors close.

options.title: Slip to the Trigger
advantages: Move through the tunnels quietly, reach the control room before the guard reacts, and arm the flood with the most time left on your escape clock
A quiet approach means the doors-and-water countdown starts with the guard scattered, not lined up across your escape route
disadvantages: A silent move through a hardened cavern is fragile. One contact and the team is in a tunnel fight deep underground.
If discovered short of the control room, the team must fight forward to the trigger and then fight back out, with no margin against the flood
options.consequence: If the team stays unseen, the flood is armed before anyone knows and the escape has its full margin. If they are spotted, they are deep in the rock in a pipe fight with the trigger still ahead and a long way back to the exit.

costs.resource: The whole approach is staked on reaching the deep control room unseen.
costs.risk: Being discovered deep in the cavern traps the team in a tunnel fight with the trigger not yet thrown and the exit far away.

options.title: Drive Straight Through
advantages: Push through the tunnels fast, fight straight to the control room, and arm the flood before the guard can fully concentrate against you
Speed gets the trigger thrown quickly, leaving the most time to fight back out before the doors seal
disadvantages: Fighting your way into a sealed box is costly. The team takes losses against defended junctions on the way in and must do it again on the way out.
The guard concentrates behind you as you push in, so the escape runs back through tunnels the team has already stirred up
options.consequence: You reach and throw the trigger fast, at the cost of a hard fight both ways. The flood is armed, but the escape is a run back through a concentrated guard with the water rising and the doors closing.

costs.resource: The team's strength is spent fighting through the tunnels in and back out.
costs.risk: A guard concentrated behind the team turns the escape into a second fight, run against the flood timer.

options.title: Hold the Door, Arm the Flood
advantages: A holding force keeps the entrance and the approach to the blast doors open while a small team pushes in to arm the flood, guaranteeing a way out
The holding force can keep the path to the doors clear, so the arming team is not racing a closing door through a contested tunnel
disadvantages: A divided force is weaker at both ends. The holding force may not keep the entrance, and the arming team has little to fall back on.
When the flood triggers, the holding force also has to clear the doors before they seal, and a force dug in at the entrance may be slow to pull out
options.consequence: Done well, the arming team throws the trigger and falls back through a held entrance to a clean escape. Done poorly, the holding force is overrun or trapped at the doors, and the flood seals part of the team inside.

costs.resource: The force is split between holding the entrance and reaching the trigger.
costs.risk: A holding force dug in at the entrance is caught by the sealing doors while the arming team is still escaping.

entries.event: The team enters the cavern's entrance. Depending on the approach, the guard either stays unaware or the depot alarm sounds in the tunnels.
The team reaches the repair bays in the middle of the cavern. The guard force begins concentrating against them.
The team reaches the control room at the deep end and begins arming the flood-and-suppression system.
The flood is armed. The countdown to the blast doors sealing and the tunnels flooding begins, and the team turns back for the entrance.
The blast doors seal and the water rises. Anyone not clear of the entrance by now is trapped in the flooding cavern.

reactionTimeline.hardDeadline: Clear the entrance before the blast doors seal at T+34:00. That is the countdown the team started when they armed the flood. After that the doors are shut and the tunnels are flooding, and anyone still inside drowns with the depot they came to destroy. The sabotage works but kills the people who set it, so the mission is won and lost at the same time.

opforSketch.composition: A Clan underground-depot guard, all 'Mechs in the tunnels: light 'Mechs (20-40 tons) suited to the confined underground works, at Regular to Veteran quality, plus a guard force represented as infantry holding the junctions, since the tunnels are too tight for much else. No vehicles, because the tunnels are no place for them. The depot's machines under repair are powered down (some may be partly working and may stir if the fight reaches their bay). The flood system and the control room are the objective, not combatants.
opforSketch.behavior: The guard fights the cavern as a sealed box, holding junctions and concentrating against the team rather than maneuvering. It defends the control room hardest, knowing what its loss means, and falls back deeper rather than give up the trigger. Once the flood is armed, the guard switches to escaping the cavern itself ahead of the doors and the water. A guard that realizes the depot is lost will race the team for the entrance rather than fight to the last.

forks.name: OPERATION DROWNED FORGE
forks.trigger: The flood was armed and triggered, the depot flooded, and the team cleared the entrance before the doors sealed.
forks.consequence: The forward refit depot is buried under its own water, and {TARGET_FACTION}'s front loses the works that kept its machines running. The next operation strikes the now-unsupported occupation forces while their damaged 'Mechs sit unrepairable and the touman scrambles for repair capacity it no longer has.

forks.name: OPERATION SEALED IN
forks.trigger: The trigger was never reached, the flood failed to arm, or part of the team was sealed in the cavern by the doors.
forks.consequence: Either the depot still runs or part of the team is lost in the flooded tunnels. The next operation is a fighting withdrawal of the survivors out of the depot district, under an alerted garrison and with a hunt closing in on the ridge. They leave the works still intact behind them, or their own dead sealed in the rock.

storyElementSeed: A team works fast at a control console deep in the rock, idle repair machinery humming around them. An engineer reads off the arming sequence by the light of a single lamp. Every one of them is listening past the words for the first groan of the great pumps coming alive.

merc.objectives.primary: Get to the control room at the bottom of the cavern, turn the depot's own flood on against it, and be back out the entrance before the doors slam shut and the water comes up. There are no charges for this one. The only weapon is their own pumps, and the only way to lose worse than failing is to drown with the place.

is-steiner.objectives.primary: Reach the flood controls deep in the works, arm the suppression system to flood the refit depot, and clear the entrance before it seals. We cannot break into this vault with anything we own, so we make it destroy itself, and we leave before its own design closes the door on us.

GALLERY_DEPTH_M.unit: meters of gallery to the control room

FLOOD_COUNTDOWN_MIN.unit: minutes from arming to the doors sealing

inspiration: A fast mobile force races to get ahead of a retreating enemy mobile headquarters and throw a block across its line of march before it can reach safety, where the enemy keeps displacing to stay ahead and the whole problem is outrunning it to the chokepoint rather than catching it from behind.
skeleton: a fast pursuit force must overtake a continuously self-displacing enemy mobile field headquarters and block it short of its fortified laager, where the HQ never stops moving and outrunning it to a chokepoint ahead is the only way to fix it, so the crux is the cross-country race to get in front rather than the fight to take it
title: OPERATION GET AHEAD
situation: A {TARGET_FACTION} mobile field headquarters is running for its fortress. {EMPLOYER} has one fast force to get in front of it and cut it off. The occupation's forward command on {WORLD} never stays in one place. It is a mobile headquarters, a column of command and support vehicles that keeps moving across the {DISTRICT} flats. Moving is how it stays ahead of exactly the kind of strike {EMPLOYER} now intends. An offensive elsewhere has flushed it out and forced it to retreat. It is now heading for a fortified base at the edge of the flats, where it will be beyond reach. {EMPLOYER} wants it captured or destroyed before it gets there. Capturing the occupation's command would collapse their front. Letting it reach the fortress means a long, drawn-out campaign. {NPC:intel-source} is tracking the column by its radio and engine emissions and has its route and its speed. It moves fast for a headquarters, guarded by an escort force, stopping only briefly to keep its command duties running. It will reach the fortress in hours. This intelligence is {INTEL_AGE_DAYS} hours old, and the headquarters can change its route at any moment. The problem is not catching the column. A chase from behind never catches a force moving at the same speed. The problem is getting ahead of it. Somewhere on the flats, between the column and its fortress, the terrain forces the column's heavy vehicles through one narrow gap. A force that reaches that gap first can block the only route the headquarters can take and pin it in the open. The flats are open and fast going for hovercraft and light units. But the column has that same fast going, plus a head start. So both sides are racing to the gap along different paths. You cut straight across while the headquarters runs the longer curve. Recommended force: {FORCE_SIZE}, mostly hovercraft and light units. Speed is your only weapon here, so field the fastest force {EMPLOYER} can muster. You win by reaching the gap before the column does. You lose by arriving a minute too late. The fight for the headquarters only matters if you are in front of it when it gets there.

objectives.primary: Get ahead of the {TARGET_FACTION} mobile headquarters and block it at the chokepoint before it reaches its fortress, pinning the column in the open so it can be captured or destroyed.
objectives.secondary: Capture the headquarters' command staff and command vehicles intact rather than destroying them. A captured command yields the occupation's plans. A wrecked one yields only wreckage.
objectives.bonus: Cut off and capture the headquarters' communications section before it can radio a warning to the fortress. A fortress that does not know its command is lost will not send a force out to rescue it.

complications.name: The Stern Chase Never Closes
complications.text: A force chasing a moving column from behind never catches it. The column keeps the lead it started with and runs out the clock until it reaches its fortress. The only way to pin the headquarters is to get ahead of it, which means not following its path but cutting across to a point on it. This is a race won by taking the shorter route, not by raw speed alone.
complications.mechanicalEffect: Chasing directly behind the column cannot bring it to battle before it reaches the fortress. The pursuit force must move to intercept the chokepoint ahead, not the column's current position. A force that commits to chasing from behind arrives too late, and the primary objective fails (dropping to its withdrawal value).

complications.name: The Column Keeps Moving
complications.text: The mobile headquarters does not stop. It halts only briefly to keep its command duties running, then moves again, always toward the fortress. There is no fixed target to close in on, only a route and a speed, and a headquarters that changes both the moment it senses a force cutting across its front.
complications.mechanicalEffect: The headquarters advances toward the fortress every turn and cannot be pinned anywhere except the chokepoint. If it detects the pursuit force angling to cut it off, it may change its route or speed up, forcing the pursuer to re-plan the intercept on the move against a headquarters actively dodging the block.

complications.name: The Guard Screens the Run
complications.text: The headquarters travels behind a guard force whose only job is to keep a pursuer off the column long enough to reach the fortress. The guard does not need to win. It needs to delay, to force the pursuit force to fight when it should be racing, sacrificing itself for the minutes the headquarters needs to get past the chokepoint.
complications.mechanicalEffect: The guard force places itself between the pursuit force and the column and tries to force fights that cost the pursuer time. Stopping to destroy the guard loses the race. Going around it leaves it free to harass the block. The pursuer must decide how much of the guard to fight and how much to outrun.

complications.name: The Route May Change
complications.text: A mobile headquarters tracked by its emissions knows it can be tracked, so it changes its route to throw off the trackers. The chokepoint the pursuit force is racing toward may not be the one the column uses if it swings wide, and the intelligence on its route is already hours old and getting less reliable by the minute.
complications.mechanicalEffect: If the dice call for it during the race, the column turns toward a different route and a different chokepoint. The pursuit force must detect the change and redirect its intercept, losing ground if it committed early to the wrong chokepoint and risking arriving at an empty block while the headquarters runs through a different gap.

decisionPoints.name: Winning the Race
decisionPoints.context: The column runs for its fortress and the chokepoint is the only place to pin it. You have three ways to play this. You can commit everything to the fastest possible intercept and trust that the short route beats the long one. You can split your force, sending a blocking force ahead and a harassing force after the column. Or you can drive straight at the guard force to strip away the column's protection first. Each choice trades how sure you are of reaching the chokepoint first against how much of your force is there to hold it when the column arrives.

options.title: All Speed to the Block
advantages: Commit the whole force to the fastest route to the chokepoint, giving the best chance of getting in front of the column before it passes
Arriving at the block at full strength means the headquarters hits a wall it cannot push through and is pinned in the open for the taking
disadvantages: An all-out race ignores the guard force, which is then free to harass the block and buy the column time once it arrives
If the column changes its route, a force fully committed to one chokepoint has the farthest to redirect and may miss the block entirely
options.consequence: If you win the race, the headquarters is pinned against your full strength. If the route changes or the guard reaches the block first, a fully committed force is caught out of position with no reserve to recover.

costs.resource: The whole force is staked on one intercept route to one chokepoint.
costs.risk: A route change leaves the full force racing to the wrong block with no margin to redirect.

options.title: Block Ahead, Harry Behind
advantages: Split off a fast blocking force for the chokepoint and a harassing force onto the column's rear to slow it down and disrupt the guard
The harassing force can make the headquarters fight to its rear while the block sets up ahead, improving the odds the block is ready in time
disadvantages: A divided force is weaker at the block. If the column reaches the chokepoint before the block is strong, it may push through.
The harassing force risks being drawn into the guard's delaying fight, helping neither the race nor the block
options.consequence: Done well, the harassment slows the column enough for the block to set up and the headquarters is caught between the two forces. Done poorly, the block is too thin to hold and the harassers are too tied up to help, and the column slips through.

costs.resource: The force is divided between the block ahead and the harassment behind.
costs.risk: A thin block reached too late is pushed through by a column the harassers could not slow down enough.

options.title: Strip the Screen First
advantages: Drive at the guard force and break it, stripping away the column's protection so the headquarters runs unprotected for the fortress
A broken guard cannot delay or harass the block. Once the protection is gone, the column is far easier to pin and capture.
disadvantages: Fighting the guard loses the race. The time spent breaking the guard is time the headquarters uses to reach the chokepoint or the fortress.
The guard may delay just long enough to cost the pursuer the race while still being destroyed, the worst of both outcomes
options.consequence: You remove the guard at the cost of time. If the guard breaks fast, the column is yours to run down. If it sells its delay well, the headquarters is through the chokepoint before the pursuit force is free to chase.

costs.resource: Time in the race spent breaking the column's guard force.
costs.risk: The guard's delay costs the race even as it is destroyed, letting the headquarters reach the fortress.

entries.event: The pursuit force is released onto the flats. The mobile headquarters is already moving toward its fortress with a head start.
The column detects a force angling across its front and adjusts its speed and guard, pushing toward the fortress.
The pursuit force's intercept route crosses toward the chokepoint. The column nears the open ground in front of it.
The race converges on the chokepoint. Whichever force reaches it first holds it, and the other must fight for it.
The column reaches the approaches to the fortress. A headquarters not blocked before this point passes under the fortress guns and is gone.

reactionTimeline.hardDeadline: The pursuit force must reach the chokepoint and block the column before the headquarters passes into the fortress approaches at T+2:30. After that the headquarters is under the fortress guns and beyond reach, and a pursuit force that arrives behind it has run a hard race for nothing. The front stays whole, the occupation keeps its command, and the chance does not come again.

opforSketch.composition: A Clan mobile headquarters and its guard, combined arms. The headquarters is a column of command and support vehicles (the vehicle element of the force, and the objective, to be captured intact). The guard is a fast 'Mech Star (light-to-medium, 25-50 tons, Regular to Veteran) plus its own fast combat vehicles, built for screening and delay. If blocked, the column's guard fights to break the block open; if cornered, the headquarters vehicles scatter rather than stand. A fortress garrison stays put and only sends out a force if the headquarters reaches the approaches.
opforSketch.behavior: The headquarters runs for the fortress and does not stop, changing route and speed to dodge an intercept. The guard fights to delay rather than to win, trading ground and itself for the column's time, and places itself between the pursuer and the headquarters. If the block is set up first, the guard tries to force it open while the headquarters looks for another gap. If the block holds, the column is pinned and its guard fights hardest then. The guard breaks off if reduced to roughly a third of its strength and the headquarters is already pinned or lost.

forks.name: OPERATION FRONT COLLAPSED
forks.trigger: The headquarters was blocked before reaching the fortress and captured or destroyed in the open.
forks.consequence: The occupation's forward command is captured or shattered, and {TARGET_FACTION}'s front on {WORLD} loses its leadership. The next operation exploits the now-leaderless occupation forces. The headquarters' captured staff and records open up the whole campaign. An entire front is rolled up because one fast race was won.

forks.name: OPERATION RAN HOME
forks.trigger: The headquarters reached its fortress, or the pursuit force was caught out of position or worn down by the guard.
forks.consequence: The headquarters is safe behind the fortress guns and the chance is gone. The next operation is a withdrawal of the pursuit force off the flats before the fortress garrison comes out after an exposed, spent raiding force deep in contested ground far from support.

storyElementSeed: A hover lance throws up a rooster-tail of dust across the open flats on a slanting line. A commander watches a display where two tracks crawl toward the same point on the map. The whole thing comes down to which dust cloud reaches the gap first.

is-steiner.objectives.primary: Get in front of that running headquarters and slam the chokepoint shut before it reaches its fortress. You will not catch it from behind. Win the race to the gap, pin it in the open, and take the command staff intact, because a captured occupation headquarters is a whole front added to the ledger.

merc.objectives.primary: Outrun the column to the chokepoint and block it before it reaches the fortress. Chasing it from behind is a fool's errand. You win by getting ahead. Pin the headquarters in the open and the contract is paid in full. Let it reach the fortress and we ran the flats for nothing.

inspiration: A single infiltrator threads a guarded sensor line by timing movement to the gaps in a regular sweep, crossing into the enemy's rear not to fight but to emplace something that must be in place before a coming operation — where being detected ruins everything and the whole skill is reading the cadence of the watch.
skeleton: a single stealth-equipped unit must thread a Clan sensor-picket line by moving only inside the gaps of a regular detection sweep and emplace a beacon deep in the enemy rear, where any detection voids the mission and the unit cannot fight its way through, so the crux is reading and beating the sweep cadence to plant a thing rather than to destroy one
title: OPERATION QUIET STEP
situation: {EMPLOYER} has one stealth 'Mech and one chance to walk it through {TARGET_FACTION}'s sensor line. The occupation screens the approaches to its rear staging area on {WORLD} with a sensor-picket line across the {DISTRICT} icefields. The line is a chain of detection posts plus a regular sweep, and together they make the open ice a wall no force has crossed unseen. {EMPLOYER} does not need to cross it with a force. It needs to place one thing on the far side. That thing is a guidance beacon, planted deep in the enemy rear and left switched off. When the coming offensive begins, its lead units will have a navigation fix and a set of eyes in ground the enemy believes is a safe, unwatched rear area. The tool for the job is a single 'Mech carrying recovered stealth armor. The picket's sensors have trouble holding a lock on it, though only trouble, not total failure. {NPC:intel-source} is a defector from the signals staff who has found the weakness to exploit. The sweep runs on a fixed rhythm, passing over the line again and again with brief gaps between passes. A stealthed unit that moves only during the gaps and holds still during the passes can slip through without the line ever locking onto it. This intelligence is {INTEL_AGE_DAYS} days old, and the sweep rhythm can be changed. This is not a fight and cannot become one. The 'Mech carries the beacon, not weapons for a raid. A single 'Mech detected on the wrong side of a picket line is a single 'Mech hunted down by an entire occupation rear area. The whole skill is reading the rhythm. Move when the sweep has passed, freeze when it comes back, and step through the gaps to plant the beacon and walk back out. Never let the line lock onto your position. The icefield is flat, open, and cold. The cold, quiet background helps the stealth armor hide its emissions, but the open ice offers no cover at all if the sweep catches the 'Mech moving. On the ice there is nowhere to hide. There is only the stealth and the timing between your 'Mech and the sweep. Recommended force: {FORCE_SIZE}, one stealth-equipped 'Mech and the discipline to cross a sensor line by patience instead of firepower. Beat the sweep, plant the beacon deep, and bring the 'Mech home undetected. You win by never being seen and lose the instant the picket gets a lock on you.

objectives.primary: Slip through the sensor-picket line undetected, plant the guidance beacon at the assigned point deep in the enemy rear, and withdraw the stealth 'Mech back across the line without the picket ever locking onto it.
objectives.secondary: Map the picket line's post positions and sweep rhythm on the way through. This is the information that lets the coming offensive's main force cross the line at the spot where this 'Mech proved it can be crossed.
objectives.bonus: Plant a second dormant relay at a fallback point on the way out. This backup keeps the offensive's eyes open even if the main beacon is found and destroyed.

complications.name: Detection Voids It
complications.text: The whole mission depends on staying unseen. A stealth 'Mech the picket has trouble holding a lock on is not a stealth 'Mech it can never lock onto. The instant the line gets a lock, the beacon's secret dies along with the surprise. The enemy knows something crossed, hunts the 'Mech, and sweeps its own rear for whatever was planted. There is no fighting through. One lock and the operation is over.
complications.mechanicalEffect: Any sustained detection by the picket line ruins the mission's value (the FAILURE fork triggers even if the beacon is planted, because a beacon the enemy knows to look for is a beacon the enemy finds). The stealth 'Mech cannot attack to clear a post, because firing reveals it. Success requires reaching the planting point and returning without the picket ever locking on.

complications.name: The Sweep Cadence
complications.text: The sensor sweep passes over the line on a fixed rhythm, alternating passes and gaps, and the 'Mech survives in the gaps. Move while the sweep is on the unit and the stealth armor's margin shrinks toward a lock. Move only in the gap and hold still for each pass, and the line cannot lock on. The rhythm is the whole problem, and it does not wait for the unit to be ready.
complications.mechanicalEffect: The picket sweep runs on a timed rhythm of passes and gaps. The stealth 'Mech may move during gaps with little detection risk and must keep movement to a minimum during passes (moving during a pass builds up detection risk toward a lock). Reading and timing to that rhythm is the core mechanic. Mistiming a move into a pass risks being located.

complications.name: The Cadence May Have Changed
complications.text: The defector's read of the sweep is days old, and a sensor watch that suspects nothing still rotates its patterns. The rhythm may have changed, a post may have been added, and the rhythm the 'Mech is timing to may not be the rhythm the line is actually running. The unit may step into a gap that is no longer there.
complications.mechanicalEffect: If the dice call for it at the line, the actual sweep rhythm differs from the briefed pattern. The 'Mech must re-read the rhythm on the spot by watching one full cycle before committing to cross, spending time exposed near the line while it confirms the real rhythm rather than trusting the stale one.

complications.name: The Open Ice
complications.text: The icefield gives the stealth armor the quiet, cold background that helps it hide, but it gives the unit no cover at all. If the sweep catches the 'Mech moving, there is nowhere to break line of sight, no terrain to duck behind. There is only the stealth, and the stealth alone does not save a unit the line has locked onto.
complications.mechanicalEffect: The icefield hides emissions (which helps the stealth) but offers no physical cover (nothing to break line of sight). A 'Mech that draws detection cannot use terrain to shake it. It must rely entirely on holding still and the stealth margin, with no fallback if the line gets a partial lock and works to confirm it.

decisionPoints.name: Crossing the Line
decisionPoints.context: The picket sweeps on its rhythm and the beacon must be planted deep. You have three ways across. You can cross fast in a single bold dash between passes. You can creep through patiently over many sweep cycles. Or you can cross at a seam, where the coverage of two posts overlaps the thinnest. Each choice trades how long the 'Mech is exposed near the line against how much safety margin it keeps against a lock.

options.title: The Bold Dash
advantages: Cross the line fast in a single move timed to one wide gap, cutting down the number of passes the 'Mech has to survive near the posts
Less total time near the picket means fewer chances for a changed rhythm or a lucky sweep to find the unit
disadvantages: A fast move means moving during part of a pass, and speed near the line builds up detection risk the stealth has to absorb
If the dash mistimes the gap, the 'Mech is moving fast and bright across the open ice just as the sweep comes on
options.consequence: If the gap holds, the 'Mech is across in one stroke with little exposure. If the rhythm has changed, the dash crosses right into a pass and the line gets the lock that ends the mission.

costs.resource: The whole crossing is staked on one timed dash through a single gap.
costs.risk: A mistimed dash moves the 'Mech across open ice as the sweep comes on, drawing a lock.

options.title: The Patient Creep
advantages: Cross over many cycles, moving only in confirmed gaps and holding still for every pass, keeping the stealth margin at its widest
Patience lets the 'Mech re-read a changed rhythm as it goes, adapting to the real rhythm rather than the briefed one
disadvantages: A long crossing keeps the 'Mech near the line for far longer, with more total cycles in which something can go wrong
Time spent creeping is time off the clock the coming offensive set for the beacon to be in place
options.consequence: The creep keeps the best margin against detection at the cost of time. The 'Mech is least likely to be caught moving, but the long exposure and slow pace risk the beacon being late for the offensive.

costs.resource: The time of a slow, many-cycle crossing, spent against the offensive's clock.
costs.risk: A long creep near the line multiplies the cycles in which a changed rhythm or a chance lock can catch the 'Mech.

options.title: Cross at the Seam
advantages: Cross where the coverage of two posts overlaps the thinnest, exploiting the layout of the line rather than just the timing of the sweep
A seam crossing needs less detection margin, giving the stealth armor the easiest stretch of the whole line
disadvantages: The seam is a known weak point the picket may watch more closely or sweep more often precisely because it is thin
Reaching the seam may mean a longer approach along the line, more exposure just to get to the one good crossing
options.consequence: If the seam is as thin as briefed, the 'Mech slips through where the line is weakest. If the picket has reinforced its own known gap, the seam is a trap and the approach to it wasted the 'Mech's concealment.

costs.resource: The approach along the line to reach the thinnest seam.
costs.risk: A seam the picket has reinforced turns the line's known weak point into its best-watched one.

entries.event: The stealth 'Mech reaches the sensor-picket line and begins reading the sweep rhythm for a gap to cross.
The 'Mech crosses the line into the enemy rear, timing its movement to the sweep's gaps.
The 'Mech reaches the planting point deep in the rear and begins planting the dormant beacon.
The beacon is planted and the 'Mech turns back for the line, facing the sweep again from the inside.
The 'Mech recrosses the picket line. If it was never locked onto, it withdraws cleanly and the beacon sits silent in the enemy's unwatched rear.

reactionTimeline.hardDeadline: The 'Mech must plant the beacon and recross the picket line without ever being locked onto, before the crossing window closes at T+2:40. At that point the sweep rhythm the defector mapped is due to rotate, and the line's rhythm, the whole basis of the crossing, can no longer be trusted. A 'Mech still inside when the rhythm changes is timing to a rhythm that no longer exists, and a single lock turns a silent infiltration into a hunt across open ice.

opforSketch.composition: A Clan sensor-picket screen, all 'Mechs in any fight it forces. The line itself is detection posts and a sweeping sensor watch (this is a sensor problem, not a force to be fought). If the 'Mech is located, the rear area's reaction is a fast light 'Mech Star (20-40 tons, Regular to Veteran) that hunts the detected intruder across the ice. No vehicles are central, because the mission is evading a sensor line, and the only combat is a hunt the 'Mech is built to avoid. The beacon and the planting point are inert.
opforSketch.behavior: The picket sweeps on its rhythm and reports contacts rather than chasing them. It does not pursue a contact it cannot hold a lock on, but a sustained lock releases the rear area's reaction Star to hunt. Once loosed, the reaction force works the open ice methodically to locate and corner the intruder, knowing a stealth 'Mech on open ground has nowhere to hide once it is locked on. The line's strength is patience and pattern; its weakness is the gap in its own rhythm.

forks.name: OPERATION OPEN EYES
forks.trigger: The beacon was planted and the 'Mech withdrew without ever being locked onto, the line none the wiser.
forks.consequence: The coming offensive has a navigation fix and eyes in the enemy's unwatched rear, and {TARGET_FACTION} stages its forces behind a line it believes secure. The next operation is the offensive itself, its lead units crossing the picket where this 'Mech proved it could be crossed and striking a rear area that never saw them coming.

forks.name: OPERATION GHOST HUNT
forks.trigger: The 'Mech was located at the line or in the rear. The beacon is found or the crossing is blown.
forks.consequence: The picket knows something crossed, and the rear area sweeps for the beacon while a reaction Star hunts the 'Mech. The next operation is a desperate run to get the irreplaceable stealth 'Mech back across the line and off {WORLD} ahead of an alerted occupation rear. The surprise is spent and the offensive's eyes are blinded before it began.

storyElementSeed: A pilot holds a stealthed 'Mech dead still on open ice, every system turned down to its faintest setting. On the threat display, a sweep indicator crawls past. The pilot counts the seconds until the rhythm opens a gap wide enough for one more silent stride into the enemy's rear.

merc.objectives.primary: Walk the stealth 'Mech through the picket line, plant the beacon deep in their rear, and bring it home without ever getting a hard enough sensor hit for them to lock on. This is not a fight and it cannot become one. One solid lock on a single 'Mech behind the line and the contract, the beacon, and the 'Mech are all gone together.

is-steiner.objectives.primary: Slip the stealth 'Mech through the sensor line undetected, plant the beacon at the marked point, and withdraw without ever being locked onto. The 'Mech is irreplaceable and the surprise even more so. We are buying the offensive its eyes, and the price of being seen is the eyes, the 'Mech, and the whole advantage all at once.

PICKET_DEPTH_KM.unit: km of picket depth to the emplacement point

SWEEP_GAP_SEC.unit: seconds of gap between sweep passes

inspiration: A force is sent to both scout an enemy's assembling offensive and disrupt it before it can launch, where pushing deep enough to learn the enemy's plan is the same as pushing deep enough to be drawn into the battle the recon was meant to avoid, so the depth that buys intelligence is the depth that costs survival.
skeleton: a star must run a reconnaissance-in-force that doubles as a spoiling attack against an enemy's assembling counter-offensive, where the depth needed to map the assembly is the depth at which the recon becomes a battle it cannot win, so the crux is a single sliding decision of how far to push as scouting and wrecking pull against each other on one gauge
title: OPERATION FAR ENOUGH
situation: The Inner Sphere remnant facing {EMPLOYER} on {WORLD} is massing for an attack. {EMPLOYER} sends one Star to find out where the attack will fall and to damage the enemy before it can begin. The remnant has stopped retreating. {NPC:intel-source} is a Watch element reading the enemy's rear, and it sees the signs of a counter-offensive assembling in the {DISTRICT} valleys. Fuel is moving forward, formations are massing together, and a force is building up to attack. The Galaxy commander wants two things from your Star, and both come from the same advance carried to different depths. The first is information. How strong is the assembly, where is it aimed, and when will it be ready. This is what lets the touman meet the attack rather than be surprised by it. The second is disruption. A spoiling attack into the assembly destroys its fuel, scatters its forming units, and sets its schedule back before it can launch. One Star, sent forward, to both scout and disrupt. The catch is depth. The assembly's strength and direction can only be read from inside it, and the fuel and forming units worth destroying sit at its center. So the deeper the Star pushes, the more it learns and the more it can destroy. But depth is also danger. A Star deep inside a massing enemy is a Star the enemy can surround. The same advance that maps the assembly can turn a reconnaissance into a battle against a force gathering specifically to fight. This intelligence is {INTEL_AGE_DAYS} days old, and a build-up changes fast. The valley system is a branching network feeding into the assembly area. The valley floors are fast going, but ridges the enemy watches overlook them. Every kilometer deeper is a kilometer further from the open ground a Star needs to break off the fight, and a kilometer further into ground the enemy knows. The whole mission is one question asked over and over: how far is far enough? Far enough to learn, far enough to hurt, but not so far that the reconnaissance becomes a last stand. Recommended force: {FORCE_SIZE} combined arms, fast and able to fight its way back out. Push into the assembly to read it and wreck it. Judge at each ridge whether the next one is worth what it will cost to reach, because the deeper you push, the more you gain and the more likely you are to lose the Star.

objectives.primary: Determine the assembling counter-offensive's strength, direction, and timing, AND disrupt it by destroying its forward fuel and scattering its forming units. Push deep enough to do both, but not so deep that the Star cannot break off the fight and withdraw.
objectives.secondary: Capture or kill the assembly's command element, the headquarters or senior command group holding the build-up together. This sets the schedule back further than any amount of burned fuel.
objectives.bonus: Bring out a forming unit's 'Mech as isorla. A captured 'Mech from the broken assembly is both proof of the disruption done and materiel for the touman.

complications.name: Depth Is Both the Prize and the Trap
complications.text: The assembly can only be read from inside it and only be hurt at its center. So every kilometer deeper buys more information and more disruption. Those same kilometers carry the Star further into a massing enemy and further from the open ground it needs to escape. Pushing deeper raises both the payoff and the danger at the same time.
complications.mechanicalEffect: Both the intelligence gathered and the disruption achieved scale with how deep the Star pushes into the assembly area. So does the difficulty of breaking off the fight and the strength of the force that can close in behind it. No depth maximizes the gains without also maximizing the risk. The commander turns one dial for both.

complications.name: The Enemy Is Gathering to Fight
complications.text: This is not a sleeping garrison. It is a force massing specifically to attack. The deeper the Star goes, the more of that gathering strength is within reach to turn on it. A reconnaissance that pushes into the center of a build-up is pushing into the thickest concentration of exactly the enemy it is trying to avoid fighting.
complications.mechanicalEffect: Enemy density rises the deeper the Star goes into the assembly area. The forming units that would be the Star's targets are also the force that closes in on it. Pushing deep to wreck the center of the assembly means doing so amid the greatest concentration of the enemy, with the worst odds of a clean withdrawal.

complications.name: The Closing Ring
complications.text: An enemy that detects a Star in its rear closes off the valleys behind it. It puts troops on the ridges and blocks the valley floors to trap the intruder it has found. The deeper the Star is when this trap starts to close, the longer and harder its road back out.
complications.mechanicalEffect: Once the Star is detected, the enemy moves to close the valley routes behind it (see the reaction timeline). The withdrawal must beat the closing trap. A Star that pushed deep and lingered finds the valley floors blocked and the ridges held on its way back, fighting through ground it passed freely on the way in.

complications.name: The Picture Is Days Old
complications.text: The Watch's read of the assembly is days old, and a build-up is the most fast-changing thing on a front. The direction may have shifted, and the concentration may be further along or in a different place than the report says. The Star may push to where the center should be and find the assembly has moved, grown, or aimed somewhere new.
complications.mechanicalEffect: If the dice call for it at depth, the assembly's layout differs from the briefed picture. The fuel or the command element may be deeper, elsewhere, or better protected than expected. The Star must push further or change direction to achieve its objectives. That extends the advance and the risk past what the plan assumed.

decisionPoints.name: How Far Is Far Enough
decisionPoints.context: The valleys run deeper into the assembly, and every ridge offers more to learn and more to wreck at more risk. You have three ways to play this. You can push all the way to the center for the fullest picture and the hardest blow. You can take a measured advance and break off cleanly with a partial result. Or you can hit the nearest worthwhile target and run before the trap can close. Each choice trades how much the Star achieves against how surely it gets back out.

options.title: Push to the Heart
advantages: Push to the center of the assembly for the complete picture (strength, direction, timing) and the chance to wreck its central fuel and command
The deepest strike sets the counter-offensive back the furthest and gives the touman the fullest warning, the best possible result
disadvantages: The center of the assembly is the thickest enemy and the furthest point from a clean break. The trap closes behind a deep Star the hardest.
A Star committed to the center may not get back out. The reconnaissance becomes the last stand the mission was meant to avoid.
options.consequence: If the Star reaches the center and breaks out, it delivers everything and cripples the offensive. If the trap closes first, it is trapped deep in a gathering enemy with the longest, worst road home.

costs.resource: The Star is committed to the deepest advance and the longest withdrawal.
costs.risk: A Star at the center when the trap closes is trapped amid the thickest enemy with the worst odds of getting out.

options.title: A Measured Bite
advantages: Push deep enough to read the assembly's shape and wreck a worthwhile part of it, then break off the fight while the way out is still open
Balances a real result against a real chance of withdrawal, delivering information and disruption while keeping the Star intact
disadvantages: A measured depth leaves the center of the assembly unread and unhurt. The picture is good but not complete, the blow real but not crippling.
Judging the moment to break off is unforgiving. Push one ridge too far and the measured plan becomes the deep one anyway.
options.consequence: You get a solid picture and a solid blow and bring the Star home. The offensive is set back but not broken, and the touman is warned but not handed the whole plan. This is the disciplined middle option that wins less and keeps the Star.

costs.resource: The center of the assembly is left unread and unhurt to keep the way out open.
costs.risk: Pushing one ridge too deep slides into the trapped-deep outcome it was meant to avoid.

options.title: Strike Near and Run
advantages: Hit the nearest worthwhile target (a forward fuel point or a screening unit) and withdraw before the enemy can detect the Star and close the trap
The surest withdrawal and the least risk to the Star. Whatever is learned and wrecked comes cheap and clean.
disadvantages: A shallow strike reads little of the assembly's real strength or direction and wrecks only its edge. The warning is thin and the disruption minor.
An offensive damaged only at its forward edge launches close to on time. The spoiling attack barely spoils anything.
options.consequence: You keep the Star safe and learn and break little. The touman gets a hint, not a picture, and the counter-offensive comes nearly as planned. This is the cautious choice that preserves the force and gives up the result.

costs.resource: The deep picture and the crippling blow are both given up for a clean, shallow strike.
costs.risk: A spoiling attack that barely spoils anything lets the counter-offensive launch nearly on schedule.

entries.event: The Star crosses into the valley system and begins advancing toward the assembly area.
The Star reaches the assembly's outer formations, reading their strength and screening units and striking forward targets of opportunity.
The enemy detects a Star in its rear and begins moving to hold the ridges and close the valley floors behind it.
The trap tightens. The Star's depth at this moment decides how hard the road back out has become.
The valleys behind the Star are closing. A Star not withdrawing by now fights the gathering enemy for its way home.

reactionTimeline.hardDeadline: The Star must break off the fight and withdraw before the assembly closes the valley routes behind it at T+5:30. After that the reconnaissance has become the battle it was sent to prevent. A single Star fights a massing counter-offensive for its survival, the intelligence undelivered and the spoiling attack turned into a last stand. How deep the Star pushed is exactly how much of that road it now has to fight through.

opforSketch.composition: An Inner Sphere remnant counter-offensive assembling, combined arms. The assembly is a massing force: medium and heavy 'Mechs (Regular to Veteran) forming up, with combat vehicles and forward fuel and supply (the vehicle element of the force sits among the forming units and the targets worth wrecking). A command group holds it together. Screening units hold the valley ridges. Density and strength rise toward the assembly's center. The forming units are both the Star's targets and the force that closes in on it.
opforSketch.behavior: The assembly is gathering to attack, not defending, but it reacts hard to a Star in its rear, holding the ridges and closing the valley floors to trap the intruder. Forward units skirmish and delay; the deeper formations mass together to close the trap. The enemy fights to protect its build-up and to destroy the Star that has seen it, pressing hardest as the Star tries to withdraw. Screening units break off if reduced to roughly a third of their strength, but the closing trap re-forms behind them.

forks.name: OPERATION BRUISED FIST
forks.trigger: The Star read the assembly and disrupted it, then broke off the fight and withdrew with its intelligence intact.
forks.consequence: The counter-offensive is mapped and set back, and the touman knows where and when the attack will fall and meets it prepared. The next operation is the prepared defense or the pre-emptive strike the Star's intelligence made possible. The enemy's offensive is broken before it began because one Star pushed far enough.

forks.name: OPERATION CAUGHT DEEP
forks.trigger: The Star pushed too far or lingered too long and the trap closed. It is trapped in the valleys fighting the gathering enemy.
forks.consequence: The reconnaissance became the battle it was meant to prevent, with the intelligence undelivered. The next operation is a fighting breakout of the surviving Star out of the closing valleys. The counter-offensive is undisrupted and now alert, and it launches against a touman that lost both its warning and a Star.

storyElementSeed: A Star commander halts a lance at the mouth of yet another valley branch. The enemy grows thicker on the slopes ahead. The commander weighs the next ridge against the long road already travelled, deciding one more time whether what waits up there is worth how far it is back to open ground.

clan-wolf.objectives.primary: Read the gathering enemy and break what you can of it, then bring the Star home. Push as far as the knowledge and the kill are worth, but a Wolf does not throw itself into a closing trap for a deeper bite. Judge each ridge, and know when far enough is far enough.

VALLEY_DEPTH_KM.unit: km of valley depth to the assembly heart

RING_CLOSE_HR.unit: hours before the valley routes close

inspiration: A surrounded force must conduct a fighting evacuation off a beach under continuous pressure, where the perimeter is not held to win but only to keep the embarkation point alive long enough to lift everyone out, and the line shrinks deliberately as the numbers behind it fall.
skeleton: an escort element must walk a column of civilians and walking-wounded out of a falling district to a single working lift point while the column itself is the line that must be screened on the move, where stopping to fight loses the people and a perimeter only ever shrinks toward the loading ramps as the last of them board
title: OPERATION LAST OMNIBUS
situation: {TARGET_FACTION} has broken into the {DISTRICT} sprawl on {WORLD}. {EMPLOYER} is paid to get the people out, not to hold the ground. The district is already lost. Planetary command wrote it off and pulled its line back to the river. That left tens of thousands of people trapped on the wrong side: factory workers, families, and the walking wounded of a battalion that was beaten here. The occupier's spearhead is grinding south from the north edge of the district. There is one way out. A freight terminal sits at the south edge, and {EMPLOYER}'s DropShips can land there in waves, lifting a few thousand people at a time. To reach it, the crowd walks south on foot down one broad avenue, the old bus route. Your contract is that column of people. Walk them to the terminal and keep them alive on the way. {NPC:intel-source}, an evacuation coordinator at the terminal, has the numbers. Each DropShip wave carries only a few thousand. The crowd moves at the pace of its slowest members. The occupier's lead units are pushing into the north of the district right now. The report on how fast they are advancing is {INTEL_AGE_DAYS} hours old, and a spearhead can speed up, so treat that pace as a floor. This is not a wall you hold. What you defend is moving: a column of frightened people, kilometers long, shuffling south. Your escort is a screen that has to move with the crowd. Stay between the crowd and the enemy pressing in from the north and the flanks. You cannot stop and make a stand, because a stand halts the column, and a halted column gets caught. The line you hold is not a circle around a position. It is the length of the avenue. It shrinks toward the loading ramps only as the DropShips carry the front away and the rear catches up. The side streets are the hard part. The avenue runs straight to the terminal, but every side street feeding into it is an opening the enemy can push through to cut the column in two. Each block the crowd advances opens new side streets to screen and leaves old ones behind. Recommended force: {FORCE_SIZE} combined arms. Use vehicles to herd the crowd and block side streets, and 'Mechs to anchor the moving screen. Keep the column walking, screen the side streets as you pass them, and load the people onto the DropShips wave by wave. The job is not to beat the enemy. It is to outlast him until the whole crowd has passed. The last DropShip south carries whoever is still on the avenue when the spearhead reaches the ramps.

objectives.primary: Escort the column of civilians and walking wounded down the avenue to the freight terminal and load as many as possible onto the DropShips before the occupier's spearhead reaches the loading ramps.
objectives.secondary: Keep the column together in one body. If a thrust through a side street cuts the crowd in two, the severed half is lost. Keeping the column whole saves more people than loading fast does.
objectives.bonus: Get the beaten battalion's walking wounded and their officers out among the civilians. These are trained survivors of the lost line. Recovering them gives {EMPLOYER} the core to rebuild a unit, not just refugees saved.

complications.name: The Line That Walks
complications.text: There is no perimeter to dig into. What you defend is a moving column of people. The screen has to move with it, always between the crowd and the enemy, never still. If you stop to make a stand, the column stops too, and a stopped column gets overrun. You win only by keeping pace with the crowd, not by holding ground.
complications.mechanicalEffect: The screen force must stay within escort range of the column each turn. The column advances toward the terminal at a fixed walking pace. If you halt the screen to make a stand, the column stops advancing. A column that stops falls behind its loading schedule and is caught by the spearhead. The ground you can defend is the column's own length, not a fixed line.

complications.name: The Open Side Streets
complications.text: The avenue itself is open, easy going. But every side street feeding into it is a way in the enemy can use to cut the column in two. As the crowd advances, it passes new side streets to screen and leaves old ones behind. There are always more side streets than the screen can block, so you are always choosing which ones to hold.
complications.mechanicalEffect: The side-street junctions along the avenue are enemy entry points, and the enemy probes them to split the column. The screen cannot cover every junction at once, so you must choose which ones to block as the column passes them. An unscreened junction at the column's position lets a thrust cut the crowd and strand the portion behind the cut.

complications.name: The DropShips Set the Pace
complications.text: Each DropShip takes only so many people per wave and turns around on a fixed cycle. The crowd reaches the ramps faster than the DropShips can carry it away. So people pile up at the terminal, and the screen has to hold the terminal itself while the DropShips clear the backlog. The rear of the column is still walking while the front waits its turn to board.
