complications.mechanicalEffect: The DropShips carry a fixed number per wave on a fixed turnaround time. The crowd backs up at the terminal, so it must be screened there as well as along the avenue. Success is the number who board before the hard deadline. Every wave lost to delay or to a threatened ramp means people left behind.

complications.name: The Spearhead Quickens
complications.text: The occupier's lead units are pushing in from the north, and a spearhead that senses a withdrawal pushes harder. The advance rate in the briefing is hours old. If the enemy works out that this is an evacuation, it will drive hard to reach the ramps before the DropShips empty the avenue.
complications.mechanicalEffect: If the dice call for it during the operation, the spearhead speeds up and reaches the terminal sooner. You then face a choice. Move the column faster, and risk leaving the slowest behind. Or hold the spearhead harder at the rear, and risk pinning the moving screen in place. Either way, the loading clock tightens.

decisionPoints.name: Screening the Ribbon
decisionPoints.context: The column walks south, side-street junctions keep coming up along the avenue, and the DropShips can only load so fast. You have three ways to deploy the screen. Weight it to the rear against the spearhead pushing from behind. Weight it to the flanks against the side-street thrusts. Or spread it thin everywhere and use speed to outpace the enemy. Each choice protects one part of the column and leaves another part exposed.

options.title: Weight the Rear Guard
advantages: Massing the screen at the column's tail holds the spearhead off the slowest people and the last to board
A strong rear stops the spearhead from rolling up the column from behind, which is where the main enemy weight is coming from
disadvantages: Weighting the rear thins the flanks, leaving side streets open for a thrust to cut the column in the middle
Holding the rear hard can pin those units in a stand while the column's front pulls away toward the ramps
options.consequence: You protect the tail and the slowest, but the flanks pay for it. If a side-street thrust comes while the rear is committed, the column is cut and the severed part is stranded between the spearhead and the gap.

costs.resource: The flanks are thinned to hold the pressing rear.
costs.risk: A side-street thrust cuts the column while the rear guard is pinned against the spearhead.

options.title: Weight the Flanks
advantages: Spreading the screen to block side streets as the column passes them keeps the column whole and uncut down the avenue
A whole column loses no one to a thrust through a gap, and it boards faster than a severed crowd can regroup
disadvantages: Weighting the flanks weakens the rear guard, letting the spearhead press closer onto the column's tail
Covering every side street spreads the force thin everywhere, with little strength to stop a determined push at any one point
options.consequence: You keep the column whole, but the rear pays for it. If the spearhead drives hard while the screen is spread to the flanks, it crowds the tail onto the ramps faster than the DropShips can take them.

costs.resource: The rear guard is weakened to block the avenue's openings.
costs.risk: The spearhead presses the column's tail onto a terminal the DropShips cannot clear fast enough.

options.title: Thin Screen, Best Speed
advantages: A light screen all around lets you drive the column south at its fastest pace and beat the spearhead to the ramps
Speed shortens the whole danger period: fewer side streets passed under threat, fewer DropShip waves needed, less time on the avenue
disadvantages: A thin screen cannot stop anything for long. A serious thrust at the rear or a flank punches through and the column takes losses.
Driving the crowd faster than its slowest can go leaves the wounded and the weak behind to keep up the pace
options.consequence: You race the enemy to the terminal and save the most who can keep up. The price is everyone who cannot make the pace, plus anyone lost where the thin screen fails to hold.

costs.resource: The slowest of the column are left behind to keep up the pace.
costs.risk: A thin screen punched through anywhere costs the column lives for the speed it bought.

entries.event: The column sets off down the avenue toward the terminal. The screen forms around it and the first DropShip lands at the ramps.
The occupier's spearhead pushes into the north of the district and begins probing the side streets toward the avenue.
The column's front reaches the terminal and begins boarding. The crowd backs up at the ramps as the DropShips work through the waves.
The spearhead reaches the avenue's middle blocks and presses the column's rear and flanks hard. The side-street junctions are now contested.
The spearhead nears the terminal. Anyone not aboard or screened at the ramps by now is within the enemy's reach.

reactionTimeline.hardDeadline: Load as much of the column as you can and get the DropShips away before the spearhead reaches the loading ramps at T+3:30. After that the terminal is under direct attack. The last DropShip lifts with whoever made it aboard, and the avenue behind belongs to the enemy. The people still on it are lost, and the screen that stayed to cover them lifts out last, if it lifts out at all.

opforSketch.composition: An occupier breakthrough spearhead, combined arms. The lead is a fast medium 'Mech force (40-65 tons, Regular to Veteran) driving down the district, supported by mechanized infantry and combat vehicles probing the side streets (the vehicle element of the force). Behind it presses the weight of a heavier follow-on force. The crowd and the DropShips are non-combatants and the protected objective. The spearhead pushes from the north and through the flank openings, speeding up if it reads the evacuation for what it is.
opforSketch.behavior: The spearhead drives to cut and catch the column, not to hold ground. It probes the side streets to split the crowd and presses the rear to pin the screen and overrun the slow. It exploits any gap in the moving screen aggressively and speeds up toward the terminal if it senses the DropShips emptying the avenue. It does not break off for casualties while the column is in reach; the prize is the people, and it presses until the last DropShip is gone.

forks.name: OPERATION SOUTH RAMP
forks.trigger: The bulk of the column was loaded and lifted out before the spearhead reached the ramps.
forks.consequence: The people of the district are out. {TARGET_FACTION} takes empty streets, denied the hostages and the labor it meant to seize. The next operation rebuilds from the recovered survivors and the saved officers. {EMPLOYER} becomes known as the unit that got the column out, and that reputation travels the front ahead of it.

forks.name: OPERATION STRANDED AVENUE
forks.trigger: The column was cut and a large part stranded, or the spearhead reached the ramps before the DropShips cleared the crowd.
forks.consequence: Part of the column is lost on the avenue, and the screen is pinned at a contested terminal. The next operation is a fighting extraction of the screen force itself. You must get the survivors aboard the last DropShip and off the ramps before the spearhead overruns the terminal.

storyElementSeed: A 'Mech walks backward down a broad avenue at the pace of a shuffling crowd. Its gun is trained up a side street at movement it cannot fire on yet, because the people are in the way. A vehicle commander waves the column past the junction one block at a time and counts heads against the next DropShip.

is-davion.objectives.primary: Walk the people down that avenue to the terminal and load as many onto the DropShips as the waves will carry before the spearhead reaches the ramps. The ground is already lost. The job is the column, not the district. Keep the screen moving with the crowd and hold the side streets as you pass them.

is-steiner.objectives.primary: Escort the column to the terminal and load as many as possible before the enemy takes the ramps. Every person aboard is one kept off the occupier's labor rolls. The district is written off. The people on that avenue are the asset, and the number loaded is the only number that matters.

AVENUE_LENGTH_KM.unit: km of avenue to the terminus

inspiration: A garrison defends an intact, irreplaceable installation it is forbidden to wreck even to deny the enemy, so the easy soldier's answer — rig it and blow it rather than lose it — is taken off the table, and the defenders must hold the thing whole through an assault meant to take it whole.
skeleton: a garrison must hold an intact recovered-tech facility through a deliberate assault under a standing order never to demolish it even in extremity, where the soldier's reflex to deny-by-destruction is forbidden because a relief means to inherit it working, so the crux is holding the prize whole rather than choosing when to break it
title: OPERATION KEEP THE LIGHTS
situation: {EMPLOYER} holds something the whole front wants intact. The order is to keep it whole or die trying, never to destroy it. On the edge of the {DISTRICT} works on {WORLD} stands a recovered Star League fabrication plant. The occupiers spent years restoring this lostech machine shop before {EMPLOYER}'s offensive took it back. It is the only facility on this front that can cut the precision parts a touman's recovered 'Mechs need. {EMPLOYER} means to keep it, and a relief column is already on the road to make the hold permanent. But {TARGET_FACTION} wants it back and is coming with a deliberate assault to retake the plant before the relief arrives. The hard part is the standing order: hold the plant intact. Do not rig it with charges. Do not wreck it. Do not deny it to the enemy by destroying it, even as a last resort. The relief means to inherit a working plant, so a garrison that blows up what it cannot hold has destroyed the very prize the whole campaign is being fought for. {NPC:intel-source}, a planning officer with the relief, has the timetable. The relief is days away. The assault is hours away. So you must hold the plant whole through the attack until the column arrives. The one move a soldier would normally make here, wrecking a position you cannot keep so the enemy gets nothing, is the one move forbidden. The terrain makes it harder. The plant is a sprawling works of fabrication halls, gantry yards, and a hardened core. Around it sits an industrial district of mixed buildings and rail lines that lets an attacker close to within meters of the wire under cover. You have to fight forward of the halls to keep the battle out of them, because fighting inside the plant wrecks the machines whether you mean to or not. Recommended force: {FORCE_SIZE} combined arms. Use vehicles for the district approaches and 'Mechs to anchor the works' perimeter. Hold the plant whole through the assault until the relief arrives. Fight forward to keep the wreckage out of the halls. And refuse the easy option of destroying it, which would turn a hard hold into a hollow victory. You win only by keeping the plant running, and you lose the moment it is wrecked, whether by the enemy or by your own hand.

objectives.primary: Hold the recovered fabrication plant intact and running through {TARGET_FACTION}'s assault until the relief column arrives. Keep the fighting forward of the fabrication halls so the prize comes through the battle whole.
objectives.secondary: Above all, keep the plant's hardened core and its irreplaceable machine tools undamaged. Even if the outer halls are contested, the core is what the whole front is fighting for, and it must not be touched.
objectives.bonus: Hold the plant's full perimeter and give up none of the works to the enemy. A defense that yields no ground keeps every hall producing and hands the relief a plant that never stopped running.

complications.name: Do Not Blow It
complications.text: When a soldier cannot hold a position, the usual last answer is to deny it: rig it, wreck it, leave the enemy rubble. That answer is forbidden here. The relief means to inherit a working plant, so you hold the plant whole or lose it whole, with no option to destroy it. The urge to wreck it grows with every meter lost, and you must refuse it right to the end.
complications.mechanicalEffect: You may not demolish the plant or deny it by scorched earth. Destroying it to deny it fails the mission entirely, because the relief then inherits nothing. You must hold the facility intact. There is no fallback of wrecking it. That removes the usual last-ditch option and forces you to keep the plant whole even when things are desperate.

complications.name: Keep the Fight Out of the Halls
complications.text: A battle inside the fabrication halls wrecks the machines whether anyone means to or not. Stray fire, a 'Mech's bulk in tight quarters, a fallen unit across a tool line, any of it does the damage. So fight forward of the works, out in the district approaches. Letting the assault into the halls destroys the prize as surely as a demolition charge would.
complications.mechanicalEffect: Combat inside the fabrication halls damages the plant's machinery and slides the intact objective toward FAILURE, no matter who wins the exchange. You must hold the assault forward of the works, in the surrounding district. A defense that collapses back into the halls saves the perimeter but loses the very thing it is defending.

complications.name: The Covered Approaches
complications.text: An industrial district of mixed buildings and rail rings the plant and lets an attacker close to within meters of the wire under cover. There is no clean field of fire around the works. The enemy can mass against any face from concealment, and you cannot see the assault form until it is already at close range.
complications.mechanicalEffect: The surrounding district gives the attacker covered approaches to short range on every face of the plant. You have limited long-range observation and fields of fire. The assault can mass against a chosen face from concealment, so you must read the main effort from little warning and shift your forward defense to meet it.

complications.name: The Relief Runs Its Own Clock
complications.text: The relief is days out, traveling its own road, and you do not control when it arrives. A column can be slowed, diverted, or delayed. You hold until it comes, however much longer than promised that turns out to be. You do not control when the hold ends. It ends only when the relief arrives, whenever that is.
complications.mechanicalEffect: On a die roll during the defense, the relief column is delayed and the hold must extend past the briefed arrival window. You cannot end the operation on your own terms. You hold until relieved, and a slipped relief schedule means more waves to absorb with the plant kept intact throughout.

decisionPoints.name: Where the Line Holds
decisionPoints.context: The assault is forming in the district and the plant has to come through it whole. You have three ways to set the defense. Hold a wide forward line out in the district to keep the fight far from the halls. Pull tight to the works' wire and give up district ground for a concentrated defense. Or hold a mobile forward screen that gives ground but never lets the fight settle into the halls. The wider your line, the farther the fight stays from the machines, but the harder it is to actually hold.

options.title: Hold Forward in the District
advantages: A wide line out in the surrounding district keeps the assault and its fire well clear of the fabrication halls
The farther forward the fight stays, the safer the plant. A battle won at the district's edge never touches the machines.
disadvantages: A wide forward line in covered ground is thin everywhere and hard to hold against a concentrated assault coming from concealment
Forward positions can be cut off and overrun in the district's tangle, costing the garrison units before the main hold even begins
options.consequence: You keep the fight farthest from the plant, but the line is thin and exposed. If the assault masses and breaks the forward positions, you fall back toward the very halls you most need to keep the fight out of.

costs.resource: the garrison spread thin across a wide forward line in covered ground
costs.risk: A concentrated assault breaks the thin forward line and drives the fight back toward the halls

options.title: Tight to the Wire
advantages: Pulling in tight to the works' perimeter concentrates the garrison along its strongest and shortest line
A tight line is hard to break and easy to reinforce, holding the plant's edge against the heaviest push
disadvantages: A close perimeter means the fight is right at the wire, with fire falling near the halls and little margin to keep it out of them
Giving up the district hands the attacker covered ground right up to the works, from which to mass for the final push
options.consequence: You hold the perimeter at its strongest, but the fight is close to the halls. The plant's edge is secure, yet a single push that breaks the tight line is instantly among the machines.

costs.resource: the district given up and the fight drawn close to the halls
costs.risk: A breach of the tight perimeter puts the fight among the machines at once

options.title: Mobile Forward Screen
advantages: A mobile screen gives ground on purpose but never lets the assault settle, keeping the fight fluid and away from the halls
Trading district ground for time, and never getting pinned, lets a smaller force keep the battle out of the works longer than a static line could
disadvantages: A screen that gives ground gives it toward the plant, so each withdrawal brings the fight one step closer to the halls
Mobile defense in a dense district is hard to control, and a screen that gives up too much too fast is suddenly at the wire
options.consequence: You keep the fight moving and unpinned, but you steadily give ground. The screen buys time and space, yet every step back is toward the machines, and a screen that breaks has nowhere left to give.

costs.resource: district ground traded steadily backward toward the plant in exchange for time
costs.risk: A screen that gives ground too fast is driven back to the halls with no space left

entries.event: The assault's lead elements enter the industrial district and begin closing on the plant under cover. The garrison mans its forward positions.
The attacker probes the plant's faces from the district to find the garrison's positions and the best approach for its main effort.
The main assault commits against a chosen face, massing from covered ground to drive for the works.
The assault presses hardest. The garrison fights to keep the battle forward of the halls as the attacker tries to break into the works.
The assault makes its peak effort to crack the plant before the relief can arrive. The hold is at its most strained.

reactionTimeline.hardDeadline: Hold the plant intact and forward of the halls until the relief column arrives. The briefed window closes around T+4:30, later if the relief is delayed. Fail to hold and the plant is taken, or the fight is driven into the halls and the machines are wrecked. The one ending worse than losing the plant is destroying it by your own hand, which throws away the very prize the whole campaign is being fought to keep.

opforSketch.composition: A {TARGET_FACTION} deliberate assault force, combined arms. The main effort is a heavy 'Mech force (heavy and assault, 60-90 tons, Regular to Veteran) massing to crack the plant's perimeter, supported by mechanized elements and combat vehicles working the district's covered approaches (the vehicle element of the board). The attacker wants the plant intact too — it will not destroy the prize — so it presses to take the works whole rather than batter them down. It breaks contact on a face if reduced below roughly a third strength and shifts its main effort elsewhere.
opforSketch.behavior: The assault probes from the covered district to find the garrison's weakest face, then masses against it to break into the works. It fights to take the plant intact, avoiding the heavy fire that would wreck the prize, which forces it into a close assault rather than a stand-off bombardment. It presses to crack the plant before the relief can arrive, accepting losses to beat the clock, and treats a delayed relief as a chance to grind the garrison down through extended waves.

forks.name: OPERATION LIGHTS STILL ON
forks.trigger: The plant was held intact and forward of the halls until the relief column arrived.
forks.consequence: The relief arrives to find a working plant and a held perimeter. {EMPLOYER}'s front gains the one facility that keeps its recovered 'Mechs supplied. The next operation consolidates the secured works, and the precision parts the plant cuts begin reaching the line that fought to keep it whole.

forks.name: OPERATION DARK HALLS
forks.trigger: The plant was taken, the fight was driven into the halls and the machines wrecked, or the garrison was forced to destroy it.
forks.consequence: The prize is lost or ruined and the garrison is broken at the works. The next operation is a withdrawal of the survivors out of the industrial district before the assault consolidates its capture. The plant is back in {TARGET_FACTION}'s hands or wrecked beyond either side's use, and the campaign's reason for this front is gone with it.

storyElementSeed: A defender holds a position at a rail yard short of the fabrication halls. By order, the demolition charges stay crated and unrigged at their back. They listen to the assault mass in the buildings ahead, knowing the one thing they may not do is the one thing that would make holding simple.

merc.objectives.primary: Hold the plant whole until the relief shows up, and keep the shooting out of the halls. The contract pays for a working plant handed over, not a hole where one used to be. And no, you do not get to rig it and walk away. Blowing it up is the one sure way to lose the fee entirely.

is-steiner.objectives.primary: Hold the fabrication plant intact and producing until the relief arrives. Fight forward of the halls to keep the machinery whole. This asset is the campaign's whole purpose on this front. Destroying it to deny it to the enemy is not a fallback. It is exactly the loss we are here to prevent. Keep the lights on.

DISTRICT_DEPTH_KM.unit: km of industrial district around the plant

RELIEF_ETA_HR.unit: hours until the relief column arrives

inspiration: A relief force must break through to a surrounded body of its own people who are still fighting under a strict code that limits how they may engage, where the besiegers exploit that code to bleed the trapped force, and the rescue must reach them before the rules that keep them alive also use them up.
skeleton: a Clan relief star must cut through to a surrounded Cluster fighting under zellbrigen and break the siege before the besiegers' deliberate dueling-by-attrition wears the trapped warriors down, where the relief must decide whether to honor the same code that is slowly killing the besieged or break it to reach them in time
title: OPERATION UNBROKEN CIRCLE
situation: A Cluster of {EMPLOYER} is surrounded, fighting under the Clan honor code, and its enemy is using that same code to kill it slowly. In the {DISTRICT} highlands of {WORLD}, a Cluster of {EMPLOYER}'s touman was cut off during its advance. It now holds a hill, encircled by a rival {TARGET_FACTION} force that outnumbers it. The trapped Cluster fights under zellbrigen, the Clan code of single combat: one warrior to one challenge, no ganging up, no firing on a warrior already in a duel. Its enemy follows the same code openly. But the besiegers have the numbers, and they are spending them coldly. They send one fresh warrior after another to challenge a Cluster that cannot rest or refuse, dueling the defenders down one honorable kill at a time. It is a siege fought like a tournament, and it grinds the encircled Cluster smaller by the hour. {EMPLOYER} sends your star to break through and lift the siege before the Cluster is worn away. {NPC:intel-source} is in contact with the trapped commander and has the picture: the Cluster's strength is falling steadily, the besiegers hold the approaches, and one hard choice waits for you. Here is the choice. Come in by the code, challenging the ring one duel at a time, and you risk being worn down exactly as the Cluster is. Or break zellbrigen, hit the ring with massed firepower, and lift the siege fast, but at the cost of the honor both sides have kept. The report on the Cluster's strength is {INTEL_AGE_DAYS} hours old, and a worn-down Cluster collapses fast, so treat its strength as a ceiling. The terrain forces the issue. Ridgelines lead up to the hill, and the besiegers screen them with their dueling line. The ground between you and the ring is open, with no cover to mass behind unseen. Fight up the ridges by the code and you fight duel by duel. Break the code and you must cross that open ground in full view of a ring you have chosen to strike all at once. Recommended force: {FORCE_SIZE}, MECH_ONLY. Bring a star with the weight to break a ring and the judgment to know what breaking it will cost. Cut through to the Cluster and lift the siege before the tournament finishes it. Decide on the way in whether to honor the code that is killing them or break it to save them.

objectives.primary: Break through the besieging ring and lift the siege before the enemy's steady dueling wears the trapped Cluster below the strength it needs to survive. Reach the warriors while there is still a Cluster to relieve.
objectives.secondary: Preserve your own star's honor where you can. Lifting the siege within the code answers the besiegers for exploiting it and keeps your standing, but only if you can be both honorable and on time.
objectives.bonus: Defeat or capture the besieging commander who turned the code into a grinding machine. Beating the warrior who ordered this answers the dishonor of it directly.

complications.name: The Code That Kills
complications.text: The trapped Cluster fights by zellbrigen and is being killed by it. Fresh warriors challenge it in series until the numbers grind it down. The besiegers both honor the code and exploit it. You face the same trap. Come in by the code and risk being worn down the same way, or break it and lift the siege fast at the cost of the honor both sides have kept.
complications.mechanicalEffect: Your choice to honor or break zellbrigen governs your whole approach. Honoring it means fighting the ring in single combats: slower and costlier in time, but it keeps your honor and standing. Breaking it means massed fire on the ring: faster relief, but a loss of honor that carries consequences in the campaign's Clan politics beyond this battle.

complications.name: The Tournament Clock
complications.text: The siege is a tournament, and the trapped Cluster is losing it one duel at a time. Its strength falls by the hour as fresh besiegers wear it down. You are not racing a wall's collapse. You are racing steady attrition toward a known end: the hour the circle is too small to hold. That hour comes whether you honor the code or not.
complications.mechanicalEffect: The trapped Cluster's strength drops steadily through the operation as the besiegers duel it down, and you must arrive before it falls below a survival threshold. Honoring the code is slower and may not beat the clock. Breaking the code is faster but costs honor. Your choice weighs time, standing, and the survival of the besieged against each other.

complications.name: The Open Dueling Ground
complications.text: The besiegers screen the approaches to the hill with their dueling line across open ridges. There is no cover to mass behind unseen. Honor the code and you fight up the ridges duel by duel in full view. Break it and you must cross the same open ground in full view of a ring you have chosen to strike all at once, with nothing to hide the massing.
complications.mechanicalEffect: The highland approach is open ground overlooked by the besieging line, and there is no covered route to the hill. Honoring the code means serial duels on the ridges. Breaking it means a massed strike across the open under observation, with no surprise. Either way you fight in the open, and the terrain offers no way to dodge the besiegers' choice of fight.

complications.name: The Trapped Commander's Will
complications.text: The surrounded Cluster's commander fights by the code as a matter of honor. He may not welcome a relief that breaks it on his behalf, because a siege lifted by dishonor can shame the rescued as much as the rescuers. Your choice is not only tactical. It affects the standing of the very warriors you come to save, and those warriors have a will of their own.
complications.mechanicalEffect: On a die roll at link-up, the trapped commander's stance on the code shapes the outcome. A Cluster relieved by broken zellbrigen may regard the relief, and its own survival, as dishonored, which hurts the campaign-political result even on a tactical win. You must weigh how the rescued will take the manner of their rescue, not just whether they are rescued at all.

decisionPoints.name: By the Code or Through It
decisionPoints.context: The ring grinds the Cluster down and you have to reach it. You have three ways to try. Honor zellbrigen and fight up the ridges duel by duel. Break the code and strike the ring with massed weight to lift the siege fast. Or honor it until the clock forces your hand, and break it only at the last moment. Each choice weighs your honor against the speed the dying Cluster needs.

options.title: Honor the Code
advantages: Fighting up the ridges by zellbrigen answers the besiegers' challenges in single combat and keeps your honor and standing intact
A siege lifted within the code shames the besiegers for exploiting it and keeps the rescued Cluster's honor whole alongside your own
disadvantages: Serial duels up a screened ridge are slow, and the trapped Cluster is dying by the hour while you fight one foe at a time
You risk being worn down by the same tournament math that is killing the besieged, and arriving too weak or too late
options.consequence: You keep the honor but risk the clock. If the duels go fast enough, the siege is lifted with both Clusters' standing intact. If they do not, the Cluster falls while you are still fighting honorably up the ridge.

costs.resource: the relief's speed, spent on serial single combats up the ridge
costs.risk: The tournament math wears down both the relief and the Cluster while the duels run their course

options.title: Break the Ring
advantages: Striking the besieging line with the massed weight of the whole star at once shatters the ring and lifts the siege fast
Speed reaches the dying Cluster in time. A ring broken by concentrated force ends the tournament before it finishes the besieged.
disadvantages: Breaking zellbrigen costs the relief its honor and standing, with consequences in the campaign's Clan politics beyond this battle
The rescued Cluster may regard a siege lifted by dishonor as a shame, souring even a successful relief
options.consequence: You reach the Cluster fastest, but you pay with the code. The siege is lifted and the warriors saved, yet the way it was done stains you and may stain the rescued. It is a victory the Clans will remember.

costs.resource: the relief's honor and standing, given up to break the ring fast
costs.risk: A siege lifted by broken zellbrigen carries political and honor consequences past the battlefield

options.title: Honor Until the Clock Forces It
advantages: Fight by the code as long as the Cluster can hold, and break zellbrigen only at the last moment if the duels will not lift the siege in time
Keeps honor where possible and reaches for speed only when the alternative is the Cluster's destruction: the least dishonor for the most rescue
disadvantages: Judging the moment to break is unforgiving. Break too early and you threw the honor away for nothing. Break too late and the Cluster is already lost.
Starting by the code and switching mid-fight does both things half-well, neither fully honorable nor fully fast
options.consequence: You reach for both the honor and the speed and may end up with the worst of each. Timed right, the siege is lifted with honor mostly kept. Timed wrong, the code is broken too late to save a Cluster already worn away.

costs.resource: the relief's honor, staked on reading the exact moment the clock forces the break
costs.risk: A break timed wrong loses both the honor and the Cluster

entries.event: The relief star reaches the highland approaches. The besieging line screens the ridges, and the trapped Cluster signals its falling strength.
The relief commits to its approach, either challenging up the ridges by the code or massing to break the ring, and the besiegers respond in kind.
The relief is engaged with the besieging line. The trapped Cluster's strength keeps falling under the tournament's serial duels.
The Cluster nears the threshold below which it cannot hold. The relief's progress now decides whether it arrives in time.
The siege reaches its crisis. Either the ring is broken and the Cluster relieved, or the circle is worn too small to survive.

reactionTimeline.hardDeadline: Break the ring and reach the trapped Cluster before the besiegers' dueling wears it below survival, at roughly T+3:30. After that there is no Cluster left to relieve. The tournament has finished it, and a relief that arrives at an empty hill has run the ridges, kept or broken its honor, and saved no one. The besiegers' attrition sets the clock, and it does not pause for the code.

opforSketch.composition: A {TARGET_FACTION} besieging force, MECH_ONLY: a ring of medium and heavy 'Mechs (50-85 tons, Veteran to Elite) that outnumbers the trapped Cluster, fighting under zellbrigen openly but spending its numbers in series to grind the besieged down. No vehicles — this is a Clan siege fought as a tournament of single combats. The surrounded Cluster is {EMPLOYER}'s own, falling in strength. The besieging commander coordinates the serial challenges that turn the code into a machine.
opforSketch.behavior: The besiegers both honor zellbrigen and exploit it, issuing challenges in series — fresh warrior after fresh warrior — to wear the trapped Cluster down without ever ganging up or breaking the form. Against the relief they respond in kind, dueling its advance up the ridges if it honors the code and reacting to mass against it if it breaks the ring. They fight to finish the siege before the relief arrives, and a besieging line whose ring is broken by massed force may itself abandon the code in response. The besiegers break off if reduced below roughly a third strength with the Cluster not yet taken.

forks.name: OPERATION CIRCLE HELD
forks.trigger: The ring was broken and the trapped Cluster relieved before the tournament finished it.
forks.consequence: The siege is lifted and the Cluster saved. How it was done, by the code or through it, sets {EMPLOYER}'s standing on the front. The next operation reunites the relieved Cluster with the touman and turns on the broken besiegers. The highland sector is reopened by a relief that arrived in time.

forks.name: OPERATION EMPTY HILL
forks.trigger: The relief arrived too late, or was worn down short of the Cluster, and the besieged fell before the ring could be broken.
forks.consequence: The trapped Cluster is destroyed, and the relief is now itself in the open against an intact besieging force. The next operation is a fighting withdrawal of the relief star off the highland approaches, ahead of a victorious enemy. The circle is gone, the relief is spent, and only the honor of the attempt survives.

storyElementSeed: As another duel ends on the ridge, a star commander watches the besieging line wave a fresh warrior forward to challenge. The trapped Cluster's strength is read off lower than the last report. He weighs the code in one hand and the clock in the other, with the ridge still to climb.

clan-wolf.objectives.primary: Break the ring and lift the siege before the Cluster is worn away. Honor the code if the clock allows it, and break it without flinching if it does not. A Wolf does not let its own be dueled to death by a slower hand for the sake of a form. Reach them while there is still a circle left to save.

RIDGE_APPROACH_KM.unit: km of open ridge to the besieged hill

CLUSTER_FALL_HR.unit: hours until the Cluster falls below survival

inspiration: A rearguard holds a contracting perimeter around the last working embarkation point so the force behind it can lift out in relays, knowing the rearguard itself can only be among the last to leave and may not get off at all, where every loading cycle that succeeds shrinks the ground the rearguard has left to hold.
skeleton: a rearguard must hold a contracting perimeter around a single working DropPort so a defeated force can embark in lift relays, where each relay that lifts shrinks the perimeter the rearguard defends and the rearguard can only board last, so the crux is matching the shrink of the held ground to the rate of the lift while the enemy presses the closing ring
title: OPERATION LAST KEEL UP
situation: The campaign on {WORLD} is lost, and {EMPLOYER} is paid to make sure the army gets off the planet. A broken offensive is falling back on the one DropPort still in friendly hands: a coastal field at {DISTRICT}, ringed by a defensive perimeter. The DropShips lift the beaten force off-world in relays, as fast as they can land, load, and launch. Your contract is to be the rearguard. Hold the perimeter around the field so the DropShips can keep loading and launching, and keep holding it as it shrinks. You cannot hold this ground for good. You only have to hold it long enough for everyone to get off. {NPC:intel-source}, the embarkation control officer, lays out the hard math. Each relay lifts one DropShip's worth of troops, but the force still on the ground is roughly ten times what a single relay can carry. And the enemy that broke the offensive is driving toward the field to overrun it before the last DropShip lifts. The latest report on that enemy is {INTEL_AGE_DAYS} hours old, and an enemy that senses a withdrawal will push harder. This defense eats itself as it goes. Every relay carries away some of your own perimeter defenders along with the other troops, so you have fewer units to hold the line after each launch. To make up for it, you pull the perimeter inward toward the loading aprons as your strength flies away. Managing that shrink is the core task. Decide which sectors to give up and when. Fold the line inward without the pullback turning into a rout. Keep a defensible ring that is smaller after every relay but never so small the enemy reaches the aprons. And the rearguard boards last. The units holding the final perimeter lift on the last relay, if there is room and time, and there may not be. The coastal ground is the main terrain problem. The landward sides are open shore flats with clear approaches for the enemy. The sea is at your back, with no retreat that way. The perimeter is a shrinking arc pinned against the water, with the loading aprons at its center. Recommended force: {FORCE_SIZE} combined arms. Use vehicles to hold the open landward flats and 'Mechs to anchor the contracting arc. Match how fast you give up ground to how fast the DropShips lift. Fold the line in relay by relay without letting it break. Hold the last ring around the aprons long enough for the final DropShip to clear, knowing your own lift is the one that may not come.

objectives.primary: Hold the shrinking perimeter around the DropPort so the beaten force can lift off-world in relays. Fold the line inward after each relay to match your falling strength, and keep holding until the last load is away.
objectives.secondary: Get the rearguard itself onto the final relays. A rearguard that holds to the end and then lifts is a force preserved. A rearguard overrun on the aprons is the cost of holding too long.
objectives.bonus: Lift the offensive's heavy equipment and damaged 'Mechs along with the troops. Recovering the gear, not just the people, gives {EMPLOYER} an army to rebuild rather than survivors who must be re-equipped from scratch.

complications.name: The Hold That Eats Itself
complications.text: Every relay carries away ordinary troops and the units that were holding their slice of the perimeter. Your strength drops with each launch, so you must shrink the perimeter to match, folding it inward toward the aprons as your defenders fly out. This defense is not static. It loses strength on a schedule, and the line that held the wide ring early cannot hold that same ring once half its strength is gone.
complications.mechanicalEffect: Your force loses strength with each lift relay as units embark, so the perimeter must shrink by the same amount. You cannot hold the original wide perimeter with the reduced force. You must give ground on purpose and fold the line in, keeping the held area matched to your falling strength. Fail to contract and the line is too thin to hold. Contract too fast and you hand the enemy ground you could have denied it.

complications.name: The Rearguard Boards Last
complications.text: The units holding the final perimeter are the last to lift, on the last relay, and only if there is room and time. The rearguard gets no earlier seat. It holds until the force behind it is gone, then races to load itself while the enemy is already at the shrunken ring. The rearguard's survival is the last and least certain item on the manifest.
complications.mechanicalEffect: The rearguard cannot embark until the protected force is fully lifted. It boards on the final relays. If you keep the rearguard holding too long, or shrink the perimeter too slowly to keep it boardable, the rearguard may have no room or no time left on the last lift. In that case the secondary objective, saving the rearguard, fails even if the main force escaped.

complications.name: The Sea at the Back
complications.text: The field is pinned against the water. Open shore flats face the land, and the sea is behind. There is no retreat inland and no flank to fall back on. The perimeter is a shrinking arc with its back to the water and the loading aprons at its center. You cannot trade ground for time the usual way. You can only hold the arc or fold it tighter against the sea.
complications.mechanicalEffect: The perimeter is a coastal arc with no landward retreat. The sea anchors the rear, and there is no fallback position beyond the aprons. The open shore flats give the attacker clear approaches, and your only maneuver is to shrink the arc, because the only place left to withdraw to is onto the DropShips themselves.

complications.name: The Pursuer Smells It
complications.text: The enemy that broke the offensive is closing on the field. Once it reads the withdrawal, it will push hard to reach the aprons before the lift empties them. The approach in the briefing is already hours old. If the enemy drives hard, it crowds the shrinking perimeter faster than the relays can clear the ground behind it.
complications.mechanicalEffect: On a die roll during the operation, the pursuing force speeds up and reaches the perimeter sooner. You then face a choice. Lift faster, and accept a sloppier contraction or leave equipment behind. Or hold the closing enemy harder, and risk the units that must board last. Either way, the time available for the lift shrinks against the pursuit.

decisionPoints.name: Managing the Shrink
decisionPoints.context: As the relays lift, the perimeter must fold inward to match your falling strength. You have three ways to do it. Contract evenly all the way around to keep a balanced ring. Give up the open landward flats fast and pull tight against the sea early. Or hold the wide perimeter as long as you can, then fold late and fast at the very end. Each choice weighs how much ground you deny the enemy against how cleanly the rearguard reaches its own last lift.

options.title: Contract Evenly
advantages: Folding the perimeter in evenly all around after each relay keeps a balanced ring with no weak face for the enemy to exploit
A measured, even contraction is the most controllable and the least likely to tip from an orderly fold into a collapse
disadvantages: An even contraction gives up defensible ground on every face, whether or not the enemy is pressing it, so you cede terrain you could have held
Spreading strength evenly around the whole ring means no sector is held in real force, so a determined enemy push at any one point is still met by a thin line
options.consequence: You keep a clean, balanced ring, but you give up ground evenly to do it. The perimeter stays controllable and boardable, while the enemy is handed terrain on quiet faces it never had to fight for.

costs.resource: defensible ground ceded evenly on every face to keep the ring balanced
costs.risk: A thin balanced ring is too weak everywhere when the enemy concentrates its force at one point

options.title: Tight to the Sea Early
advantages: Giving up the open landward flats fast and pulling tight against the water early gives you a short, strong arc around the aprons
A short perimeter can be held in concentrated strength and reached quickly when the rearguard's turn to board finally comes
disadvantages: Giving up the flats early lets the enemy close to short range while the lift still has many relays left to run
A tight early arc keeps the enemy near the aprons for longer, pressuring the loading itself through most of the operation
options.consequence: You hold a strong, short arc and board cleanly, but the enemy gets near the aprons early. The contraction is safe and controllable, while the lift has to work under close pressure for most of its cycles.

costs.resource: the landward flats given up early, leaving the enemy near the aprons for the whole lift
costs.risk: An enemy at close range through most of the lift threatens the loading of every relay

options.title: Hold Wide, Fold Late
advantages: Hold the full perimeter as long as your strength allows, denying the enemy ground and keeping the aprons far from the fighting
A wide hold kept late protects the loading through most of the lift and may save equipment that a tighter ring would have to abandon
disadvantages: Holding the wide perimeter with falling strength stretches the line dangerously thin, risking a break that turns into a collapse
Folding late and fast is the hardest maneuver of all, and a rushed final contraction can leave the rearguard scrambling for the last lift
options.consequence: You deny the most ground and protect the lift the longest, but at the highest risk. If the late fold holds, the rearguard boards last off ground it never gave up cheaply. If it breaks, the collapse comes with the enemy already deep inside the perimeter.

costs.resource: the line stretched thin to hold wide, with the whole contraction gambled on one late, fast fold
costs.risk: A thin, wide line breaks into a collapse with the enemy already inside the perimeter

entries.event: The rearguard mans the perimeter around the field. The first DropShip grounds, loads, and launches, and the contraction begins.
One relay after another lifts the beaten force. The perimeter folds inward as its own defenders embark, and the pursuing enemy nears the open flats.
The enemy reaches the landward approaches and presses the shrinking perimeter. The lift now has to work against closing pressure.
The perimeter is down to a tight arc around the aprons. The last of the protected force boards, and the rearguard prepares its own lift.
The enemy reaches the approaches to the aprons. The final relays must lift the rearguard now or leave it on the field.

reactionTimeline.hardDeadline: Lift the protected force, and then the rearguard, before the enemy overruns the loading aprons at roughly T+4:00. After that the last DropShip launches with whoever made it aboard, and the field belongs to the enemy. A rearguard caught on the aprons is the cost of a perimeter that either shrank too slowly or held too long, and the last keel up leaves without it.

opforSketch.composition: A pursuing enemy combined-arms force exploiting the broken offensive. The lead is a fast medium-to-heavy 'Mech force (45-75 tons, Regular to Veteran) driving on the field, supported by mechanized elements and combat vehicles moving across the open shore flats (the vehicle portion of the enemy force). It presses the contracting perimeter to reach the aprons before the lift empties them. The beaten force and the DropShips are what the player is protecting; the rearguard is the player's contracting line.
opforSketch.behavior: The enemy drives to overrun the field before the lift finishes, pressing the perimeter's weakest face and crowding the aprons. It will exploit either a contraction that gives up ground too fast or a line stretched too thin, reading the withdrawal and speeding toward the loading point. It does not break off because of casualties while the field is still within reach, because the prize is the army on the ground and the rearguard holding it, and it presses hardest as the final relays load.

forks.name: OPERATION ALL ABOARD
forks.trigger: The beaten force and the rearguard were both lifted off-world before the enemy overran the field.
forks.consequence: The army is off {WORLD} intact, and {TARGET_FACTION} takes an empty field, denied the destruction of a force it had already beaten. The next operation rebuilds the preserved army off-world. {EMPLOYER} becomes known as the rearguard that got everyone off, and that reputation arrives at the next contract ahead of it.

forks.name: OPERATION LEFT ON THE SAND
forks.trigger: The perimeter collapsed before the lift was complete, or the rearguard was overrun on the aprons before its relay came.
forks.consequence: Part of the force, or the whole rearguard, is lost on the field, and the enemy holds the DropPort. The next operation is a last stand, or a desperate scramble for any DropShip still grounded. The army's escape has turned into a disaster on the sand, with the survivors fighting for a seat that may not exist.

storyElementSeed: A 'Mech walks backward across the emptying loading aprons toward the last grounded DropShip. The perimeter behind it is now a third the size it was at dawn. On the ramp, a loadmaster counts the rearguard aboard one machine at a time, against a relay that cannot wait much longer.

is-davion.objectives.primary: Hold the ring around the field so the army can lift off, and shrink that ring to match as your own strength flies out with them. Fold the line in cleanly, relay by relay, and hold the last arc around the aprons until the final keel is up. Then get your own people aboard. The rearguard boards last, and there is no one behind you to cover the door.

is-steiner.objectives.primary: Hold the shrinking perimeter until the force is lifted, matching the size of the ring to the strength each relay leaves you. The army on this field is the asset to preserve. The rearguard is the cost of preserving it. A rearguard lifted clear turns a lost campaign into a force kept whole. Hold to the last load, then board.

PERIMETER_START_KM.unit: km of perimeter arc at the start

inspiration: A defender holding a chokepoint controls a dam upstream and can release a flood to wash the only assault corridor, but the same flood that stops the enemy also cuts the defender's own line of withdrawal and ruins the ground a relief would need, so the decisive weapon can be used only once and only at the right moment.
skeleton: a defender holding a valley chokepoint can release an upstream reservoir to flood the enemy's only assault corridor, but the flood also severs the defender's own withdrawal and drowns the ground the relief must cross, so the crux is whether and when to spend a single irreversible flood that stops the attack at the cost of the way out
title: OPERATION OPEN THE GATES
situation: {EMPLOYER} holds the gateway to the {DISTRICT} lowlands on {WORLD}. The gateway's strongest weapon is a wall of water it can use exactly once. The occupier's drive into the lowlands has only one practical route: up the river valley and through a chokepoint where the floodplain narrows between high ground. This is the one corridor a heavy force can use to reach the farms and towns beyond, and {EMPLOYER}'s garrison holds it. Above the chokepoint, on the valley's shoulder, sits a repaired irrigation reservoir behind a dam. The garrison controls its gates. Open those gates and the reservoir floods the valley floor, turning the assault corridor first into a torrent and then into a mire that no 'Mech or vehicle can cross while the water runs. This is the defense's strongest weapon, but it works only once. The reservoir empties in a single release, the flood cannot be called back, and its effect lasts the whole flooding. {NPC:intel-source}, an engineer who maintains the dam, explains the catch that turns the weapon into a trap. The flood that drowns the enemy's corridor also drowns the garrison's own retreat down the valley, and it ruins the very ground a friendly relief force would have to cross to reach the chokepoint. So opening the gates stops the attack, strands the garrison, and blocks its rescue all at once. The report on the enemy's assembly is {INTEL_AGE_DAYS} hours old, and an attack massing for the corridor will hit hard. The whole defense turns on one choice that cannot be undone. Hold the chokepoint with weapons alone and keep the flood in reserve. Spend the flood early to break the assault before it closes, and accept that the garrison will be stranded. Or hold to the last and open the gates only when the line is about to break, gambling that the relief reaches the valley before the water makes that impossible. The floodplain chokepoint is the main terrain problem. It is a narrow corridor of soft river-bottom ground between high shoulders. Movement is fast only on the built-up tracks the enemy must use, and the whole valley becomes a lake the moment the gates open. Recommended force: {FORCE_SIZE} combined arms. Use vehicles for the built-up tracks and 'Mechs to hold the narrows. Hold the gateway, and decide whether and when to spend the one flood that stops the enemy at the cost of your own way out and your relief's way in.

objectives.primary: Hold the valley chokepoint against the occupier's assault and deny it the corridor to the lowlands. Use the upstream flood if and when the situation demands, knowing the release cannot be undone and cuts off both the garrison's withdrawal and the relief's approach.
objectives.secondary: Where you can, preserve the garrison's route of withdrawal and the relief's approach. Holding the chokepoint by weapons alone keeps the valley open behind you. Spending the flood seals the garrison in with the enemy it stopped.
objectives.bonus: Hold the chokepoint without releasing the flood at all. A corridor denied by fighting alone keeps the dam's one release in hand for the next attack, and keeps the valley passable for both the relief force and the harvest.

complications.name: The Flood Spends Once
complications.text: The reservoir empties in a single release that cannot be called back or repeated. Open the gates and the flood is gone. The valley floor becomes a torrent and then a mire for as long as the water runs, and your one decisive move is played for good. There is no second flood and no taking it back, so the whole defense turns on whether and when to use it.
complications.mechanicalEffect: The flood release is a one-time action that cannot be undone. It floods the assault corridor and denies it to enemy ground movement for the rest of the operation. You cannot do it in stages, partially, or more than once. Once spent, you have only your weapons. Held in reserve, the flood stays a threat the enemy must respect, but it does nothing to actually stop the assault.

complications.name: The Trump Strands the Holder
complications.text: The flood that drowns the enemy's corridor also drowns the garrison's own withdrawal down the valley, and it ruins the ground the relief must cross to reach the chokepoint. Opening the gates stops the attack, strands the garrison, and blocks its rescue in one stroke. The defense's strongest weapon is also the act that seals the garrison's own fate.
complications.mechanicalEffect: Releasing the flood cuts off the garrison's route of withdrawal and blocks the relief's approach for the whole flooding. Spend the flood and you commit to holding the chokepoint alone, with no withdrawal and no relief until the water falls. You are trading the enemy's mobility for your own mobility and your rescue.

complications.name: The Soft Narrows
complications.text: The chokepoint is soft river-bottom ground between high shoulders. Fast movement is possible only on the built-up tracks the enemy's heavy force must use. The narrows favor the defender, because the corridor is tight and the approaches are few, but the soft ground off the tracks bogs down maneuver. So the fight is funneled onto the same built-up tracks the flood would drown, for both sides.
complications.mechanicalEffect: Off-track movement in the floodplain is slow because of the soft ground, so both forces are funneled onto the built-up tracks through the narrows. This helps you hold the chokepoint. But it also means the decisive ground is exactly what the flood would destroy. Releasing the flood denies the tracks to the enemy and to your own maneuver alike.

complications.name: The Relief Races the Water
complications.text: A friendly relief force is on its way down the valley, and the garrison does not control when it arrives. Hold without flooding and the relief can reach the chokepoint. Open the gates and the relief is locked out until the water falls. Two clocks, the pressure of the assault and the approach of the relief, pull the flood decision in opposite directions.
complications.mechanicalEffect: On a die roll during the defense, the relief's estimated arrival time shifts, so you must weigh the flood decision against whether the relief can arrive before the line breaks. Holding by weapons keeps the relief's approach open but risks the line. Flooding stops the assault but strands you until the water falls, which may be later than the relief could have arrived. Within the operation's time window, the flood and the relief cannot both happen. Choosing one rules out the other.

decisionPoints.name: Whether to Open the Gates
decisionPoints.context: The assault masses for the corridor while the dam waits above. You have three options. Hold the chokepoint with weapons alone and keep the flood in reserve. Open the gates early to break the assault before it closes, and accept that the garrison will be stranded. Or hold to the last and flood only if the line is about to break. Each choice weighs a sure way to stop the enemy against your own way out and the relief's way in.

options.title: Hold by Weapons, Flood in Reserve
advantages: Holding the narrows by fighting alone keeps the valley open behind you for the garrison's withdrawal and the relief's approach
The unspent flood stays a standing threat the enemy must respect, and the dam's one release stays in hand for the worst case
disadvantages: Holding a heavy assault in the chokepoint by weapons alone is hard, and a garrison that waits too long to flood may be overrun before it can open the gates
If the line breaks while the flood is still in reserve, the decisive weapon is lost unused and the corridor falls open
options.consequence: You keep your way out and the relief's way in, but you face a harder fight. The chokepoint either holds by weapons or it does not, and the flood waits unused, either a saved weapon or a missed chance.

costs.resource: the chokepoint held by fighting alone against a heavy assault
costs.risk: The line breaks before the flood is spent, losing both the flood and the corridor

options.title: Open the Gates Early
advantages: Releasing the flood before the assault closes drowns the corridor and stops the attack cold while the garrison is still at full strength
Spending the flood early breaks the enemy's heavy thrust for certain, denying it the lowlands without a desperate fight in the narrows
disadvantages: The flood strands the garrison and locks out the relief at the same moment, so the chokepoint is held in isolation with no way out until the water falls
An early release spends the flood on an assault that might have been held by weapons, sealing the garrison in for nothing if that was so
options.consequence: You stop the enemy for certain, but the garrison is now isolated. The corridor is denied and the line is spared a hard fight, but the valley is a lake behind a garrison holding alone until the water recedes.

costs.resource: the garrison's withdrawal and the relief's approach, both cut off by the early flood
costs.risk: The flood spent early strands the garrison against an assault it might have held without it

options.title: Hold to the Last, Flood at the Break
advantages: Holding by weapons as long as the line stands, then opening the gates only when it is about to break, gets the most from the fight before spending the flood
Delaying the flood keeps the relief's approach open the longest and saves the water for the true crisis
disadvantages: Judging the exact moment is unforgiving. Flood too late and the line is already broken with the enemy through. Flood too soon and the wait was wasted.
A flood released at the last instant, amid a collapsing line, may catch the garrison's own units on the wrong ground as the water rises
options.consequence: You get the most from both the fight and the flood, but at the highest risk. Timed right, the assault is stopped at the last moment and the relief has nearly reached the valley. Timed wrong, the gates open onto a line already broken, or your own units are caught by the rising water.

costs.resource: the flood decision staked on reading the exact moment the line is about to break
costs.risk: A flood released too late opens onto a broken line, and too early wastes the wait and strands the garrison anyway

entries.event: The occupier's assault masses at the mouth of the valley corridor. The garrison mans the chokepoint, and the dam stands ready above.
The assault's lead elements push onto the built-up tracks into the narrows, probing the garrison's hold.
The main assault commits up the corridor. The garrison fights to hold the narrows, and the flood decision starts to press.
The assault strains the chokepoint hardest. The line bends, and the moment to spend or withhold the flood arrives.
The crisis arrives. The corridor is held or broken, the flood is spent or saved, and the relief is in the valley or locked out.

reactionTimeline.hardDeadline: Deny the corridor, by weapons or by flood, before the assault forces the chokepoint at roughly T+3:30. After that, the lowlands are open if the gate fell, or held at the cost you chose. That cost is either a corridor drowned and the garrison stranded, or a line held whole with the relief arriving and the flood still in hand. The one outcome worse than a hard fight is a line broken with the flood unspent: the corridor lost, and the flood that would have saved it never opened.

opforSketch.composition: An occupier's deliberate combined-arms assault up a single corridor. The main effort is a heavy 'Mech force (heavy and assault, 60-90 tons, Regular to Veteran) driving up the built-up tracks through the narrows, supported by mechanized elements and combat vehicles confined to the same tracks by the soft ground (the vehicle portion of the enemy force). The assault wants the corridor to the lowlands and must use the funneled approaches. It breaks contact if reduced past roughly a third of its strength, and a corridor drowned by the flood forces it to abandon the axis entirely until the water falls.
opforSketch.behavior: The assault drives up the funneled corridor to force the chokepoint, massing on the built-up tracks because the soft ground denies maneuver. It respects the standing threat of the dam and pushes hard to close before the garrison can flood, knowing a released reservoir denies it the axis. If the flood is spent, it cannot cross the drowned corridor and must wait or look for another route. If the garrison holds by weapons alone, it presses the narrows relentlessly to break the line before any relief arrives.

forks.name: OPERATION GATE HELD
forks.trigger: The corridor was denied, either by a well-timed flood or by the garrison's fighting, and the lowlands were kept.
forks.consequence: The occupier's drive into the lowlands is stopped at the gate, and how it was stopped shapes what comes next. Either a valley held whole with the relief arriving, or a corridor drowned and a stranded garrison to be recovered when the water falls. The next operation holds or recovers the secured chokepoint and the lowlands behind it.

forks.name: OPERATION FLOODGATE LOST
forks.trigger: The chokepoint was forced: the line broke with the flood unspent or released too late, and the corridor fell open.
forks.consequence: The occupier is through the gate and into the lowlands, with the garrison broken or stranded in a drowned valley for nothing. The next operation is a fighting withdrawal of the survivors out of the lowlands, ahead of the enemy's advance. The gate is lost, and with it the farms and towns the chokepoint was the last thing guarding.

storyElementSeed: An engineer stands at a dam's control housing above a narrow valley, one hand on the gate release. Below, the assault grinds up the tracks, and the garrison's line reports keep bending. He waits for the order that can be given only once and never taken back.

merc.objectives.primary: Hold the gate and keep the enemy out of the lowlands, and decide for yourself whether to pull the dam, which you can do only once. Open the gates and you stop them cold but trap yourself in with no relief coming. Hold by guns and you keep the door open behind you, but it is a harder fight. The flood is yours to spend, but only once, and not a drop comes back.

is-steiner.objectives.primary: Deny the corridor and hold the lowlands, using the upstream flood if the situation demands it. The flood is a one-time asset that stops the enemy but strands you at the same time. Spend it only if the chokepoint cannot be held any other way. A corridor denied by your guns keeps the dam in reserve and the valley open, and that is the better outcome if you can manage it.

CHOKEPOINT_WIDTH_M.unit: meters of corridor width at the narrows

FLOOD_DURATION_HR.unit: hours the corridor stays drowned after release

inspiration: A fresh unit must take over a held line from a spent one without the enemy noticing the handover, because a relief-in-place caught mid-swap — neither unit fully set, the line at its most fragile — is the moment an alert enemy attacks to roll up both, so the whole problem is the silent exchange under contact.
skeleton: a fresh relief force must take over a cut-off unit's held line position-by-position without the besieging enemy detecting the handover, where a relief-in-place caught mid-swap is the line at its most fragile and any sign of the exchange invites the attack that destroys both units, so the crux is the silent in-place relief under the enemy's eyes
title: OPERATION CHANGING OF THE GUARD
situation: A {EMPLOYER} company has held a line too long, and {EMPLOYER} wants to relieve it without the enemy knowing the line changed hands. On the {DISTRICT} ridge on {WORLD}, this company has held a defensive position against a probing {TARGET_FACTION} force for weeks. It is spent: machines worn, warriors exhausted, ammunition low. It can hold a little longer only because the enemy does not know how thin it has become. Your force is being sent to take the line over. The hard part is the hand-over itself. A relief-in-place means a fresh unit moving into the positions a tired unit is leaving. It is the most fragile moment a held line ever has. During the swap, neither unit is fully set, positions are only half-manned, and two forces are tangled on the same ground. If the enemy spots a relief in progress, they attack into it, and that attack can wreck both units at once: the one not yet dug in and the one not yet clear. {NPC:intel-source}, the spent company's commander, lays out three facts. The enemy probes the line on a steady rhythm. The firing positions are linked by covered routes on the reverse slope, so a unit can move in or out unseen if it is done right. And the whole exchange has to happen without the enemy reading a single sign that the line is changing hands. The report on the enemy's probing pattern is {INTEL_AGE_DAYS} hours old, so treat it as a guide, not a guarantee: a watchful enemy can change its habits. The job is not to win a battle. It is to make a change invisible. Move the fresh force into the line position by position as the spent force slips out. Keep every position manned and the line looking unchanged the whole time. Finish the relief before the enemy ever notices the guard has changed. The ridge is the main terrain problem. It is a chain of linked firing positions along high ground, joined by covered routes on the reverse slope where movement stays hidden. But the front faces an enemy whose whole job is to watch for exactly the disturbance a relief creates. Recommended force: {FORCE_SIZE} combined arms. Use the vehicle element to move fast on the reverse-slope routes and 'Mechs to hold the firing positions. You win with a hand-over the enemy never sees. You lose the instant they read the line in flux and attack into the gap.

objectives.primary: Relieve the spent company in place. Move the fresh force into its defensive positions as it pulls out, and do not let the besieging enemy detect the handover. Keep every position manned and the line looking unbroken the whole time.
objectives.secondary: Get the spent company's worn 'Mechs and tired warriors out intact. A tired unit that escapes whole can be refit and fight again. A unit caught and cut up mid-withdrawal is the very company the relief came to save, lost.
objectives.bonus: Finish the relief with the fresh force's full strength hidden. If the enemy misses the swap and never learns the line was reinforced, it will probe a position it thinks is still weakening and run into a defense now at full strength.

complications.name: The Fragile Swap
complications.text: A relief-in-place is the weakest moment a held line ever has. During the handover, neither unit is fully set, positions are only half-manned, and two forces are tangled on the same ground. If the enemy attacks a relief in progress, they can wreck both units at once: the one not yet dug in and the one not yet clear. The danger is the exchange itself, not the holding before or after it.
complications.mechanicalEffect: During the handover, each position being swapped is briefly weaker as one unit moves out and the other moves in. An enemy attack that hits a position mid-swap finds it at its weakest. Sequence the exchange so no position is dangerously weak when the enemy probes it. A swap caught mid-transition can lose both the incoming and outgoing units in that sector.

complications.name: Make the Change Invisible
complications.text: The spent company holds only because the enemy does not know how thin it is. If the besiegers spot the relief, they learn the line is in flux and attack to destroy it. So keep every position manned and the line looking unbroken the whole time. Movement, signatures, and firing rhythm all stay as if nothing is changing. The job is to make a change the enemy never sees.
complications.mechanicalEffect: The enemy grows suspicious from signs of the relief: movement on the routes, positions that go briefly silent, changes in the line's signature. If suspicion crosses a set threshold, the enemy attacks into the relief. Keep suspicion below that threshold: time movement to covered windows and keep positions active so the swap shows as little as possible.

complications.name: The Watched Front
complications.text: The front of the ridge is watched by an enemy whose whole job is to spot the disturbance a relief creates. The covered reverse-slope routes can pass a unit in or out unseen, but the firing positions themselves are in that enemy's view. The move between the front and the routes is the exposed seam, and the besiegers are watching exactly the ground where a relief shows itself.
complications.mechanicalEffect: The firing positions are watched from the front. The reverse-slope routes are covered. The moment a unit leaves or occupies a firing position is the exposed one. Time movement to the covered routes and stay concealed at the positions themselves. Careless movement in view of the front raises suspicion fast.

complications.name: The Probe May Come Anyway
complications.text: The enemy probes the line on a rhythm whether or not it suspects a relief. A probe that lands on a position mid-swap finds it weak by chance, not by plan. The spent company's read of the probing pattern is hours old. A probe that comes off-rhythm, or a watchful enemy that changes its habits, can stumble onto the handover at its most fragile moment.
complications.mechanicalEffect: On a die roll during the relief, the enemy sends a probe against a sector, scheduled or off-rhythm. If it lands on a position mid-swap, that position is at its weakest, and you must hold it through the probe without revealing the exchange. Weather the probe without the enemy realizing it hit a relief and the swap stays secret. Let it expose the flux and the wider attack begins.

decisionPoints.name: Sequencing the Relief
decisionPoints.context: The line must change hands unseen, and the order of the swap decides how exposed it is. You have three options. Relieve position by position in sequence, so all but one stays set at any time. Swap the whole line at once in a single fast exchange. Or relieve the strongest positions first and leave the quiet sectors for last. Each choice trades how long the relief takes against how weak the line gets at any single moment.

options.title: One Position at a Time
advantages: Relieve the line one position at a time, so only one position is ever in flux while the rest stay set and manned
The line never has more than one weak point at once, which is easiest to cover and least likely to be caught broadly exposed
disadvantages: A one-at-a-time relief is slow, keeping two forces tangled on the ridge for the longest total time
The longer the exchange runs, the more probes it must survive and the more chances the enemy has to read the flux
options.consequence: You keep the line strongest at any single moment, but it costs time. The swap is safe position by position, but drawn out. The long handover must weather more of the enemy's probing rhythm before it finishes.

costs.resource: the longest total exchange time, with two forces tangled on the ridge
costs.risk: A drawn-out relief weathers more probes and more chances to be read

options.title: Swap the Whole Line at Once
advantages: Exchange the whole line in a single fast handover, cutting the total time two forces are tangled on the ridge
A quick swap is exposed for the shortest span, with fewer probes to survive before the relief is set
disadvantages: During the all-at-once swap, the whole line is in flux together, so every position is weak at the same time if the enemy attacks then
An all-at-once exchange has no margin: a probe that lands during it finds not one weak position but the entire ridge fragile
options.consequence: You shorten the exposure to one fast window, but you are wide open inside it. If the enemy probes during the swap, the whole line is weak at once. If it does not, the relief is finished before the besiegers can react.

costs.resource: the whole line in flux at once for one short exposed window
costs.risk: A probe during the all-at-once swap finds the entire ridge weak together

options.title: Strong Positions First
advantages: Relieve the strongest, most-watched positions first while the fresh force is freshest, leaving the quiet sectors for last
The key positions are handed over cleanly early, and the quiet sectors' brief weakness late draws the least enemy attention
disadvantages: Doing the strongest positions first means the most exposed swaps happen while the relief still has the whole exchange ahead of it
Leaving the quiet sectors for last assumes they stay quiet. If the enemy shifts its probing to a sector saved for the end, it catches it weak
options.consequence: You secure the vital ground early, but you front-load the risk. The key positions are safe, but you are gambling that the quiet sectors stay quiet until their turn. An enemy that probes them late finds the seam.

costs.resource: the most exposed swaps front-loaded while the whole exchange remains ahead
costs.risk: An enemy probing a quiet sector saved for last catches it weak, off the assumed rhythm

entries.event: The fresh force reaches the reverse-slope routes. The spent company holds the line, and the relief begins by the covered ways.
The first positions change hands. The fresh force occupies firing positions as the spent units slip out, with the line kept manned throughout.
The relief is half-complete. Both forces are tangled on the ridge, and the enemy probes the line on its rhythm.
The last positions change hands. The spent company withdraws by the covered routes as the fresh force sets the final firing positions.
The relief finishes: the fresh force is set, the spent company is clear, the line is whole, and the handover was unseen. Or the enemy read the flux and attacked into it.

reactionTimeline.hardDeadline: Finish the relief before the enemy detects the handover and attacks the seam: the fresh force set, the spent company clear. That window closes around T+3:30. Miss it and two tangled units are caught mid-swap by an attack timed to the line's weakest moment. A handover the besiegers read turns a quiet exchange into the loss of both companies, the one coming and the one going.

opforSketch.composition: A {TARGET_FACTION} besieging force probing a held line, combined arms. The force facing the ridge is a medium 'Mech force (45-65 tons, Regular to Veteran) that probes the line on a rhythm, supported by mechanized elements and combat vehicles (the vehicle portion of the enemy force), watching the front for any sign of weakness. It is not yet assaulting in strength, but it has the strength to attack into a detected relief and roll up a line caught in flux. The spent company is {EMPLOYER}'s own, holding thin; the relief is the player's force.
opforSketch.behavior: The besiegers probe the line on a pattern to test its strength and watch for change, content to wear the spent company down by pressure rather than risk a costly assault. The moment they read the line in flux (a relief in progress, positions weakening, the rhythm broken) they attack into the seam with their full weight to destroy both tangled units. Their strength is vigilance and the threat of that attack; their habit is the probing rhythm the relief must work around.

forks.name: OPERATION GUARD CHANGED
forks.trigger: The relief finished unseen: the fresh force set, the spent company clear, the enemy none the wiser.
forks.consequence: A fresh force now holds a line the enemy thinks is still weakening, and the spent company is out whole to refit.
