In the next operation, the besiegers probe a position they believe is failing and run into a defense at full strength. The relief's secrecy becomes the trap that breaks the next attack.

forks.name: OPERATION CAUGHT IN THE OPEN
forks.trigger: The enemy detected the handover and attacked the relief, catching both units tangled mid-swap.
forks.consequence: The attack rolls up the line at its weakest, with both the fresh and spent forces caught in flux. The next operation is a desperate fight to pull whatever survives off the ridge. The relief is blown, the spent company is lost mid-withdrawal, and the line the handover was meant to save is broken open.

storyElementSeed: A fresh 'Mech settles into a firing position still warm from the worn machine that just slipped down the reverse slope. Its crew copies the old unit's firing rhythm exactly, so the watchers across the valley see nothing change, while a sergeant times the next swap to the enemy's probing clock.

merc.objectives.primary: Take the line over from the worn-out company without the enemy seeing it change hands. Keep every position manned, match their firing rhythm, and move only on the covered routes. The moment the besiegers read a relief in progress, they hit the seam, and an attack on a half-finished swap kills both companies at once. Make the change, and make it invisible.

is-steiner.objectives.primary: Relieve the spent company in place, unseen, and keep the line whole through the exchange. The handover is the fragile moment: two forces tangled and the line at its weakest. Concealment is your whole defense. Get the tired unit out intact and the fresh one set without the enemy reading a single sign, and the line changes hands without a shot.

inspiration: A small detachment holds a high observation post that directs the fire of distant guns onto the enemy, and must keep the post functioning and calling fire even as it is overrun, because the moment the eyes go dark the guns fall silent and the whole front loses its reach, so the value is in the post still working, not merely in the ground held.
skeleton: a detachment must hold a mountain observation-and-fire-direction post functioning under assault so the distant guns it directs keep firing, where the value is the post still calling fire rather than the ground itself and going dark to save the detachment blinds the whole front, so the crux is keeping the eyes working while they are overrun
title: OPERATION STILL WATCHING
situation: {EMPLOYER}'s guns reach across the {DISTRICT} front on {WORLD} only because one post on a mountaintop can see, and {TARGET_FACTION} is coming to blind it. The post sits on a peak above the front and watches the whole approach. From it, {EMPLOYER}'s distant long-range batteries and aerospace strikes are aimed at anything that moves in the valleys below. The post is the front's reach. As long as it sees and calls fire, the guns land accurately on an enemy that is kilometers away, beyond what the gunners themselves can see. Blind the post and the batteries fire into the dark, wasted, and the front loses the long arm holding the enemy back. The enemy knows this and has sent a force up the mountain, not to hold the peak, but to silence the post. {EMPLOYER}'s detachment holds it. {NPC:intel-source}, who coordinates the batteries, lays out the hard part. The post must keep working and calling fire even while it is attacked, because its value is the fire it still directs, not the ground it sits on. If the detachment goes dark to protect itself, by pulling back, sheltering, or stopping its transmissions, the whole front goes blind that instant. A post held but silent is a post lost. The report on the assault force is {INTEL_AGE_DAYS} hours old, and a force climbing to silence a post climbs hard. So the job is a hold with a cruel condition. Do not just keep the enemy off the peak. Keep the post working, observing, transmitting, and directing fire, all through the assault. The observers call strikes onto the very force closing on them while the detachment fights to keep the eyes open as they are being gouged out. The peak is the main terrain problem. Only two or three climbing approaches reach it, the post and its gear crowd the summit, and there is little room to maneuver. The slopes around it are the killing ground the post directs fire onto. The detachment holds the approaches while the observers keep calling the guns down on the climbers, and the closer the enemy gets, the nearer the summit the directed fire must fall. Recommended force: {FORCE_SIZE} combined arms. Use the vehicle element for the climbing approaches and 'Mechs to hold the summit. You win by keeping the post watching when the assault breaks. You lose the instant the eyes shut, whether the enemy closes them or the detachment does.

objectives.primary: Keep the observation post working all through {TARGET_FACTION}'s assault, observing, transmitting, and directing the distant guns onto the enemy, until the assault is broken. Never let the eyes go dark.
objectives.secondary: Direct the batteries' fire onto the climbing assault to break it on the slopes. The post's called fire is its heaviest weapon, and a force shattered by directed strikes never reaches the summit.
objectives.bonus: Keep the post's observation gear intact through the fight. A post that survives undamaged keeps directing the front's fire afterward. One that holds but loses its gear is blind even in victory.

complications.name: Going Dark Blinds the Front
complications.text: The post's value is the fire it directs, not the peak it sits on. If the detachment goes dark to protect itself, by sheltering, withdrawing, or stopping its transmissions, the whole front's guns go blind that instant. A post held but silent is a post lost. Shutting the eyes is the one move that is forbidden, because shut eyes mean failure whether the enemy closes them or the detachment does.
complications.mechanicalEffect: The post must keep working, observing and transmitting, throughout the operation. Any stretch where the detachment goes dark, by sheltering the observers or stopping its transmissions, blinds the distant batteries and pushes the primary objective toward FAILURE, even if the peak is held. Holding the ground while silent does not satisfy the mission. The eyes must stay open under fire.

complications.name: Calling Fire on the Climbers
complications.text: The post's heaviest weapon is the fire it directs. As the assault climbs, those strikes fall nearer and nearer the summit, onto slopes the post overlooks, closer to the detachment with every meter the enemy gains. The observers call the guns down on the force closing on them, and the nearer it gets, the more the called fire risks the post's own ground.
complications.mechanicalEffect: The post directs the distant batteries onto the climbing assault, and that directed fire is most of the detachment's striking power. As the enemy nears the summit, called strikes land closer to the post and threaten the detachment's own positions. A danger-close call that breaks the assault may also hit the defenders, so the observers must judge how near the summit to bring the fire.

complications.name: The Climbing Approaches
complications.text: A few steep climbing approaches reach the peak, and the post and its gear crowd the summit with little room to maneuver. The detachment holds the approaches while the observers work the gear above. The cramped summit has no depth and no flank. The defense is the approaches plus the killing ground the post directs fire onto, with nowhere to fall back but the eyes themselves.
complications.mechanicalEffect: Only a few steep climbing approaches reach the summit, and the post area is cramped with no room to maneuver or fall back. The detachment defends the approaches while the directed fire covers the slopes between them. There is no depth. A breached approach is at the summit at once, and the observers' gear is in the front line of any close fight.

complications.name: The Assault Climbs Hard
complications.text: A force sent to silence a post climbs fast, accepting losses to reach the summit before the called fire breaks it. The assault's strength and pace in the briefing are hours old. A determined climb pushed up several approaches at once can reach the post faster than the directed strikes can stop it, racing to close the eyes before the guns shut the climb down.
complications.mechanicalEffect: On a die roll during the defense, the assault presses harder or adds an approach, shortening the time before it reaches the summit. The detachment must then either bring the directed fire nearer the post to break the faster climb, risking its own ground, or hold the approaches harder with weapons, risking the cramped summit. The race between the called fire and the climb tightens.

decisionPoints.name: Holding the Eyes Open
decisionPoints.context: The assault climbs and the post must keep watching. You have three options. Keep the directed fire well out on the lower slopes to break the climb early and safely. Bring it danger-close as the enemy nears to stop the final rush, at the risk of your own ground. Or hold the approaches with the detachment's own weapons and save the called fire for the worst moment. Each choice trades how surely the assault is broken against how much you risk the post and its observers.

options.title: Fire Out on the Slopes
advantages: Call the batteries onto the lower slopes to break the assault early, well away from the summit and the post's own ground
Keeping the directed fire far from the peak protects the observers and the gear while still hammering the climb
disadvantages: Fire out on the slopes may not stop a determined climb that pushes through it, and the assault that survives the lower strikes reaches thinner defenses above
Breaking the climb far out spends the batteries' effort on the assault's strongest, most spread-out stage, when it is hardest to shatter
options.consequence: You keep the post safe and break the assault early, but you give up some certainty. If the lower fire breaks the climb, the summit is never seriously threatened. If it does not, the enemy reaches the cramped peak with the called fire now too close to use freely.

costs.resource: the batteries' effort spent on the assault's spread-out lower stage
costs.risk: A climb that survives the lower fire reaches the thin summit defenses with fire now too close to use

options.title: Danger-Close at the Summit
advantages: Bring the directed fire near the post as the enemy closes, stopping the final rush with strikes falling close to the summit
Danger-close fire breaks the assault at its most concentrated, decisive moment, shattering the climb just short of the eyes
disadvantages: Fire that close to the summit risks the post, the observers, and the gear the whole mission depends on
A danger-close call that is mistimed or falls wrong damages the very post it is defending, blinding the front with the detachment's own guns
options.consequence: You break the final rush, but you risk the post itself. If the danger-close fire falls true, the assault dies just short of the summit. If it falls wrong, the detachment closes its own eyes with the batteries it called.

costs.resource: the post and its gear risked under danger-close directed fire
costs.risk: A danger-close call that falls wrong damages the post and blinds the front with friendly fire

options.title: Weapons Forward, Fire in Reserve
advantages: Hold the climbing approaches with the detachment's own weapons and save the called fire for the single worst moment of the assault
Keeps the directed fire in reserve for the crisis while the detachment fights the climb directly, sparing the batteries' effort
disadvantages: A cramped detachment holding steep approaches by weapons alone against a hard climb may be overrun before the reserved fire is ever called
Holding the fire in reserve risks calling it too late: the crisis arrives faster than the call, and the fire goes unspent as the summit falls
options.consequence: You hold with your own weapons and keep the fire for the crisis, but you face a harder direct fight. If the approaches hold, the reserved fire breaks the decisive push. If they do not, the post is overrun with the batteries still waiting for the call.

costs.resource: the cramped approaches held by the detachment's own weapons
costs.risk: The summit is overrun before the reserved fire is called, leaving it unspent

entries.event: The assault begins its climb up the approaches. The post observes and transmits, and the first directed strikes fall on the lower slopes.
The assault pushes up the approaches under directed fire. The detachment mans the summit defenses, and the called strikes follow the climb upward.
The assault nears the upper slopes. The directed fire falls closer to the summit, and the detachment's approaches come under direct pressure.
The assault reaches the summit's approaches. The called fire is now danger-close, and the detachment fights at the post itself to keep the eyes open.
The assault makes its peak effort to take the post: the crisis of whether the eyes stay open through the final rush.

reactionTimeline.hardDeadline: Keep the post working and calling fire until the assault is broken, with the crisis falling around T+3:30. After that, one of two things happens. Either the fire the post directed shatters the assault on the slopes and the eyes stay open, or the summit is overrun and the post goes dark. A post that goes dark, whether the enemy closes it or the detachment shelters to survive, blinds the front's guns in that moment and loses the mission no matter what ground is held.

opforSketch.composition: A {TARGET_FACTION} assault force sent to silence the post, combined arms. The climb is led by a medium-to-heavy 'Mech force (50-80 tons, Regular to Veteran) pushing up the approaches, supported by mechanized elements and a few combat vehicles where the slopes allow (the vehicle portion of the enemy force). It climbs to take the summit and put out the post's eyes, accepting cost to reach it before the directed fire breaks the climb. It breaks off if reduced past roughly a third of its strength while the post is still functioning.
opforSketch.behavior: The assault climbs hard to reach and silence the post, pressing multiple approaches to split the directed fire and the detachment's defense. Its goal is the eyes, not the ground: it drives for the observation gear and the summit, not to hold the peak. It accepts heavy fire to close fast, racing the called strikes, and presses hardest at the summit's approaches to take the post before the front's guns can shatter the final rush. A climb broken on the slopes by directed fire may abandon the attempt rather than feed itself into the strikes.

forks.name: OPERATION EYES OPEN
forks.trigger: The post was held working and the assault broken: the eyes stayed open and the directed fire shattered the climb.
forks.consequence: The front keeps its reach, the batteries still landing true across kilometers because one post never stopped watching. The next operation presses the advantage of an intact long arm against an enemy that spent an assault and failed to blind it. The directed fire is now free to range the whole sector again.

forks.name: OPERATION GONE DARK
forks.trigger: The post was overrun or went dark: the eyes closed, by the enemy or by the detachment's own hand, and the guns fell silent.
forks.consequence: The front's batteries fire blind or not at all, and the long arm that held the enemy back is gone. The next operation is a fighting withdrawal off the peak for any survivors, and a front that must now hold without its eyes. The directed fire is silenced, and the enemy moves freely through valleys no one can see into anymore.

storyElementSeed: An observer keeps a glass on the slope below and reads grid coordinates into a transmitter in a steady voice as the enemy climbs into them. The directed fire walks up the mountain toward the post itself, each strike called a little closer than the last, while the detachment holds the approach a few meters away.

merc.objectives.primary: Keep the post watching and calling fire while they climb up to shut it. The contract is the eyes, not the hilltop. Go dark to save yourselves and the whole front's guns go blind in the same second, and a post held quiet is a post lost. Keep transmitting, walk the fire down on the climbers, and do not shut your eyes until the assault breaks.

is-steiner.objectives.primary: Keep the observation post working throughout the assault, directing the batteries onto the enemy the whole time. The post is the front's reach, and its value is the fire it calls, not the peak it holds. Keep it observing and transmitting under fire, break the climb with the guns it directs, and never let the eyes go dark, because dark is a loss no matter how the ground stands.

ASSAULT_CLIMB_HR.unit: hours for the assault to reach the summit

inspiration: A forward medical station must be torn down and its non-ambulatory wounded moved out ahead of an advancing enemy, where the casualties cannot move themselves and the pace is set by litter and ambulance, so the defense must buy exactly the time the slow evacuation needs and not a minute it cannot use.
skeleton: a covering force must screen the teardown and evacuation of a forward field hospital full of non-ambulatory wounded ahead of an enemy advance, where the casualties set a litter-slow pace and the teardown competes with the defense for the same hands and time, so the crux is buying exactly the slow evacuation's time against an enemy that wants the ground
title: OPERATION GENTLE HANDS
situation: {EMPLOYER}'s forward field hospital is in the path of an advance, and the wounded in it cannot get up and walk. The hospital is a clearing station in the {DISTRICT} backcountry on {WORLD}, treating casualties from a front that has now bent. A {TARGET_FACTION} advance is pushing toward the clearing and is only hours away. The hospital must come out: its surgical gear, its supplies, and above all its patients. There are scores of non-ambulatory wounded who cannot move themselves and cannot be left to an enemy that may or may not treat them decently. {EMPLOYER} sends your force to cover the evacuation. {NPC:intel-source}, the hospital's senior surgeon, explains the pace. The wounded move at the speed of a litter and an ambulance, no faster. The worst cases cannot be rushed without killing them. And tearing down the hospital, meaning the gear plus the medics needed to move patients safely, competes for the same time and the same hands as everything else. The report on the advance is {INTEL_AGE_DAYS} hours old, and an advance that finds a soft target speeds up. This is not a hold for its own sake, and not a race the wounded can run. It is a covering action timed to a slow, fragile evacuation. Buy exactly the time the litter-paced evacuation needs, and hold the ground until the last patient is loaded and away, no longer and not a minute short. Screen too far forward and the force is stretched, leaving the hospital exposed if the screen breaks. Pull in too tight and the enemy is on the clearing before the slow evacuation can finish. The teardown itself eats the clock: every casualty loaded gently costs time the advance is using to close the distance. The backcountry clearing is the main terrain problem. It is a cleared station in close country with few but covered approaches. The way out is a single track through dense terrain, one an ambulance convoy can use but cannot hurry on, slow going every kilometer for a column of wounded. Recommended force: {FORCE_SIZE} combined arms. Use the vehicle element to screen the covered approaches and shepherd the convoy, and 'Mechs to anchor the clearing's defense. You win by getting every patient out alive. You lose with every wounded soldier the advance reaches before the slow, careful hands can move them.

objectives.primary: Cover the teardown and evacuation of the field hospital and its non-ambulatory wounded ahead of the {TARGET_FACTION} advance. Hold the clearing until the last patient is loaded, then screen the ambulance column out the evacuation track.
objectives.secondary: Get the hospital's surgical gear and supplies out alongside the patients. A field hospital recovered whole can treat the front's next casualties. One stripped to save only its patients leaves tomorrow's wounded with nothing.
objectives.bonus: Evacuate every patient, including the worst cases. Buy even the casualties who cannot be rushed the slow time they need and you lose no one. A defense that breaks early forces the triage no one wants to make.

complications.name: The Litter-Slow Pace
complications.text: The wounded move at the speed of a litter and an ambulance, no faster. The worst cases cannot be rushed without killing them. Careful hands and slow loading are not a luxury. They are the only way the casualties survive the move. The evacuation cannot go faster than that fixed slow pace, so the defense must buy exactly that much time, weighing the enemy's speed against the litter's.
complications.mechanicalEffect: The evacuation runs at a fixed slow rate set by safe patient handling, and it cannot be sped up without losing casualties. The covering force must hold the clearing for the full time the slow evacuation needs. Success is measured by patients gotten out alive, so the job is to buy the litter-paced clock its time, not to win a fight or hold forever.

complications.name: The Teardown Eats the Clock
complications.text: Tearing down the hospital, meaning the surgical gear, the supplies, and the medics needed to move patients safely, competes for the same time and people as everything else. Every casualty loaded gently costs time the advance is using to close in, and the hands packing gear are hands not loading the wounded. The evacuation's own work is part of the clock the defense must cover.
complications.mechanicalEffect: The teardown and the patient evacuation draw on the same limited medical staff and time, so favoring gear recovery slows patient loading, and the reverse. The covering force's hold must cover both. An evacuation that tries to save everything moves slower and needs more time held. One that abandons gear to speed the patients out clears faster but loses the hospital's future capacity.

complications.name: The Single Track Out
complications.text: The way out is a single track through dense close country, one an ambulance convoy can use but cannot hurry on. The wounded leave by that one slow road. A column of ambulances on it is strung out, fragile, and unable to speed up or turn around. The screen must hold the track open and shepherd the convoy down it at the litter's pace, slow going the whole way.
complications.mechanicalEffect: The evacuation track is a single slow route through close terrain, and the ambulance convoy moves down it at a fixed slow pace, strung out and vulnerable. The screen must keep the track open and cover the convoy along it. A cut track or a halted convoy strands the wounded in the open, and the slow pace means the column is exposed for a long trip.

complications.name: The Advance Quickens on a Soft Target
complications.text: An advance that finds a soft target speeds up, and a field hospital is the softest target there is. If the enemy reads the clearing for what it is, a hospital evacuating rather than a position holding, it may push hard to reach the wounded before they are gone. It might want prisoners, or the ground, or just an easy prize. The advance's pace in the briefing is hours old.
complications.mechanicalEffect: On a die roll during the operation, the advance speeds toward the clearing, shortening the time before it arrives. The covering force must then either speed the evacuation, risking the worst cases that cannot be rushed, or hold the advance harder forward, risking the screen and the clearing. The enemy's quicker pace closes on a litter-slow evacuation that cannot match it.

decisionPoints.name: Covering the Evacuation
decisionPoints.context: The advance closes and the slow evacuation needs every minute. You have three options. Screen far forward to keep the enemy off the clearing entirely. Hold a tight close defense and get patients out fast. Or weight the screen toward the evacuation track to protect the convoy on its slow trip. Each choice trades how long the clearing stays safe against how surely the wounded reach the far end of the track.

options.title: Screen Far Forward
advantages: Hold a screen well forward of the clearing to keep the advance off it entirely, buying the evacuation its full slow time at the station
A forward screen keeps the fighting away from the wounded, letting the teardown and loading go at the safe pace the worst cases need
disadvantages: A far-forward screen is stretched in close country and can be bypassed or broken, exposing the clearing if it fails
Holding forward commits the force away from the evacuation track, leaving the convoy's slow trip lightly covered
options.consequence: You keep the clearing safe and the loading unhurried, but the screen is stretched. If it holds, the evacuation finishes at its own careful pace. If it breaks, the advance is suddenly at the clearing with the wounded still loading.

costs.resource: the force committed forward, leaving the evacuation track lightly covered
costs.risk: A stretched forward screen broken or bypassed puts the advance at the clearing mid-loading

options.title: Tight Defense, Speed the Patients
advantages: Hold a tight close defense of the clearing and push the patient loading as fast as the casualties can safely bear, to clear the station quickly
A concentrated defense is hard to break, and a faster-cleared clearing shortens the whole exposure of the evacuation
disadvantages: Speeding the loading risks the worst cases that cannot be rushed, trading those casualties for speed
A tight defense lets the advance close to the clearing's edge, putting the fighting near the wounded while they load
options.consequence: You clear the station fastest, but it costs the worst cases and a fight close to the wounded. Most of the patients get out quickly, but the casualties who cannot be hurried, and the calm the loading needs, are the price of the speed.

costs.resource: the worst cases risked by a loading pushed faster than is safe
costs.risk: Rushing the casualties who cannot be rushed loses the ones that cannot bear the pace

options.title: Weight the Track
advantages: Weight the screen toward the evacuation track to protect the ambulance convoy on its long, slow trip out through the close country
A covered track keeps the strung-out convoy safe down the one slow road, where the wounded are most fragile and most exposed
disadvantages: Weighting the track thins the clearing's own defense, letting the advance press the station harder while the loading continues
Covering a long, slow convoy stretches the force down the track, leaving little mass to hold the clearing if the advance reaches it
options.consequence: You protect the convoy on the road, but it costs the clearing's defense. The wounded already loaded get out safe down the track, but the station and the patients still loading are held by a thinner line as the advance closes.

costs.resource: the clearing's defense thinned to cover the long convoy track
costs.risk: A thin clearing defense lets the advance press the station while patients still load

entries.event: The covering force deploys around the clearing. The hospital begins teardown, and the first ambulances load the most movable wounded.
The advance's lead elements push toward the clearing through the close country. The screen makes first contact forward.
The evacuation is in full flow, with the convoy moving out the single track at the litter's pace as the worst cases are loaded last and slowest.
The advance presses the clearing's approaches. The last patients load while the screen holds the ground the evacuation still needs.
The advance reaches the clearing: the last litter is loaded and away, or the wounded still at the station are within the enemy's reach.

reactionTimeline.hardDeadline: The last patient must be loaded and the convoy clear of the clearing before the advance reaches the station at roughly T+3:30. After that, the clearing is overrun, and any wounded not yet loaded are left to an enemy that may or may not treat them decently. The covering force bought time, but came up a minute short of the litter-slow evacuation it was there to cover. The casualties that calm, careful hands could not move fast enough are the price.

opforSketch.composition: A {TARGET_FACTION} advance force, combined arms. The lead is a medium 'Mech force (40-65 tons, Regular to Veteran) pushing through the close country toward the clearing, supported by mechanized elements and combat vehicles on the few covered approaches (the vehicle portion of the enemy force). It advances to take the ground and may speed up on a soft target. The hospital, its wounded, and the ambulance convoy are non-combatants and the protected objective; the covering force is the player's screen.
opforSketch.behavior: The advance pushes to take the clearing and the ground beyond, probing the few covered approaches. If it reads the clearing as a hospital evacuating rather than a held position, it may speed up to reach the wounded before they are gone, for the ground, the prisoners, or the soft prize. It exploits a stretched or thin screen and presses the evacuation track if it can reach it. It does not necessarily fight to the last, but it presses hard while the clearing and the slow convoy are within reach.

forks.name: OPERATION ALL LITTERS OUT
forks.trigger: The hospital and its wounded were evacuated and the convoy cleared before the advance reached the clearing.
forks.consequence: The wounded are out alive and the hospital is saved to treat the front's next casualties, and {TARGET_FACTION} takes an empty clearing. The next operation sets the field hospital back up behind the new line. {EMPLOYER}'s name as the force that got the wounded out follows it to the troops it covers next.

forks.name: OPERATION LEFT BEHIND
forks.trigger: The clearing was overrun before the evacuation was complete, or the convoy was caught on the track, and wounded were left to the advance.
forks.consequence: Casualties are lost to the advance and the covering force is pinned at a contested clearing. The next operation is a fighting withdrawal of the screen and whatever convoy survives off the track ahead of the enemy. The wounded the careful hands could not move in time are left behind, and the hospital's future capacity is lost with them.

storyElementSeed: Orderlies carry a litter across a clearing to a waiting ambulance at a careful walk that will not jar the wounded man on it. A 'Mech holds the treeline beyond at the same unhurried pace, matching its patience to theirs, buying the slow careful loading the one thing it needs: time.

is-davion.objectives.primary: Cover the hospital while it tears down and gets the wounded out, and hold the clearing until the last litter is loaded, not a minute longer than the evacuation needs and not a minute short. The patients move at a litter's pace and you cannot rush them. Buy them exactly that time and screen the ambulances out the track, because every one you get out alive is the whole job.

is-steiner.objectives.primary: Screen the field hospital's evacuation and hold the clearing until the last patient is away, then cover the convoy out the track. The wounded are the asset, and the surgical gear is the next casualties' chance. Get them out at the pace the casualties can bear, and measure the job in litters loaded, not ground held.

EVAC_TRACK_KM.unit: km of single track out through close country

inspiration: A force must protect a grounded ship that took damage and cannot move until its repairs finish, holding a perimeter around an immobile, irreplaceable asset through a fixed repair clock against an enemy bent on destroying it where it sits, where the asset's own helplessness is the whole problem and the win is the moment it can finally move.
skeleton: a garrison must hold a perimeter around a grounded damaged DropShip immobilized by a fixed repair clock until it can lift, where the ship cannot move or fully defend itself and the enemy comes to destroy it on the ground, so the crux is keeping the immobile asset alive through its repair window rather than holding territory
title: OPERATION DEAD WEIGHT
situation: {EMPLOYER}'s DropShip is down and cannot fly, and {TARGET_FACTION} is coming to make sure it never does. Damage forced it down on the {DISTRICT} flats of {WORLD}. It sits grounded, its drives crippled and unable to lift, while its crew works against the clock to repair enough to get it off the ground. Until those repairs are done it is dead weight: an immobile, irreplaceable hull whose weapons cover only a fraction of the ground around it, unable to do the one thing a ship is for, which is leave. {TARGET_FACTION} knows it is down and knows it is worth destroying, and it has sent a force across the flats to kill the ship where it sits before it can be made to fly. {EMPLOYER} sends your force to hold the perimeter around it. {NPC:intel-source}, the ship's engineer, gives the one number that matters: how long the repairs will take. It is a fixed clock the crew cannot rush past a certain point, and the hull has to survive everything the enemy throws at it until that clock runs out. The report on the approaching force is {INTEL_AGE_DAYS} hours old, and a force hunting a downed ship presses hard. This is not a hold for ground, and not a fight you can win by maneuver. The thing you are defending cannot move, cannot run, and cannot be shifted to better terrain. It is fixed where it fell, and the perimeter is whatever you can hold around it. Your job is to buy the repair clock its time. Hold the perimeter around the immobile ship through the full repair window, against an enemy whose only goal is to reach the hull and destroy it, until the drives come alive and the dead weight becomes a ship again. The open flats are the main terrain problem. The ship is down on level desert ground with little natural cover. Long fields of fire help you see the enemy coming, but there is no terrain to hold beyond the ship itself. The perimeter is a ring on open ground with the helpless hull at its center. Recommended force: {FORCE_SIZE} combined arms. Use the vehicle element to range the open flats and 'Mechs to anchor the perimeter around the hull. You win by getting the ship into the air. This fight is measured by one clock, and lost the instant the dead weight is cracked open where it lies.

objectives.primary: Hold the perimeter around the grounded DropShip through its repair window, keeping the enemy off the immobile hull until the drives are restored and the ship can lift. The enemy's only goal is to destroy it on the ground.
objectives.secondary: Protect the repair work itself from disruption. Fire and pressure on the hull slow the crew, and a repair clock dragged out by a harassed work party means a longer hold against a stronger enemy.
objectives.bonus: Hold the perimeter without the ship taking more damage. A hull that lifts whole flies clear and fights again. One cracked but salvaged limps off needing the months of repair the hold was meant to spare.

complications.name: The Asset Cannot Move
complications.text: The ship is fixed where it fell. It cannot run, cannot move to better terrain, and cannot maneuver away from a threat. It can only sit and be defended, or be destroyed. Its weapons cover a fraction of the ground around it, and the rest is yours to hold. The whole problem is the asset's helplessness: a thing that cannot move, defended on the open ground it happened to come down on.
complications.mechanicalEffect: The DropShip is immobile and cannot be moved, so the perimeter must be held around its fixed location whatever the terrain. The ship's own weapons cover only limited arcs, leaving most of the perimeter to the garrison. You cannot withdraw the asset to better ground. The defense is anchored to where the hull lies until the repair clock completes.

complications.name: The Repair Clock
complications.text: The repairs need a fixed amount of time that the crew cannot rush past a certain point, and that time is the whole length of the hold. The drives come alive when the work is done and not before. You cannot end the fight early by any feat of arms. You can only outlast the enemy until the clock runs out and the ship can lift. The repair window is the mission's real length, set by the engineer, not by the battle.
complications.mechanicalEffect: The repair finishes on a fixed clock, and the ship can lift only when it runs out. The garrison must hold the perimeter for the full repair time. There is no early victory. The operation ends when the clock completes and the ship lifts (success), or when the hull is destroyed before then (failure). Holding ground past the clock is pointless, and ending the fight before it is impossible.

complications.name: Pressure Slows the Work
complications.text: Fire and pressure on the hull slow the crew. A work party under attack works worse, and an enemy that gets close enough to harass the work can drag the repair out even without destroying the ship. The closer the enemy presses, the longer the repairs take. A hold that lets the enemy near the hull lengthens the very clock it is trying to outlast.
complications.mechanicalEffect: Enemy fire or units within range of the hull slow the repair clock, because they disrupt the work party. Keep the enemy at a distance and the clock stays on schedule. Let it close and the repair drags out, lengthening the hold you have to survive. Perimeter discipline directly sets how long the mission lasts: a leaky perimeter makes its own job longer.

complications.name: The Hunters Press Hard
complications.text: A force hunting a downed ship presses hard, because a grounded hull is a prize that escapes the moment its drives light. The enemy drives to reach the hull before the repairs finish, accepting losses to crack it on the ground while it cannot run. The force's strength and pace in the briefing are hours old, and a hunter racing a repair clock pushes faster as the window closes.
complications.mechanicalEffect: On a die roll during the defense, the enemy presses harder or commits more strength to reach the hull before the repair clock completes. The garrison must then either hold a heavier push or accept the enemy closer to the hull, which slows the clock. The closer the clock comes to completion, the harder the enemy drives to crack the ship before it can lift.

decisionPoints.name: Holding the Ring
decisionPoints.context: The ship lies helpless and the hunters come across the flats. You have three options. Hold a wide perimeter to keep the enemy far from the hull and the work on schedule. Pull tight to the ship and defend it in concentrated strength. Or hold a mobile defense on the open flats, meeting the enemy forward and never letting it pin you down. Each choice trades how far you keep the enemy from the hull against how surely you can hold the ground at all.

options.title: Hold Wide
advantages: Hold a wide perimeter to keep the enemy far from the hull, keep the work on schedule, and keep the ship out of harassing range
Distance protects the repair clock: an enemy held far out cannot slow the work or threaten the hull directly
disadvantages: A wide perimeter on open flats is thin everywhere and hard to hold against a concentrated push from any direction
Stretched around a large ring, the garrison has little mass to stop a determined drive at the hull if the line is pierced
options.consequence: You keep the enemy far out and the clock clean, but the line is thin. If the wide perimeter holds, the repairs finish on time. If it is pierced, the enemy is driving at a helpless hull with the garrison stretched too thin to plug the gap.

costs.resource: the garrison stretched thin around a wide perimeter on open ground
costs.risk: A pierced wide perimeter puts the enemy driving at the hull with no mass to stop it

options.title: Tight to the Hull
advantages: Pull the perimeter tight to the ship, concentrating the garrison and the hull's own weapons in a short, strong ring
A tight ring is hard to break and easy to reinforce, defending the hull at maximum strength where it matters most
disadvantages: A close perimeter lets the enemy approach to harassing range, slowing the repair clock and lengthening the hold
The fight is at the hull, with fire falling near the ship and the work party and little margin for error
options.consequence: You defend the hull at maximum strength, but the clock slows. The ring is hard to crack, but the enemy near the ship drags out the repairs, and the fight stays close to the helpless hull throughout.

costs.resource: the enemy allowed near the hull, dragging out the repair clock
costs.risk: A close fight near the hull slows the repairs and risks the ship to stray fire

options.title: Hold Mobile on the Flats
advantages: Meet the enemy forward on the open flats with a mobile defense, never letting it pin you down or settle into a push at the hull
Mobility on the long fields of fire lets the garrison mass against each threat in turn and keep the enemy off-balance and far from the ship
disadvantages: A mobile defense away from the hull risks being drawn off, leaving the ship briefly open if the enemy slips past
Maneuvering on open ground against a hard-driving enemy can scatter the garrison, and a force chasing threats may not be home when one reaches the hull
options.consequence: You keep the enemy off-balance and far from the hull, but the perimeter is never set. If the mobile defense controls the flats, the repairs finish untroubled. If it is drawn off, the hull is briefly open to whatever slips past the screen.

costs.resource: the perimeter never fixed, with the garrison maneuvering on open ground
costs.risk: A mobile defense drawn off leaves the helpless hull open to whatever slips past

entries.event: The garrison forms the perimeter around the grounded ship. The crew starts the repair clock, and the enemy is sighted approaching across the flats.
The enemy's lead elements reach the perimeter's outer range and begin probing for a way to the hull.
The main attack commits, driving to reach the ship before the repairs finish. The garrison holds the ring as the clock runs.
The enemy presses hardest as the repair clock nears completion. The fight for the hull reaches its crisis.
The repairs complete and the drives light, and the ship lifts clear. Or the enemy reaches the hull before the clock runs out.

reactionTimeline.hardDeadline: Hold the perimeter and keep the enemy off the hull until the repair clock completes and the ship lifts. The crisis falls around T+3:30, later if pressure on the hull slowed the work. After that, one of two things happens. Either the drives light and the dead weight becomes a ship again, flying clear, or the enemy cracks the immobile hull where it lies and an irreplaceable DropShip is lost on the ground it could not leave.

opforSketch.composition: A {TARGET_FACTION} force hunting the downed ship, combined arms. The attack is led by a medium-to-heavy 'Mech force (50-80 tons, Regular to Veteran) driving across the flats to reach the hull, supported by mechanized elements and fast combat vehicles on the open ground (the vehicle portion of the enemy force). It comes to destroy the ship on the ground before it can lift, accepting cost to crack the hull while it cannot run. It presses harder as the repair clock nears completion and breaks off only if reduced past roughly a third of its strength with the ship still intact.
opforSketch.behavior: The hunters drive to reach and destroy the immobile hull, probing the perimeter for the shortest path to the ship. They race the repair clock, pressing harder as the window closes, and they try to get within range to harass the work party even where they cannot break through, because slowing the repairs lengthens their chance. They exploit a thin or drawn-off perimeter to lunge at the hull, content to crack the ship on the ground rather than fight the garrison for its own sake, and they push hardest in the final minutes before the drives can light.

forks.name: OPERATION DRIVES LIT
forks.trigger: The repairs completed and the ship lifted clear before the enemy could destroy it on the ground.
forks.consequence: The DropShip is off {WORLD} and flying again, the dead weight a ship once more, and {TARGET_FACTION} takes the empty flats where it lay. The next operation recovers both the garrison and the flown hull. The irreplaceable ship the hold saved carries the unit's fortunes off-world intact.

forks.name: OPERATION CRACKED ON THE GROUND
forks.trigger: The enemy reached the hull and destroyed or crippled the ship before the repairs finished.
forks.consequence: The DropShip is lost or wrecked beyond hope of a quick repair, and the garrison is stranded on the flats with no hull to lift it. The next operation is a fighting withdrawal overland off the open ground ahead of the enemy. The ship is dead where it fell, and the unit that depended on it is now afoot in contested country far from any other lift.

storyElementSeed: An engineer works fast inside an opened drive housing on a grounded hull while a 'Mech holds the open flat a few hundred meters out. Dust rises on the horizon where the hunters come, and the whole defense waits on one clock that no amount of shooting can make run any faster.

is-davion.objectives.primary: Hold the ring around the downed ship until the crew gets the drives lit and it can lift. That clock is the whole fight. The hull cannot move, cannot run, and cannot help much beyond its own gun arcs. Keep the enemy off it, and keep them far enough out that the repairs do not drag, and win the moment it flies.

is-steiner.objectives.primary: Protect the grounded DropShip through its repair window and keep the enemy off the immobile hull until it can lift. The ship is both irreplaceable and helpless. Hold the perimeter for exactly as long as the repairs need, keep the work unharassed so the clock holds, and measure success by drives lit and a hull flown clear, not ground held.

REPAIR_CLOCK_HR.unit: hours of repair before the ship can lift

PERIMETER_RADIUS_KM.unit: km of perimeter radius on the open flats

inspiration: A coastal gun battery commands the approaches an invader must use, so the enemy throws a ground assault at the battery to silence it and open the way in, and the defenders must keep the guns firing on the approaches even as the assault closes on the emplacements, because a battery silenced even briefly lets the landing through.
skeleton: a garrison must keep a ground-to-orbit defense battery firing on the enemy's only descent corridor while a ground assault closes to silence it, where the battery is both the objective and the weapon and any interval it goes quiet lets a drop-wave land, so the crux is keeping the guns firing into orbit while they are stormed from the ground
title: OPERATION HEAVY SKY
situation: {EMPLOYER} holds the gun that keeps {TARGET_FACTION} out of the sky over {WORLD}, and {TARGET_FACTION} is coming overland to take the sky back. On a height above {DISTRICT} stands a recovered ground-to-orbit defense battery, a heavy emplacement of restored Star League guns that can reach into low orbit and savage a DropShip on descent. As long as it fires, the enemy cannot land its assault waves. The terrain and the battery's firing arcs leave only one descent corridor open, and the battery makes that corridor too dangerous to come down through. {EMPLOYER} took the battery and means to keep it firing. {TARGET_FACTION} cannot land in the teeth of it, so it has done the only thing it can: sent a ground force overland to storm the battery and silence it, opening the corridor for the waves waiting above. {NPC:intel-source}, who coordinates the battery's fire, lays out the hard part. The guns must keep firing on the descent corridor even as the assault closes on the emplacements. The battery is both the prize and the weapon. Any moment it goes quiet, with crews driven to cover or the guns turned from the sky to the ground threat, lets a drop-wave come down through the gap. The report on the ground assault is {INTEL_AGE_DAYS} hours old, and a force opening a landing corridor presses without counting the cost. This is a hold with a cruel twist: the thing you are defending is also the thing fighting, and it must keep firing upward while it is attacked from below. The garrison holds the emplacements and the approaches while the crews keep the guns trained on the sky. Never let the fire on the corridor lapse, even as the enemy reaches the wire, because a battery that turns its guns down to save itself opens the very sky it exists to close. The gun height is the main terrain problem. It is a commanding emplacement reached by only two or three approaches up the heights, with the guns and crews fixed at the battery and their fire committed upward. The slopes around it are the ground the garrison must hold so the crews can keep firing into orbit. Recommended force: {FORCE_SIZE} combined arms. Use the vehicle element for the approaches and 'Mechs to anchor the emplacements. You win by keeping the sky closed. You lose the instant the guns go quiet and the waves come down through the gap they leave.

objectives.primary: Keep the ground-to-orbit battery firing on the enemy's descent corridor all through {TARGET_FACTION}'s ground assault. Keep the guns trained on the sky and the corridor closed, and never let the fire lapse long enough for a drop-wave to land.
objectives.secondary: Defend the battery's crews and gun-laying gear from the assault. A wrecked emplacement or a driven-off crew opens the corridor as surely as guns turned to the ground. The fire continues only while the crews can work.
objectives.bonus: Hold the emplacements without the battery taking damage that cuts its reach. A battery that comes through the assault at full power keeps the sky closed afterward. One that holds but loses guns leaves a thinner corridor the enemy can still exploit.

complications.name: The Guns Must Stay on the Sky
complications.text: The battery is both the prize and the weapon, and its weapon points up. Any moment the guns go quiet, with crews to cover or fire shifted from the sky to the ground assault, lets a drop-wave land through the gap. You cannot turn the battery's heavy guns on the force storming it without opening the corridor those guns are closing. The weapon defending the sky cannot defend itself.
complications.mechanicalEffect: The battery must keep firing on the descent corridor throughout. The guns cannot be turned on the ground assault without opening the corridor, and any lapse in orbital fire lets an enemy drop-wave land, a major setback. The battery's heavy weapons do not help the ground defense, so the garrison must hold the emplacements with its own force while the crews keep firing upward.

complications.name: The Crews Are the Fire
complications.text: The guns fire only while the crews work them. A wrecked emplacement, a crew driven to cover, or damaged gun-laying gear silences the battery as surely as turning the guns to the ground. The assault does not need to take the battery to open the sky. It needs only to make the crews stop firing, long enough, by any means.
complications.mechanicalEffect: The battery's fire depends on its crews and gear working. Fire or pressure that drives the crews to cover, or that damages the laying gear, silences the guns. The enemy can open the corridor by forcing the crews off the guns, not only by capturing the battery. The garrison must keep the assault far enough from the emplacements that the crews can keep working under fire.

complications.name: The Stormed Heights
complications.text: The battery sits on a commanding height reached by a few approaches, with the guns and crews fixed at the emplacements and their fire committed upward. The garrison holds the slopes and approaches so the crews can keep firing into orbit. But the height has little depth: a breached approach is at the guns at once, and the emplacements are the front line of any close fight.
complications.mechanicalEffect: A few approaches up the heights reach the battery, and the emplacements have little depth or fallback. The garrison defends the approaches and slopes to keep the assault off the guns. A breach reaches the emplacements quickly, and a fight at the guns themselves both endangers the crews and risks the battery. There is no room to trade space for time near the emplacements.

complications.name: The Assault Spends Itself for the Sky
complications.text: A force opening a landing corridor for the waves above presses without counting the cost, because every minute the battery fires is a wave that cannot land. The assault drives to silence the guns at any price, and the waves waiting in orbit add to its urgency. The ground force's strength and pace in the briefing are hours old, and an assault racing the sky pushes harder as it nears the emplacements.
complications.mechanicalEffect: On a die roll during the defense, the ground assault presses harder or commits more strength to silence the battery, taking heavy losses to open the corridor for the waiting waves. The garrison must then either hold a heavier push or risk the assault reaching the crews. The pressure climbs as the assault nears the guns: the closer it gets to silencing the battery, the more the waves above drive it on.

decisionPoints.name: Keeping the Guns Up
decisionPoints.context: The assault storms the heights and the battery must keep firing on the sky. You have three options. Hold a wide forward defense to keep the enemy far from the crews. Pull tight around the emplacements to defend the guns directly. Or hold a mobile defense on the slopes, meeting the assault forward and never letting it settle in at the guns. Each choice trades how far you keep the assault from the crews against how surely you hold the heights at all.

options.title: Wide Forward Defense
advantages: Hold a wide line forward on the slopes to keep the assault far from the crews and leave the guns firing on the sky untroubled
Distance keeps the crews working and the gear safe: an assault held far down the heights cannot pressure the emplacements
disadvantages: A wide forward line on the heights is thin and can be pierced, exposing the emplacements if it breaks
Holding forward commits the garrison away from the guns, leaving little to stop a thrust that reaches the crews
options.consequence: You keep the crews safest and the fire steadiest, but the line is thin. If the forward defense holds, the guns never lapse. If it breaks, the assault is at the emplacements with the garrison stretched too far down the slopes to save them.

costs.resource: the garrison committed forward, leaving the emplacements thinly backed
costs.risk: A pierced forward line puts the assault at the crews with little to stop it

options.title: Tight Around the Guns
advantages: Pull the defense tight around the emplacements, concentrating the garrison exactly where the crews and guns must be protected
A close ring is hard to break and keeps the garrison's mass exactly where a silenced battery would be lost
disadvantages: A tight defense lets the assault climb close to the emplacements, with fire falling near the crews and the gear
Giving up the slopes hands the assault covered ground right up to the guns, from which to press the crews off them
options.consequence: You defend the guns at maximum strength, but the fight is close to the crews. The emplacements are hard to take, but the assault near the guns pressures the crews, and a single breach is instantly among them.

costs.resource: the slopes given up and the fight drawn close to the crews
costs.risk: A breach of the tight ring is among the crews and guns at once

options.title: Mobile on the Slopes
advantages: Meet the assault forward with a mobile defense on the slopes, never letting it settle into a push at the emplacements
Mobility lets the garrison mass against each thrust in turn and keep the assault off-balance and away from the crews
disadvantages: A mobile defense can be drawn off, leaving the emplacements open if the assault slips past the maneuver
Maneuvering on the heights against a hard-driving assault risks scattering the garrison, leaving it away from the guns when a thrust reaches them
options.consequence: You keep the assault off-balance and far from the guns, but the defense is never set. If the mobile defense controls the slopes, the fire never lapses. If it is drawn off, the crews are briefly open to whatever reaches the emplacements.

costs.resource: the defense never fixed, with the garrison maneuvering on the heights
costs.risk: A mobile defense drawn off leaves the crews open to a thrust that slips past the screen

entries.event: The battery fires on the descent corridor, closing the sky. The ground assault begins its climb up the heights, and the garrison mans the approaches.
The assault pushes up the approaches. The garrison holds the slopes as the guns keep firing on the corridor above.
The main assault commits against the emplacements, driving to silence the guns. The crews keep firing under mounting pressure.
The assault reaches the emplacements' approaches. The fight is at the guns, and the crews fire on the sky with the enemy at the wire.
The assault makes its peak effort to silence the battery: the crisis of whether the guns keep firing through the final storm.

reactionTimeline.hardDeadline: Keep the battery firing on the descent corridor throughout the ground assault until it is broken, with the crisis falling around T+3:30. After that, one of two things happens. Either the assault is thrown off the heights and the sky stays closed, or the guns go quiet, with the crews driven off, the emplacements taken, or the fire turned to the ground. A battery silent even briefly opens the corridor for the waves above to come down, and a single landed wave is a loss no matter what ground the garrison still holds.

opforSketch.composition: A {TARGET_FACTION} ground assault to open a landing corridor, combined arms. The assault is led by a heavy 'Mech force (heavy and assault, 60-90 tons, Regular to Veteran) storming the heights to silence the battery, supported by mechanized elements and combat vehicles on the approaches (the vehicle portion of the enemy force). Above it wait drop-waves that will land the moment the guns go quiet. The assault drives to silence the battery at any cost and presses harder as it nears the emplacements, breaking off only if reduced past roughly a third of its strength with the guns still firing.
opforSketch.behavior: The assault storms the heights to silence the battery, pressing the approaches to reach the crews and guns. Its goal is the guns going quiet, by capture or by driving the crews off; it does not need to hold the height, only to open the sky. It accepts heavy cost because every minute of fire is a wave grounded above, and it presses hardest at the emplacements to force a lapse in the orbital fire. A wave lands the moment the guns fall silent, so the assault races to make them stop rather than to win the ground fight for its own sake.

forks.name: OPERATION SKY STILL HEAVY
forks.trigger: The battery was held firing throughout the assault and the sky was kept closed. No wave landed.
forks.consequence: The descent corridor stays shut and {TARGET_FACTION}'s waves remain stranded above, denied the landing the assault was meant to open. The next operation presses an enemy that spent a ground assault and still cannot come down. The closed sky over the district holds the whole invasion off as long as the guns keep firing.

forks.name: OPERATION GAP IN THE SKY
forks.trigger: The guns went quiet, with the crews driven off, the battery taken, or the fire turned to the ground, and a drop-wave landed.
forks.consequence: The corridor opened for long enough and a wave is down, with the sky no longer closed. The next operation is a fighting withdrawal off the heights for the survivors, against a beachhead now landing in the district. The battery is silenced, the invasion is through the gap it left, and the ground fight is lost to a single lapse in the fire.

storyElementSeed: A gun crew works a heavy emplacement trained on the sky, firing on a descent corridor they cannot see the end of, while the ground assault grinds up the slope toward them. A 'Mech holds the approach a stone's throw below, and every shot fired upward is a wave that does not come down.

merc.objectives.primary: Keep the big guns firing on the sky while they climb up to shut them. The contract is to keep the corridor closed. If the crews turn the guns down to fight off the assault, or are driven to cover for even a minute, a DropShip wave lands through the gap. Hold the slopes with your own machines and keep the battery shooting up, not down.

is-steiner.objectives.primary: Keep the orbital battery firing on the descent corridor throughout the ground assault, holding the sky closed the whole time. The battery is both the asset and the weapon, and its fire points up. Defend the emplacements with your force so the crews keep firing into orbit, and never let the guns lapse, because a single landed wave means the invasion is through and the loss is complete.

BATTERY_APPROACHES.unit: approaches up the heights to the emplacements

ASSAULT_REACH_HR.unit: hours for the assault to reach the emplacements

inspiration: A column withdrawing under pursuit is burdened with heavy recovered materiel it is forbidden to abandon, so the prizes set a crawling pace and the rearguard must fight off a faster enemy at the speed of the slowest load, where dropping the cargo would free the column but forfeit the whole reason for the withdrawal.
skeleton: a rearguard must fight a recovery convoy hauling irreplaceable salvaged 'Mechs out of contested ground under pursuit at the crawling pace the heavy loads set, where the salvage cannot be abandoned and slows the column to the speed of its transporters, so the crux is a fighting withdrawal paced by dead-weight cargo against a faster enemy
title: OPERATION HEAVY HAUL
situation: {EMPLOYER} has a fortune in salvage and a pursuit on its heels, and it cannot have both the salvage and the speed. A battle on the {DISTRICT} marches of {WORLD} left the ground littered with the wrecks of recovered-tech machines. {EMPLOYER}'s recovery teams have rigged the best of them onto heavy transporters: a convoy of salvaged 'Mechs, lostech hulls worth more than the operation that won them, being hauled back to friendly ground. But {TARGET_FACTION} wants them too, or wants them denied, and a pursuit force is closing on the convoy as it crawls for the line. {EMPLOYER} sends your force as the rearguard. {NPC:intel-source}, the recovery chief, lays out the unwelcome math. The salvaged hulls are dead weight on slow transporters. The convoy moves at the pace of its heaviest load and no faster. And the pursuit is much faster than the column. The report on the pursuit is {INTEL_AGE_DAYS} hours old, and a force chasing salvage presses hard. Here is the bind, and it is the whole mission. The convoy could move fast if it dropped the loads: abandon the salvaged 'Mechs and the column outruns the pursuit easily. But the salvage is the entire reason for the withdrawal. A convoy that arrives empty has saved nothing and lost everything it fought the battle to win. So the rearguard must fight off a faster enemy at the speed of the slowest transporter, buying the crawling column its road to the line without shedding the dead weight that is the whole point. The urge to drop a load and speed up grows with every contact, and giving in to it throws away the prize the contract is paid for. The open marches are the main terrain problem. They are fast going for the pursuit's light, quick elements across the flats and broken scrub. The convoy is bound to the few tracks that can bear its heavy transporters, exposed on open ground where a faster enemy can range ahead, cut the route, and pick at the strung-out column from any side. Recommended force: {FORCE_SIZE} combined arms. Use the vehicle element to screen the flanks and contest the pursuit's speed, and 'Mechs to anchor the rearguard. You win by delivering the salvage whole. You lose the moment the prizes that were the point are dropped or taken on the open marches.

objectives.primary: Fight the recovery convoy and its salvaged 'Mechs out of the contested marches to friendly ground at the pace the heavy loads set. Hold off the faster pursuit without abandoning the salvage that is the reason for the withdrawal.
objectives.secondary: Keep the convoy intact and together. A column strung out and cut on the open marches loses its severed transporters, and a faster enemy will work to split the slow loads from each other and from the rearguard.
objectives.bonus: Deliver every salvaged hull, even the slowest and most awkward loads. A withdrawal that brings out the whole haul loses no prize. A rearguard forced to shed a load to survive throws away the very salvage it was protecting.

complications.name: The Salvage Cannot Be Dropped
complications.text: The convoy could outrun the pursuit easily if it abandoned the loads, but that throws away the whole reason for the withdrawal. The salvaged 'Mechs are the point. A column that arrives empty has saved nothing. The rearguard must fight a faster enemy at the crawling pace of the dead weight, and the urge to drop a load and speed up is the urge to throw away everything the battle won.
complications.mechanicalEffect: The convoy moves at a fixed slow pace set by the heaviest transporter, and it cannot speed up without abandoning loads. Dropping a salvaged 'Mech speeds the column but loses that prize, a setback to the objective. Success requires delivering the salvage, so the rearguard must protect the slow column at its own pace rather than outrun the pursuit. The easy speed is a defeat.

complications.name: The Faster Enemy
complications.text: The pursuit is much faster than the convoy. It can range ahead, cut the route, and strike the strung-out column from any side, choosing where and when to hit a column that cannot choose its own pace. The rearguard cannot win this by speed. It must hold a faster enemy off a slower column by fighting, screening, and contesting the ground the pursuit wants to use to get ahead.
complications.mechanicalEffect: The pursuit force is faster than the convoy and can outmaneuver it, ranging ahead to cut the route or striking the flanks at will. The rearguard cannot outrun it, so it must contest the pursuit's mobility: screen the flanks, block the moves that would cut ahead, and fight to keep the faster enemy from pinning down or splitting the slow column.

complications.name: The Strung-Out Column
complications.text: The heavy transporters are bound to the few tracks that can bear them and string out along the route, each slow load a separate target on the open marches. A faster enemy works to split the loads from each other and from the rearguard. A convoy cut in two on open ground loses its severed transporters to a pursuit that can isolate and overwhelm them one at a time.
complications.mechanicalEffect: The convoy is strung out along the route, its transporters bound to the tracks that can bear them, and the pursuit seeks to cut the column and isolate loads. The rearguard must keep the convoy together and the route open. A cut that separates transporters strands them, and the faster enemy can gang up on an isolated load while the rearguard is committed elsewhere.

complications.name: The Pursuit Presses for the Prize
complications.text: A force chasing recovered-tech salvage presses hard, because the prize is worth the cost and a slow column is a chance that will not come again. The pursuit drives to reach the loads before the convoy makes the line, ranging ahead to cut it off. The pursuit's strength and pace in the briefing are hours old, and an enemy that scents the salvage pushes faster as the convoy nears safety.
complications.mechanicalEffect: On a die roll during the withdrawal, the pursuit presses harder or sends a fast element ahead to cut the route before the convoy reaches the line. The rearguard must then either contest the cut-off, dividing its strength, or accept the pursuit closer on the column. The pressure rises as the convoy nears friendly ground: the last stretch is where the pursuit drives hardest to take the prize before it escapes.

decisionPoints.name: Fighting the Convoy Out
decisionPoints.context: The convoy crawls and the faster pursuit closes. You have three options. Mass a strong rearguard against the pursuit's main weight. Spread your screen to the flanks and the route ahead against its ranging elements. Or hold a mobile defense that fights and falls back with the column. Each choice trades which threat to the slow loads you can answer against which you must leave open.

options.title: Strong Rear Guard
advantages: Mass the rearguard against the pursuit's main weight pressing from behind, holding the heaviest threat off the column's tail
A strong rear keeps the pursuit from overrunning the slowest loads from behind, which is where the main pressure comes from
disadvantages: A rear-weighted defense leaves the flanks and the route ahead thin, open to the faster enemy ranging around to cut the column
Holding the rear hard risks pinning those units in a stand while the convoy crawls on and the pursuit's fast elements get ahead
options.consequence: You hold the tail and the slowest loads, but the flanks are thin. If the pursuit ranges ahead while the rear is committed, it cuts the route or strikes the flank, and the slow column is split on open ground.

costs.resource: the flanks and route ahead thinned to hold the pressing rear
costs.risk: The faster enemy ranges around the strong rear to cut the route or split the column off

options.title: Screen the Flanks and Route
advantages: Spread the screen to the flanks and the route ahead, contesting the faster enemy's ranging moves to cut or split the column
Keeping the route open and the column together denies the pursuit the cut-and-isolate game its speed is built for
disadvantages: A flank-and-route screen weakens the rearguard, letting the pursuit's main weight press closer on the column's tail
Covering the flanks and the route ahead spreads the force thin everywhere, leaving little mass to stop a hard push at any point
options.consequence: You keep the column together and the route open, but the rear is weak. If the pursuit drives hard from behind while the screen is spread, it crowds the slowest loads from the tail with the rearguard too thin to hold.

costs.resource: the rearguard weakened to screen the flanks and the route ahead
costs.risk: The pursuit's main weight presses the slow column's tail with the rear held thin

options.title: Mobile Fighting Withdrawal
advantages: Fight and fall back with the column in a mobile defense, meeting each threat in turn and never letting the pursuit pin the rearguard down
Mobility lets a smaller force answer the faster enemy's ranging by massing against each thrust and keeping pace with the loads
disadvantages: A mobile defense paced to a crawling column is pulled in every direction at once by a faster enemy striking from many sides
Constant maneuver risks scattering the rearguard, and a force chasing threats may not be present when one reaches the loads
options.consequence: You stay unpinned and answer each thrust in turn, but the defense is never set. If the mobile rearguard controls the threats, the convoy crawls through safely. If it is pulled too thin, a load is taken while it is fighting elsewhere.

costs.resource: the rearguard pulled in every direction by a faster enemy
costs.risk: A mobile defense stretched too thin loses a load while fighting elsewhere

entries.event: The convoy crawls for the line at the pace of its heaviest load. The rearguard forms around it, and the pursuit closes from behind.
The pursuit's fast elements make first contact, probing the column's tail and ranging toward the flanks.
The pursuit presses the column and sends elements wide to cut the route ahead. The rearguard fights at the convoy's slow pace.
The pursuit drives hardest as the convoy nears the line, racing to cut it off and take the loads before they reach safety.
The convoy reaches the friendly line and the salvage is delivered. Or the pursuit catches and splits the slow column short of it.

reactionTimeline.hardDeadline: The convoy and its salvage must reach friendly ground before the faster pursuit catches and splits the slow column at roughly T+3:30. After that, the strung-out loads are run down on the open marches, cut off and taken or destroyed by an enemy the column could never outpace. A rearguard that fought its way to the line but left loads on the marches has lost the salvage that was the whole reason for the haul.

opforSketch.composition: A {TARGET_FACTION} pursuit force chasing the salvage, combined arms. It is built for speed: fast light and medium 'Mechs (25-55 tons, Regular to Veteran) and quick combat vehicles (the vehicle portion of the enemy force, a large share for the pace), faster than the convoy by a wide margin, ranging ahead and striking the flanks. It drives to take or deny the salvaged 'Mechs before they reach the line. The convoy and its loads are the prize; the rearguard is the player's force. The pursuit breaks off if reduced past roughly a third of its strength with the convoy still moving.
opforSketch.behavior: The pursuit uses its speed to range ahead and cut the route, strike the strung-out flanks, and split the slow column rather than trading blows with the rearguard head-on. It tries to isolate transporters and overwhelm them one at a time, pressing hardest as the convoy nears the line. It wants the salvage taken or denied and will work the column's slowness against it relentlessly, content to pick off loads if it cannot take the whole haul.

forks.name: OPERATION HAUL DELIVERED
forks.trigger: The convoy reached friendly ground with its salvage, with the pursuit held off the slow column.
forks.consequence: The salvaged 'Mechs are delivered whole and {EMPLOYER} gains a fortune in recovered-tech hulls, denied to {TARGET_FACTION}. The next operation refits the recovered machines into the unit's strength. The haul the rearguard fought out at a crawl pays for the campaign that won it.

forks.name: OPERATION RUN DOWN
forks.trigger: The pursuit caught and split the column, and loads were taken or destroyed on the marches before reaching the line.
forks.consequence: The salvage is lost or scattered and the rearguard is pinned on the open marches by a faster enemy. The next operation is a fighting extraction of the rearguard itself off the marches, abandoning the haul to get the survivors out. The prizes that were the whole point are taken or wrecked, and the withdrawal is a loss in spite of the fight.

storyElementSeed: A salvaged hull rides a crawling transporter across open scrub, dead and chained to its bed. A rearguard 'Mech paces the slow column with one eye on a dust plume gaining from behind, knowing it could outrun that plume in a minute if it would only leave behind the thing it is there to save.

is-davion.objectives.primary: Fight the salvage convoy back to the line at the pace of its slowest hauler, and hold off a pursuit that is faster than you are. You could outrun them by dumping the loads, and then you would have saved nothing. The salvaged 'Mechs are the whole job. Protect the crawl, keep the column together, and bring the haul in whole.

is-steiner.objectives.primary: Escort the recovery convoy out of the marches at the loads' pace and keep the faster pursuit off the strung-out column. The salvaged hulls are both the asset and the reason for the withdrawal. Dropping a load buys speed but loses the prize, so hold the slow column together and deliver every hull, because delivering the haul is the only outcome that pays.

ROUTE_TO_LINE_KM.unit: km of open marches to the friendly line

inspiration: A relief attack must be timed to strike at the same hour a besieged garrison breaks out from inside, so the two blows fall together on the encircling line, where a relief that arrives early is destroyed alone and one that arrives late finds the garrison already overrun, so the whole problem is meeting the breakout on the minute rather than merely breaking through.
skeleton: a relief force must synchronize its break-in to the exact hour a besieged garrison sorties outward so the two blows hit the encircling ring together, where arriving early is destroyed alone and arriving late finds the garrison gone, so the crux is meeting the breakout on the minute against a clock the relief only half-controls rather than the breaching itself
title: OPERATION TWO HAMMERS
situation: A {EMPLOYER} garrison is encircled and about to break out, and your relief has to hit the ring at the very same moment or the whole thing fails twice over. In the {DISTRICT} highlands of {WORLD}, a {EMPLOYER} garrison has been surrounded by a {TARGET_FACTION} force and cannot hold much longer. It will not wait to be overrun. It means to break out, sortieing through the encircling ring at an appointed hour to fight its way clear. Your relief comes from outside to meet it, and the two blows must fall together: the relief breaking in and the garrison breaking out at the same moment, catching the ring between two hammers and shattering it. {NPC:intel-source}, in contact with the trapped garrison, has the appointed hour and the timing that rules it. Arrive early and the relief hits the ring alone, before the garrison sorties. A single force hitting an intact ring by itself gets chewed up while the garrison, not yet committed, can only watch. Arrive late and the garrison has already sortied and been overrun, thrown against a ring the relief was not there to split, destroyed in a breakout that met nothing. The report on the garrison's state is {INTEL_AGE_DAYS} hours old, and a failing garrison does not fully control its own clock. The whole mission is the timing. Do not just break through the ring. Meet the breakout on the minute, hitting the ring exactly as the garrison hits it from inside, so the two blows combine. And you only half-control the clock. You can time your own advance, but the garrison's hour can slip if the besiegers press it. You must read the breakout's real timing and match it across ground you do not fully command. The highland approach is the main terrain problem. It is ridges and valleys the relief must cross to reach the ring, and they slow the advance unevenly. Hitting a precise hour means managing that approach against the clock, neither racing ahead to arrive early nor lagging to arrive late. Recommended force: {FORCE_SIZE} combined arms. Use the vehicle element for pace on the approach and 'Mechs to strike the ring. You win when the two blows fall together. You lose with a relief that arrives alone, either early to be chewed up or late to find nothing left to save.
