objectives.primary: Synchronize the relief's break-in to the garrison's breakout. Strike the encircling ring at the appointed hour as the garrison sorties outward, so the two blows fall together and shatter the line between them, then link up with the breakout force.
objectives.secondary: Read and match the garrison's timing if its hour slips. A breakout pressed early or delayed by the besiegers must still be met on the minute. A relief that adapts to the real hour links up. One that holds to the briefed hour strikes alone.
objectives.bonus: Shatter the encircling force in the double blow rather than just breaking through. A ring caught and broken between two hammers, not merely pierced, frees the garrison cleanly and wrecks the besieger as a force.

complications.name: Two Hammers or None
complications.text: The relief and the breakout must fall together. Arrive early and the relief hits an intact ring alone, chewed up while the garrison, not yet committed, can only watch. Arrive late and the garrison has already sortied against a ring the relief was not there to split, overrun in a breakout that met nothing. Only the two blows combined shatter the line. Either one alone is destroyed. The mission is the timing, not the breaching.
complications.mechanicalEffect: Success requires the relief to strike the ring within a tight window around the garrison's breakout. Strike too early and you engage the full encircling force alone, because the garrison has not yet sortied, a heavy disadvantage. Strike too late and the garrison has already been overrun, with no breakout force left to link up with. Only a synchronized strike combines the two forces against the ring, so the timing is the decisive mechanic.

complications.name: The Clock Is Half the Relief's
complications.text: The relief can time its own advance, but it does not own the garrison's hour. A failing garrison does not fully control its own clock. The besiegers can press it, forcing the breakout early or delaying it. The relief must read the breakout's real timing and match it across ground it does not fully command, syncing to a clock that can shift out from under the plan.
complications.mechanicalEffect: On a die roll during the approach, the garrison's breakout hour slips, pressed early or delayed by the besiegers. The relief must catch the change and adjust its advance to match the real hour, not the briefed one. A relief that holds to the original timing when the breakout has shifted arrives out of sync and strikes alone. Reading and matching the slip is required to combine the blows.

complications.name: The Pacing Approach
complications.text: The highland approach to the ring is ridges and valleys that slow the advance unevenly. Hitting a precise hour means managing the approach against the clock: neither racing ahead to arrive early and alone, nor lagging to arrive late and find nothing. The terrain makes a steady, timed advance hard, and the relief must shape its pace to the ground and the clock together.
complications.mechanicalEffect: The approach terrain slows the advance unevenly, so the relief must manage its movement to reach the ring at the synchronized moment, not as fast as possible. Racing the approach risks arriving early and alone. A slow or interrupted advance risks arriving late. The relief controls its arrival by pacing against the terrain and the clock, which is a different problem from simply advancing quickly.

complications.name: The Ring Faces Both Ways
complications.text: The encircling force can turn to face the relief breaking in while still holding the garrison breaking out, because a ring built to contain can also defend its outer face. The relief strikes a line that may be ready for it. The double blow works only if the garrison's sortie pins the inner face while the relief hits the outer, because neither one alone can break a ring that can face both ways.
complications.mechanicalEffect: The encircling force can defend both its inner face, against the breakout, and its outer face, against the relief, but is hardest pressed when both are struck at once. A synchronized double blow splits the ring's attention and shatters it. A single blow lets the ring face that one threat with most of its strength. The relief's timing decides whether the besieger fights on one face or two.

decisionPoints.name: Meeting the Hour
decisionPoints.context: The breakout is set and the relief must arrive on the minute. You have three options. Pace the approach to hit the briefed hour exactly. Hold short of the ring and strike only once you confirm the garrison is sortieing. Or push to arrive a touch early and pin the ring's outer face to set up the breakout. Each choice trades how surely the blows fall together against how exposed the relief is if the timing slips.

options.title: Pace to the Briefed Hour
advantages: Manage the approach to strike the ring at exactly the appointed hour, trusting the garrison's plan and committing on the minute
A clean timed arrival hits the ring as the breakout commits, with the two hammers falling together as planned
disadvantages: If the garrison's hour has slipped and the relief holds to the briefed time, it arrives out of sync and strikes alone
Committing to a fixed hour leaves no margin to read a changed breakout: the relief is locked to a clock that may have moved
options.consequence: You hit the planned hour cleanly, but you are rigid. If the breakout holds to schedule, the blows combine and shatter the ring. If the garrison's clock slipped, the relief strikes an intact line alone while the breakout falls elsewhere.

costs.resource: the relief committed to the briefed hour with no margin for a slip
costs.risk: A slipped breakout leaves the relief striking the intact ring alone off the old clock

options.title: Hold and Confirm the Sortie
advantages: Hold short of the ring until the garrison's sortie is confirmed underway, then strike, so the relief commits only when the breakout is actually happening
Confirming the real hour before committing avoids striking alone, matching the relief to the breakout's true timing
disadvantages: Holding short risks arriving late: the lag between confirming the sortie and reaching the ring may let the garrison be overrun before the relief lands
A relief waiting to confirm gives up the initiative and may have to cross the last ground under fire against a ring already alerted
options.consequence: You avoid striking alone, but you risk arriving late. If the confirm-and-strike is quick, the blows still combine. If the lag is too long, the garrison is overrun in its sortie before the relief can reach the ring it was meant to split.

costs.resource: the initiative given up to confirm the sortie before committing
costs.risk: The lag from confirmation to contact arrives late, after the garrison is overrun

options.title: Arrive Early, Pin the Outer Face
advantages: Push to arrive a touch early and pin the ring's outer face, fixing part of the encircling force to ease the garrison's breakout
An early strike on the outer face can pull the ring's attention outward, opening the inner face for the sortie to break through
disadvantages: Arriving early means engaging the intact ring before the garrison commits, with the relief taking the full weight alone until the sortie lands
If the garrison's breakout is delayed, an early relief is left fighting the whole encircling force by itself for too long
options.consequence: You set up the breakout by pinning the ring early, but you fight alone first. If the garrison sorties soon after, the early pressure pays off in a clean double blow. If the breakout lags, the relief is ground down on the outer face before the second hammer falls.

costs.resource: the relief engaging the intact ring alone before the sortie commits
costs.risk: A delayed breakout leaves the early relief fighting the whole ring by itself

entries.event: The relief begins its approach across the highlands toward the encircling ring. The garrison signals its breakout hour from inside.
The relief paces the approach against the clock. The garrison readies its sortie, and the besiegers press the trapped force.
The relief nears the ring as the appointed hour approaches. Any slip in the garrison's timing must be read and matched now.
The appointed hour: the relief strikes the ring's outer face as the garrison sorties from inside, the two blows meant to fall together.
The double blow lands or fails to combine: the ring shattered between two hammers and the link-up made, or one force striking alone.

reactionTimeline.hardDeadline: Strike the ring in sync with the garrison's breakout at the appointed hour, around T+2:15, shifting only if the garrison's clock shifts. After that the window is gone. A relief that arrived early has been fighting the intact ring alone and may be spent before the sortie lands. One that arrives late finds the garrison already overrun in a breakout that met nothing. The ring is unbroken, the two hammers have fallen apart, and the garrison is lost for want of a blow that came at the wrong minute.

opforSketch.composition: A {TARGET_FACTION} encircling force, combined arms. The ring is a medium-to-heavy 'Mech force (50-80 tons, Regular to Veteran) holding the encirclement, supported by mechanized elements and combat vehicles (the vehicle portion of the enemy force), able to face both the trapped garrison inside and the relief breaking in. It contains the garrison and presses it toward collapse while holding its outer face against relief. The trapped garrison is {EMPLOYER}'s own, about to sortie; the relief is the player's force. The ring breaks if struck hard on both faces at once and reduced past roughly a third of its strength.
opforSketch.behavior: The encircling force holds the ring, pressing the trapped garrison to force its collapse or a premature breakout while guarding its outer face against the relief. It can shift strength between faces and is hardest pressed when both are struck together. Against a relief that arrives alone, it concentrates on that threat and holds it off while the garrison stays contained; against a synchronized double blow, it is divided and shattered. It tries to force the garrison's hand early, hoping to overrun the sortie before the relief can combine with it.

forks.name: OPERATION RING SHATTERED
forks.trigger: The relief struck in sync with the breakout: the two blows combined, the ring broke, and the link-up was made.
forks.consequence: The encircling line is shattered between the two hammers and the garrison is free, with the besieger wrecked as a force. The next operation presses the broken ring with the reunited relief and garrison. The highland sector is reopened by a relief that arrived on the minute and met the breakout it was meant to.

forks.name: OPERATION HAMMERS APART
forks.trigger: The blows did not combine: the relief struck early and alone, or arrived late to find the garrison overrun.
forks.consequence: The ring held and one force was destroyed striking it alone: the relief chewed up before the sortie, or the garrison lost in a breakout that met nothing. The next operation is a fighting withdrawal of the surviving relief off the highlands ahead of an intact besieger. The garrison is gone or still trapped, and the double blow that would have freed it fell apart on one missed minute.

storyElementSeed: A relief commander watches both a chronometer and a ridgeline, pacing the advance to neither outrun nor lag the hour, listening for the garrison's signal that the sortie has begun. The difference between victory and a force destroyed alone is measured in minutes against a clock only half theirs to keep.

merc.objectives.primary: Hit the ring at the exact moment the garrison breaks out from inside, not before, not after. Show up early and you fight the whole encirclement alone while they watch. Show up late and they are already overrun and you broke through to nothing. Pace the approach, read their clock, and land your hammer when theirs lands. Together it works. Apart it is a funeral.

is-steiner.objectives.primary: Synchronize the break-in to the garrison's breakout and strike the ring at the appointed hour as they sortie outward. The two blows together shatter the encirclement. Either one alone is destroyed. The clock is only half yours: read the breakout's real timing, match it across the approach, and bring both hammers down on the same minute, because the timing is the whole battle, not the breach.
